1	# How MORSE teaches, and why
2	
3	MORSE does not invent a way to learn Morse code. It puts a few well-known methods into a pocket
4	device. This page says what each method is, where it comes from, and what MORSE does with it, so
5	you can judge the choices or change them. Where a claim comes from secondary sources, it says so.
6	
7	## Learn each character as a sound (Koch)
8	
9	**The method.** The German psychologist Ludwig Koch reported in 1936 that Morse is best learnt as
10	acoustic shapes, at a speed fast enough that you cannot count the dots and dashes, and that visual
11	charts should not be used. His learners started with two characters at full speed and added one
12	more each time they copied the ones they had at about 90 %. The commonly quoted result is a class
13	copying 12 words per minute in under 14 hours; that figure comes from summaries, not the original
14	text. ([summary of Koch's 1936 report](https://longislandcwclub.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY-KOCH-1936.pdf),
15	[Hackaday on the method](https://hackaday.com/2020/02/21/learning-morse-code-the-ludwig-koch-way))
16	
17	**Why it matters.** People who learn from a chart of dots and dashes, or at slow character speeds,
18	tend to hear a letter, count its elements and look it up. That works at 5 WPM and stalls around
19	10-15 WPM, and the habit is hard to break. CW Academy calls the alternative *instant character
20	recognition*: the whole sound of a character, recognised at once.
21	([CW Academy beginner curriculum](https://cwops.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Beginner-curriculum.htm),
22	[LCWO ICR guidelines](https://cwops.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/LCWO-ICR-Guidelines.pdf))
23	
24	**In MORSE.**
25	
26	- New letters come in Koch order as [LCWO](https://lcwo.net/) uses it (K M U R E S N A P T L W I . J Z
27	  = F O Y , V G 5 / Q 9 2 H 3 8 B ? 4 7 C 1 D 6 0 X), five at a time. The next five open once every
28	  open letter is recognised well (box 2) and sent right once (box 1): a stricter, card-by-card form
29	  of Koch's "90 %, then one more".
30	- Characters are played at 20 WPM by default (the START preset).
31	- **LEARN BY: SOUND** is the default: no dots and dashes on the screen while you learn to recognise
32	  a letter. Muted, the key lights flash its rhythm instead of drawing it.
33	- A peek is allowed where it does no harm: `SEQ` shows a new letter's code, or an answer's, and it
34	  hides again on the next card. Cards that test recognition cannot be peeked at.
35	- Sending is another skill. Seeing your own marks is useful feedback there, so KEY's CODE and
36	  TIMING views, RHYTHM, and a keyed answer's SHOULD / YOU bars are shown whatever LEARN BY says.
37	
38	## Fast characters, stretched gaps (Farnsworth)
39	
40	**The method.** Farnsworth timing keeps each character at a high speed but lengthens the gaps
41	between characters and words, so the overall speed is slow while each letter still sounds like
42	itself. It is written as two speeds, the character speed and the overall (effective) speed. The
43	ARRL wrote its own timing standard for it, since no definitive one existed; W1AW's practice files
44	currently use 15 WPM characters below 18 WPM.
45	([ARRL timing standard, by Jon Bloom KE3Z](https://uoxyc.github.io/morse/kodbok/fs_fansworth_x9004008.pdf),
46	[ARRL code practice files](https://www.arrl.org/code-practice-files))
47	
48	Koch himself did not stretch gaps; modern trainers such as LCWO combine Koch's order with
49	Farnsworth spacing, and so does MORSE.
50	
51	**In MORSE.** `K1` is the character speed, `K2` the effective speed. The presets go from START
52	(characters at 20, overall 8) through BUILDING (20/13) and QSO (22/18) to FAST (25/25). Speeds use
53	PARIS, 50 units: a dit is 1200 / WPM ms. These presets are our reading of the methods above, not
54	values from any one course. Some guidance (LCWO's ICR guidelines) suggests 25-30 WPM characters to
55	stop counting entirely; turn `K1` up if 20 lets you count.
56	
57	## Your hand is slower than your ear
58	
59	Koch and Farnsworth are about hearing. Sending is a motor skill, and a beginner's hand cannot key
60	20 WPM evenly. So MORSE keeps two speeds: hearing (`K1`, `K2`) and sending (`K4`, default 10 WPM).
61	
62	A keyed answer in PRACTICE is judged by **its own rhythm**, not a speed: a dah about three dits, a
63	gap inside a letter about one. Its shortest dah must be at least 1.5 times its longest dit, at
64	whatever speed you key. Letters of one kind of element (E T I M S O H 5 0) have nothing inside them
65	to compare, so they are judged against your hand's speed, carried from card to card. Each keyed
66	answer gets a grade for how close it is to the textbook 1:3:1, and a near miss counts as *almost*.
67	`JUDGING: STRICT` judges at the send speed instead. RHYTHM drills even presses on their own.
68	
69	## Spaced repetition by rounds (Leitner)
70	
71	**The method.** Sebastian Leitner proposed in 1972 (*So lernt man lernen*) a box system for flash
72	cards: a card answered right moves to the next box, a card missed goes back to the first, and lower
73	boxes come round more often. It is a simple form of spaced repetition.
74	([Leitner system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leitner_system))
75	
76	**In MORSE.**
77	
78	- Two cards per letter, *recognise it* (hear it, pick it from four; later key what you hear) and
79	  *send it* (see the letter, key its code), each in a box 0-5. Box n comes back every 2^n rounds.
80	- Rounds, not days: the FM-1 has no clock that keeps running when it is off.
81	- A round asks new and due cards first; the weak ones among them (box 0-1, new letters too) come
82	  back once more later in the round, the way a deck repeats a new card on its first day; only then
83	  are free places filled with letters you know.
84	- A missed card is asked again at the end of the round; right the second time, it does not move up.
85	- The chart colours each letter by its boxes. You can mark letters known, open groups, step every
86	  box back when you are rusty, or take a placement test; each change waits for your `PLAY`.
87	
88	## What MORSE leaves to others
89	
90	Words, call signs, contest exchanges, long copy and talking to people are trained better elsewhere.
91	[Vail](https://vailmorse.com/) and its [training site](https://training.vailmorse.com/) do all of
92	them, and take the FM-1 as a MIDI key. MORSE is for the daily few minutes: the characters, their
93	sound, and an even hand.
94	
95	## Sources
96	
97	- Koch: [summary of the 1936 report](https://longislandcwclub.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY-KOCH-1936.pdf),
98	  [Hackaday](https://hackaday.com/2020/02/21/learning-morse-code-the-ludwig-koch-way),
99	  [LCWO](https://lcwo.net/) (the order MORSE uses).
100	- Instant character recognition: [CW Academy beginner curriculum](https://cwops.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Beginner-curriculum.htm),
101	  [LCWO ICR guidelines](https://cwops.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/LCWO-ICR-Guidelines.pdf).
102	- Farnsworth: [ARRL timing standard](https://uoxyc.github.io/morse/kodbok/fs_fansworth_x9004008.pdf),
103	  [ARRL code practice files](https://www.arrl.org/code-practice-files).
104	- Leitner: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leitner_system).
105
```
</details></tool-use>

4	 * it up a box, wrong sends it back to 0, and box n comes back every 2^n rounds. The FM-1 has no clock that lives
5	 * through a power-off, so the schedule counts rounds, not days.
6	 *
7	 * New characters come in Koch order (LCWO's), five at a time like a kana row; the next five open once every open
8	 * character is in box 2 or higher to recognise and box 1 or higher to send. No platform, no libc (tests/morse_test.c).
9	 *
10	 * Two ways to learn (LN_VISUAL): by sound, the default, where nothing shows the dots and dashes (Koch, LCWO and CW
11	 * Academy teach each character as one sound: read off a picture, it gets counted, and copying stalls around 10-15
12	 * WPM), and by sight, where the code is drawn too. Muted, the sound way shows the lamp flashing in the code's own
13	 * rhythm instead of a drawing. */

18	#define LN_GROUP 5u                      /* opened at a time */
19	#define LN_TOP 5u                        /* the highest box */

21	#define LN_CARDS_MAX 48u                 /* cards in a round, with the ones asked again */
22	#define LN_NEVER 0xFFFFu

24	enum { LN_REC, LN_SEND, LN_NDIR };

29	    CARD_SEE_KEY,                        /* see the letter, key its code */
30	    CARD_CODE_CHOOSE,                    /* see the dots and dashes drawn, pick from four (by sight only) */
31	    CARD_LIGHT_CHOOSE,                   /* watch the lamp flash its rhythm, pick from four (muted, by sound) */
32	    CARD_NTYPES

1	# MORSE for the M-VAVE FM-1
2	
3	A pocket Morse code machine for the [M-VAVE FM-1](https://www.m-vave.com/), built on
4	[fm1-base](https://github.com/charlesvestal/fm1-base). Key on the piano keys and read what you
5	sent, drill short and long presses, learn the code by sound with flash cards, listen to endless
6	practice, type letters and CW phrases on the keys. GPL-3.0-or-later.
7	
8	**[MORSE on the web](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/fm1-morse/web/)**: see what your FM-1 reads, send it
9	text to copy, back up and restore your progress. Chrome or Edge, the FM-1 on USB, nothing to install.
10	
11	![MORSE on the FM-1](docs/screen.png)
12	
13	## What it does
14	
15	| Page | What |
16	|---|---|
17	| **PRACTICE** | Flash cards a few minutes at a time. Two cards per letter (recognise it, send it), each in a Leitner box; new letters five at a time in Koch order. The schedule counts rounds, not days (the FM-1 keeps no clock through a power-off). Learning **by sound** is the default: no dots and dashes on the screen. A keyed answer is judged by its own rhythm (a dah about three dits), at whatever speed your hand goes, with a grade, the letter as it goes over the letter as you keyed it, and what to work on; a near miss counts as *almost* and comes back. A placement test skips the letters you already know. |
18	| **LISTEN** | Plays on and on: Koch groups of the letters you have, common words, a made-up QSO, CW abbreviations with their meaning, sayings. Shown as it plays, or hidden for copying. |
19	| **KEY** | Key freely and read what you sent: as text, as each letter over the dits and dahs you keyed, or as bars to scale. Your speed, dah:dit ratio and the gaps inside letters. |
20	| **RHYTHM** | Drills of short and long presses against the target length, a judgement for each press, a hint, and a send speed that fits your hand. |
21	| **TYPE** | The keys are letters, digits and signs, or CW phrases and prosigns (`CQ`, `<SK>`, `73`...). Each key plays at once, or compose a line and send it. |
22	| **CHART** | The course as a grid, coloured by how well you know each letter. Edit it by hand (a letter's level, the groups open, all one step back, all reset); nothing is written until you confirm. |
23	
24	A straight key (any key) or iambic A/B paddles (left half dit, right half dah). A sidetone at your
25	pitch, received signals a third higher, or silence and the key lights. Hearing and sending have
26	their own speeds: Koch wants the characters heard fast, a beginner's hand is slow.
27	
28	Keying goes out and comes in over USB-MIDI as note 0 on channel 1, the
29	[Vail adapter's format](https://github.com/Vail-CW/vail-adapter/blob/master/docs/MIDI_INTEGRATION_SPEC.md),
30	so [Vail](https://vailmorse.com/) and its training tools take it. A host program
31	([`host/morse`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/M-VAVE_FM-1/tree/main/host/morse)) types what you
32	send into the computer and sends text for the FM-1 to play.
33	
34	## Controls
35	
36	| Control | Anywhere |
37	|---|---|
38	| `HOME` | the menu (again: back) |
39	| `ALGO` | the next page |
40	| `FX` | sound on / off (off: read the key lights) |
41	| `K1`, `K2` | hearing speed, and the spacing between letters (Farnsworth) |
42	| `K3` | pitch |
43	| `K4` | sending speed: the keyer, the decoder's start, the RHYTHM target |
44	| `MASTER` | volume |
45	
46	| Page | Controls |
47	|---|---|
48	| PRACTICE | `PLAY` start / again (a new letter too); `SEQ` a peek at the code of a new letter or an answer (learning by sound); `SELECT` on the start page: a round or a placement test; `E4` `F4` `G4` `A4` (lit) pick one of four, or `SELECT` + `SEL`; key the cards that ask for it; `SEL` don't know |
49	| LISTEN | `PLAY` start / stop; `SELECT` program; `SEQ` show / hide; `SEL` peek |
50	| KEY | `SEQ` view (text, code, timing); `OCT-` clear |
51	| RHYTHM | `SELECT` drill; `PLAY` start again |
52	| TYPE | `OCT-` / `OCT+` page (letters, digits and signs, phrases); `REC` delete, held: clear; `PLAY` play / stop; `SEL` live / compose; `SEQ` the code on the keys |
53	| CHART | `SELECT` move; `PLAY` hear it; `REC` edit: `OCT-` / `OCT+` or `K1` the letter's level (0 = new again), `K2` groups open, `FX` all one box back, `SEL` held 2 s all reset; `PLAY` or `REC` then asks *SAVE CHANGES?* (`PLAY` yes, `HOME` no) |
54	| SETTINGS | `SELECT` item; `OCT-` / `OCT+` change. PRESET sets the speeds together: START (hear 20/8, send 10), BUILDING, QSO, FAST. JUDGING: by rhythm (default) or strict (the decoder at the send speed, as up to 0.3) |
55	
56	Any question on the screen about your progress (save an edit, mark what a test found, load a
57	backup) is answered only by `PLAY` (yes) or `HOME` (no); every other key is ignored while it asks.
58	
59	A longer guide (Traditional Chinese):
60	[learning with MORSE](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/M-VAVE_FM-1/dev/morse-learn/),
61	[design](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/M-VAVE_FM-1/dev/morse/),
62	[cheatsheet](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/M-VAVE_FM-1/dev/morse-cheatsheet/).
63	
64	## Learning with MORSE
65	
66	1. **Settings → PRESET START** (hear 20/8, send 10). Characters are played fast and the gaps
67	   stretched, so each letter is one sound to recognise, not dots to count.
68	2. **PRACTICE, one round a day** (2-5 minutes). New letters come five at a time once the open ones
69	   are learnt: each recognised right in two rounds, and sent right once. The start page says which
70	   letters the next group waits on.
71	3. **Key the cards back in the rhythm you heard.** Speed does not matter; the ratio does: a dah
72	   about three dits, gaps inside a letter about one. The result shows SHOULD over YOU to scale.
73	4. **LISTEN** in the background (Koch groups of your letters, words, a QSO), **RHYTHM** to even out
74	   your hand, **KEY** and **TYPE** to play.
75	5. Faster: PRESET BUILDING, then QSO. For words, call signs and QSOs with people, use
76	   [Vail](https://vailmorse.com/) with the FM-1 as its key.
77	6. Already know some? **SELECT → TEST** on the PRACTICE start page, or edit the CHART. Rusty? CHART
78	   edit, `FX`: everything one box back comes round sooner.
79	
80	Why it teaches this way (Koch, Farnsworth, instant character recognition, Leitner boxes), with
81	sources: [LEARNING.md](LEARNING.md).
82	
83	## Your progress: back up and restore
84	
85	The progress lives on the FM-1 at `0xDA000` (below). Another firmware may keep it or overwrite it
86	(SLOOP 2.8.5 kept it in our test; going back to stock V15 does not), so back it up before
87	switching. MORSE 0.4 and later:
88	
89	- In Chrome or Edge: [MORSE on the web](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/fm1-morse/web/)
90	  (or `web/index.html` from this repository, opened from your disk): *Download the progress*,
91	  later *Send it to the FM-1*.
92	- Or on the command line with the host from
93	  [M-VAVE_FM-1](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/M-VAVE_FM-1): `morse backup FILE.json`,
94	  `morse restore FILE.json`.
95	
96	The file is plain JSON, every letter's two boxes (0-5) and the rounds, and can be edited. The FM-1
97	shows what it received and loads it only after `PLAY`.
98	
99	## Screens

113	| ![type code](docs/screens/type_code.png) TYPE: the code on the keys | ![phrases](docs/screens/type_phrases.png) TYPE: phrases | ![chart](docs/screens/chart.png) CHART |

116	
117	## Install
118	
119	Back up your FM-1's flash first ([M-Flasher](https://github.com/jvitkauskas/m-flasher)).
120	
121	- From a release: download `morse-X.Y.fwsc` from
122	  [Releases](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/fm1-morse/releases) and install it with M-Flasher, or
123	  over USB-MIDI with fm1-base's `tools/fm1_install.py morse-X.Y.fwsc`.
124	- The package carries fm1-base's update loader, so another firmware can be installed from MORSE
125	  the usual way.
126	- Flash chips: the build saves to and updates on both the first FM-1s' (`856014`) and the newer
127	  ones' (`B36014`). Tested on a unit with the newer chip.
128	
129	## Other firmwares' data
130	
131	MORSE does not read other firmwares' projects or samples. It keeps one record, its settings and
132	progress (about 300 bytes), at `0xDA000`-`0xDBFFF`, written when a round ends and a few seconds
133	after a setting changes. On Felucca-family firmwares (SLOOP and others) that range is inside the
134	area for samples: if you keep many samples there, back up before switching. It writes nothing else
135	outside its own firmware area, and does not touch the global settings at `0xFC000`. (An update to
136	another firmware, as with every fm1-base firmware, stages its loader at `0xE0000`.)
137	
138	## Build
139	
140	```sh
141	git clone --recursive https://github.com/daviddwlee84/fm1-morse
142	cd fm1-morse
143	python3 fm1-base/tools/build.py . --host          # the host simulator (see fm1-base's README for its tools)
144	cd build/host && ./morse_host ../../tests/basic.txt .
145	cc -Wall -Wextra -o /tmp/morse_test tests/morse_test.c && /tmp/morse_test   # the platform-free parts
146	python3 fm1-base/tools/build.py .                 # the device package (JieLi toolchain: fm1-base's README)
147	```
148	
149	| File | What |
150	|---|---|
151	| `morse.c` | code table, PARIS / Farnsworth timing, text player with prosigns, iambic keyer, adaptive decoder, judging a keyed answer by its rhythm |
152	| `learn.c` | flash cards: Leitner boxes, rounds, Koch groups, the four choices, placement, edits by hand, the backup's bytes |
153	| `content.c` | what LISTEN plays and TYPE's phrases |
154	| `tone.c` | two sine voices with 5 ms ramps, mute |
155	| `app.c` | the pages, the 1 kHz tick (key, keyer, players, MIDI), storage, drawing |
156	| `common/` | hostlink (SysEx with a host over USB / BLE) and ledfx (LED patterns) |
157	| `tests/` | `morse_test.c` for the platform-free parts, `basic.txt` for fm1-base's host simulator |
158	| `web/` | `index.html` (MORSE on the web: live text both ways, back up / restore, over Web MIDI), `words/` (the screen reader's words) |
159	| `docs/` | `screen.png` (the Hub's card), `screens/` (this page) |
160	
161	Development and the host program live in
162	[M-VAVE_FM-1](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/M-VAVE_FM-1), which has this repository as a
163	submodule.
164	
165	## License
166	
167	GPL-3.0-or-later (see `LICENSE`): you may share and change it, and what you build from it and
168	share must stay open too. Versions up to commit `57ea786` were published under MIT and stay
169	available under it.
170	
171	- `common/` (hostlink, ledfx) is MIT, shared with other firmwares in
172	  [M-VAVE_FM-1](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/M-VAVE_FM-1).
173	- fm1-base, in `fm1-base/`, is MPL-2.0 (its files stay under it).
174	- The Koch order is LCWO's; the MIDI keying follows the Vail adapter's published format.
175	- Everything you hear is generated in code: no samples.
176

85	static uint8_t ln_type(int dir, uint32_t box, uint32_t flags)
86	{
87	    if (dir == LN_SEND)
88	        return CARD_SEE_KEY;
89	    if (flags & LN_MUTED)
90	        return (flags & LN_VISUAL) ? CARD_CODE_CHOOSE : CARD_LIGHT_CHOOSE;

98	static uint32_t ln_alike(uint32_t a, uint32_t b)   /* how alike two characters' codes are */
99	{
100	    uint8_t ca = mo_code(ln_char(a)), cb = mo_code(ln_char(b));
101	    uint32_t la = mo_len(ca), lb = mo_len(cb), k, s = la == lb ? 3u : 0u;
102	    for (k = 0; k < la && k < lb; k++)
103	        s += mo_elem(ca, k) == mo_elem(cb, k);
104	    return s;
105	}

107	static void ln_options(const ln_state_t *s, ln_round_t *r, ln_card_t *c)

111	    for (i = 0; i < pool; i++)
112	        score[i] = i == c->ch ? 0u : 1u + ln_alike(c->ch, i) * 4u + ln_rand(&r->rng) % 6u;
113	    for (k = 0; k < 3u; k++) {
114	        uint32_t best = 0;
115	        for (i = 1; i < pool; i++)
116	            if (score[i] > score[best])
117	                best = i;
118	        pick[k] = best;
119	        score[best] = 0;
120	    }
121	    c->right = (uint8_t)(ln_rand(&r->rng) % 4u);

126	static void ln_add(const ln_state_t *s, ln_round_t *r, uint32_t ch, int dir, uint32_t flags)

138	    if (ln_choose(c->type))

142	void ln_build(const ln_state_t *s, ln_round_t *r, uint32_t n, uint32_t flags, uint32_t seed)
143	{

145	    uint32_t key[LN_N * LN_NDIR];
146	    uint32_t nq = 0, i, d, j, fresh = 0, first;

160	        for (i = 0; i < nq; i++) {
161	            ln_card_t *c;

164	            c->type = ln_type(LN_REC, 2u, flags);
165	            if (ln_choose(c->type))

168	        return;
169	    }
170	    if (n > LN_CARDS_MAX / 2u)
171	        n = LN_CARDS_MAX / 2u;
172	    if (n < 4u)
173	        n = 4u;
174	    for (i = 0; i < LN_N; i++)
175	        used[i][0] = used[i][1] = 0;
176	    /* new characters: each shown first, then asked */
177	    for (i = 0; i < s->open && fresh < LN_NEW_MAX; i++)
178	        if (s->last[i][LN_REC] == LN_NEVER) {
179	            ln_add(s, r, i, LN_REC, flags);
180	            r->card[r->n - 1u].type = CARD_NEW;
181	            qch[nq] = (uint8_t)i, qdir[nq] = LN_REC, key[nq] = 0, nq++;
182	            used[i][LN_REC] = 1;
183	            fresh++;
184	        }
185	    first = nq;
186	    /* the due ones, lowest box and longest waiting first; then the weakest of the rest, to fill the round */
187	    for (j = 0; j < 2u; j++)
188	        for (i = 0; i < s->open; i++)
189	            for (d = 0; d < LN_NDIR; d++) {
190	                uint32_t wait;
191	                if (used[i][d] || (j == 0u) != (ln_due(s, i, (int)d) != 0))
192	                    continue;
193	                if (j == 1u && s->last[i][d] == LN_NEVER)
194	                    continue;            /* not yet seen, not yet due: a later round */
195	                wait = s->last[i][d] == LN_NEVER ? 0u : (uint16_t)(s->round - s->last[i][d]);
196	                qch[nq] = (uint8_t)i;
197	                qdir[nq] = (uint8_t)d;
198	                key[nq] = j * 0x10000000u + s->box[i][d] * 0x100000u + (0xFFFFu - (wait > 0xFFFFu ? 0xFFFFu : wait)) * 16u
199	                          + ln_rand(&r->rng) % 16u;
200	                used[i][d] = 1;
201	                nq++;
202	            }
203	    for (i = first + 1u; i < nq; i++) {  /* by key, new ones kept first */
204	        uint32_t k = key[i];
205	        uint8_t c = qch[i], dd = qdir[i];
206	        for (j = i; j > first && key[j - 1u] > k; j--) {
207	            key[j] = key[j - 1u];
208	            qch[j] = qch[j - 1u];
209	            qdir[j] = qdir[j - 1u];
210	        }
211	        key[j] = k, qch[j] = c, qdir[j] = dd;
212	    }
213	    {
214	        /* the new and the due first; then the weak ones of them (box 0-1, the new ones too) once more later in
215	         * the round, like a deck that repeats a new card the day it comes; only then the rest, weakest first */
216	        uint32_t ndue = first, base, weak[LN_N * LN_NDIR], nw = 0, nrep, nfill;
217	        while (ndue < nq && key[ndue] < 0x10000000u)
218	            ndue++;
219	        base = ndue > n ? (n > first ? n : first) : ndue;
220	        for (i = 0; i < base; i++)
221	            if (s->box[qch[i]][qdir[i]] <= 1u)
222	                weak[nw++] = i;
223	        nrep = nw < (n > base ? n - base : 0u) ? nw : (n > base ? n - base : 0u);
224	        nfill = nq - ndue;
225	        if (nfill > n - base - nrep)
226	            nfill = n - base - nrep;
227	        for (i = 0; i < nfill; i++) {    /* the fill moves up behind the base */
228	            qch[base + i] = qch[ndue + i];
229	            qdir[base + i] = qdir[ndue + i];
230	        }
231	        {
232	            uint8_t rch[LN_N * LN_NDIR], rdir[LN_N * LN_NDIR];
233	            uint32_t m = base + nfill;
234	            for (i = 0; i < nrep; i++)
235	                rch[i] = qch[weak[i]], rdir[i] = qdir[weak[i]];
236	            for (i = m; i > 1u; i--) {   /* asked in a shuffled order */
237	                uint32_t k = ln_rand(&r->rng) % i;
238	                uint8_t c = qch[i - 1u], dd = qdir[i - 1u];
239	                qch[i - 1u] = qch[k], qdir[i - 1u] = qdir[k];
240	                qch[k] = c, qdir[k] = dd;
241	            }
242	            for (i = 0; i < m; i++)
243	                ln_add(s, r, qch[i], qdir[i], flags);
244	            for (i = nrep; i > 1u; i--) {
245	                uint32_t k = ln_rand(&r->rng) % i;
246	                uint8_t c = rch[i - 1u], dd = rdir[i - 1u];
247	                rch[i - 1u] = rch[k], rdir[i - 1u] = rdir[k];
248	                rch[k] = c, rdir[k] = dd;
249	            }
250	            for (i = 0; i < nrep; i++) { /* the second time: right does not move it a second box */
251	                ln_add(s, r, rch[i], rdir[i], flags);
252	                r->card[r->n - 1u].again = 1;
253	            }
254	        }
255	    }
256	}

258	const ln_card_t *ln_card(const ln_round_t *r) { return r->at < r->n ? &r->card[r->at] : 0; }
259	
260	int ln_answer(ln_state_t *s, ln_round_t *r, int result)
261	{
262	    ln_card_t *c;
263	    uint8_t *box;
264	    int up = 0, right = result == LN_RIGHT;
265	    if (r->at >= r->n)
266	        return 0;
267	    c = &r->card[r->at];
268	    if (r->place) {                      /* nothing changes until ln_place_apply */
269	        if (right) {
270	            r->ok++;
271	            r->known[c->ch / 32u] |= 1u << (c->ch % 32u);
272	        } else
273	            r->miss++;
274	        r->at++;
275	        return 0;
276	    }
277	    if (c->type == CARD_NEW) {
278	        r->fresh++;
279	        r->at++;
280	        return 0;
281	    }
282	    box = &s->box[c->ch][c->dir];
283	    s->answered++;
284	    if (right) {
285	        s->right++;
286	        r->ok++;
287	        if (!c->again && *box < LN_TOP) {  /* right after a miss in the same round: stays in box 0 */
288	            (*box)++;
289	            r->up++;
290	            up = 1;
291	        }
292	    } else if (result == LN_ALMOST) {    /* close: the box stays, asked once more */
293	        r->near++;
294	        if (!c->again && r->n < LN_CARDS_MAX) {
295	            ln_card_t *a = &r->card[r->n++];
296	            *a = *c;
297	            a->again = 1;
298	        }
299	    } else {
300	        r->miss++;
301	        *box = 0;
302	        if (!c->again && r->n < LN_CARDS_MAX) {   /* asked once more at the end of the round */
303	            ln_card_t *a = &r->card[r->n++];
304	            *a = *c;
305	            a->again = 1;
306	            if (ln_choose(a->type))
307	                ln_options(s, r, a);
308	        }
309	    }
310	    s->last[c->ch][c->dir] = s->round;
311	    r->at++;
312	    return up;
313	}
314	
315	int ln_finish(ln_state_t *s, const ln_round_t *r)
316	{
317	    uint32_t i, asked = r->ok + r->miss + r->near;
318	    if (!asked || r->place)
319	        return 0;
320	    s->round++;
321	    if (r->at >= r->n)                   /* a whole round: the streak; one left halfway does not change it */
322	        s->streak = r->ok * 100u >= asked * 80u ? (uint16_t)(s->streak + 1u) : 0u;
323	    if (s->open >= LN_N)
324	        return 0;
325	    for (i = 0; i < s->open; i++)
326	        if (s->box[i][LN_REC] < 2u || s->box[i][LN_SEND] < 1u)
327	            return 0;
328	    s->open = (uint8_t)(s->open + LN_GROUP > LN_N ? LN_N : s->open + LN_GROUP);
329	    return 1;
330	}
331	
332	uint32_t ln_level(const ln_state_t *s, uint32_t i)
333	{
334	    if (i >= LN_N)
335	        return 0;
336	    return (s->box[i][LN_REC] + s->box[i][LN_SEND]) / 2u;
337	}

339	/* ----------------------------------------------------------- by hand --- */
340	static void ln_seen(ln_state_t *s, uint32_t i)   /* answered now, as far as the schedule goes */
341	{
342	    s->last[i][LN_REC] = s->last[i][LN_SEND] = s->round;
343	}
344	
345	static void ln_open_raw(ln_state_t *s, uint32_t n)   /* more open: the new ones at the line the next group needs */
346	{
347	    uint32_t i;
348	    n = (n + LN_GROUP - 1u) / LN_GROUP * LN_GROUP;
349	    n = n < LN_GROUP ? LN_GROUP : n > LN_N ? LN_N : n;
350	    for (i = s->open; i < n; i++) {
351	        if (s->box[i][LN_REC] < 2u)
352	            s->box[i][LN_REC] = 2u;
353	        if (s->box[i][LN_SEND] < 1u)
354	            s->box[i][LN_SEND] = 1u;
355	        ln_seen(s, i);
356	    }
357	    if (n > s->open)
358	        s->open = (uint8_t)n;
359	}
360	
361	void ln_set_level(ln_state_t *s, uint32_t i, uint32_t lv)
362	{
363	    if (i >= LN_N)
364	        return;
365	    if (lv > LN_TOP)
366	        lv = LN_TOP;
367	    if (i >= s->open)
368	        ln_open_raw(s, i + 1u);
369	    s->box[i][LN_REC] = s->box[i][LN_SEND] = (uint8_t)lv;
370	    if (lv == 0u) {                      /* back to new: shown again, then asked */
371	        s->last[i][LN_REC] = s->last[i][LN_SEND] = LN_NEVER;
372	    } else
373	        ln_seen(s, i);
374	}
375	
376	void ln_mark_known(ln_state_t *s, uint32_t i)
377	{
378	    if (i >= LN_N)
379	        return;
380	    if (i >= s->open)
381	        ln_open_raw(s, i + 1u);
382	    if (s->box[i][LN_REC] < 3u)
383	        s->box[i][LN_REC] = 3u;
384	    if (s->box[i][LN_SEND] < 2u)
385	        s->box[i][LN_SEND] = 2u;
386	    ln_seen(s, i);
387	}
388	
389	void ln_open_to(ln_state_t *s, uint32_t n)
390	{
391	    uint32_t i;
392	    n = (n + LN_GROUP - 1u) / LN_GROUP * LN_GROUP;
393	    n = n < LN_GROUP ? LN_GROUP : n > LN_N ? LN_N : n;
394	    if (n >= s->open) {
395	        ln_open_raw(s, n);
396	        return;
397	    }
398	    for (i = n; i < s->open; i++) {
399	        s->box[i][LN_REC] = s->box[i][LN_SEND] = 0;
400	        s->last[i][LN_REC] = s->last[i][LN_SEND] = LN_NEVER;
401	    }
402	    s->open = (uint8_t)n;
403	}
404	
405	void ln_step_back(ln_state_t *s)
406	{
407	    uint32_t i, d;
408	    for (i = 0; i < LN_N; i++)
409	        for (d = 0; d < LN_NDIR; d++)
410	            if (s->box[i][d])
411	                s->box[i][d]--;
412	}
413	
414	uint32_t ln_place_count(const ln_round_t *r)
415	{
416	    uint32_t i, n = 0;
417	    for (i = 0; i < LN_N; i++)
418	        n += r->known[i / 32u] >> (i % 32u) & 1u;
419	    return n;
420	}
421	
422	uint32_t ln_place_apply(ln_state_t *s, const ln_round_t *r)
423	{
424	    uint32_t i, g, n = 0, open = s->open;
425	    if (!r->place)
426	        return 0;
427	    for (g = open; g < LN_N; g += LN_GROUP) {   /* whole groups right, in turn: opened */
428	        uint32_t end = g + LN_GROUP > LN_N ? LN_N : g + LN_GROUP, all = 1;
429	        for (i = g; i < end; i++)
430	            all &= r->known[i / 32u] >> (i % 32u) & 1u;
431	        if (!all)
432	            break;
433	        ln_open_raw(s, end);
434	    }
435	    for (i = 0; i < LN_N; i++)
436	        if (r->known[i / 32u] >> (i % 32u) & 1u) {
437	            if (i < s->open) {
438	                ln_mark_known(s, i);
439	                n++;
440	            }
441	        }
442	    return n;
443	}

445	/* ------------------------------------------------------------ a backup --- */
446	static uint8_t *ln_put(uint8_t *b, uint32_t v, uint32_t n)
447	{
448	    uint32_t k;
449	    for (k = 0; k < n; k++)
450	        *b++ = (uint8_t)(v >> (8u * k));
451	    return b;
452	}
453	
454	static uint32_t ln_get(const uint8_t **b, uint32_t n)
455	{
456	    uint32_t v = 0, k;
457	    for (k = 0; k < n; k++)
458	        v |= (uint32_t)(*(*b)++) << (8u * k);
459	    return v;
460	}
461	
462	void ln_blob(const ln_state_t *s, uint8_t *b)
463	{
464	    uint32_t i, d;
465	    b = ln_put(b, s->round, 2);
466	    b = ln_put(b, s->streak, 2);
467	    b = ln_put(b, s->open, 1);
468	    b = ln_put(b, s->answered, 4);
469	    b = ln_put(b, s->right, 4);
470	    for (i = 0; i < LN_N; i++)
471	        for (d = 0; d < LN_NDIR; d++)
472	            *b++ = s->box[i][d];
473	    for (i = 0; i < LN_N; i++)
474	        for (d = 0; d < LN_NDIR; d++)
475	            b = ln_put(b, s->last[i][d], 2);
476	}
477	
478	int ln_unblob(ln_state_t *s, const uint8_t *b)
479	{
480	    ln_state_t t;
481	    uint32_t i, d;
482	    t.round = (uint16_t)ln_get(&b, 2);
483	    t.streak = (uint16_t)ln_get(&b, 2);
484	    t.open = (uint8_t)ln_get(&b, 1);
485	    t.rsv = 0;
486	    t.answered = ln_get(&b, 4);
487	    t.right = ln_get(&b, 4);
488	    for (i = 0; i < LN_N; i++)
489	        for (d = 0; d < LN_NDIR; d++)
490	            t.box[i][d] = *b++;
491	    for (i = 0; i < LN_N; i++)
492	        for (d = 0; d < LN_NDIR; d++)
493	            t.last[i][d] = (uint16_t)ln_get(&b, 2);
494	    if (!ln_valid(&t))
495	        return 0;
496	    *s = t;
497	    return 1;
498	}

4	
5	#define TONE_RATE 44100.0f
6	#define TONE_RAMP (1.0f / (0.005f * TONE_RATE))   /* 5 ms from silent to full */
7	#define TONE_AMP 0.3f
8	
9	static struct {
10	    volatile uint8_t gate;
11	    volatile float inc;                  /* phase step per frame, of a turn */
12	    float phase, ramp;                   /* ramp 0..1, shaped into the level */
13	} tone_v[TONE_N];
14	static volatile uint8_t tone_muted;
15	
16	void tone_pitch(int v, float hz)
17	{
18	    if (v >= 0 && v < TONE_N)
19	        tone_v[v].inc = hz / TONE_RATE;
20	}
21	
22	void tone_gate(int v, int on)
23	{
24	    if (v >= 0 && v < TONE_N)
25	        tone_v[v].gate = (uint8_t)(on != 0);
26	}
27	
28	void tone_mute(int on) { tone_muted = (uint8_t)(on != 0); }
29	
30	int tone_gated(int v) { return v >= 0 && v < TONE_N && tone_v[v].gate; }
31	
32	void tone_stop(void)
33	{
34	    uint32_t v;
35	    for (v = 0; v < TONE_N; v++) {
36	        tone_v[v].gate = 0;
37	        tone_v[v].ramp = 0.0f;
38	    }
39	}
40	
41	void tone_render(int32_t *lr, uint32_t n, float gain)
42	{
43	    uint32_t v, i;
44	    for (v = 0; v < TONE_N; v++) {
45	        float inc = tone_v[v].inc, phase = tone_v[v].phase, ramp = tone_v[v].ramp;
46	        int on = tone_v[v].gate;
47	        if (!on && ramp <= 0.0f)
48	            continue;
49	        for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
50	            float lvl, s;
51	            ramp += on ? TONE_RAMP : -TONE_RAMP;
52	            ramp = ramp < 0.0f ? 0.0f : ramp > 1.0f ? 1.0f : ramp;
53	            phase += inc;
54	            if (phase >= 1.0f)
55	                phase -= 1.0f;
56	            if (tone_muted)
57	                continue;
58	            lvl = ramp * ramp * (3.0f - 2.0f * ramp);   /* smoothstep: the ramp's corners rounded */
59	            s = fm_sinf(phase * 6.2831853f) * lvl * TONE_AMP * gain;
60	            lr[2 * i] += (int32_t)s;
61	            lr[2 * i + 1] += (int32_t)s;
62	        }
63	        tone_v[v].phase = phase;
64	        tone_v[v].ramp = ramp;
65	    }
66	}

Try the new design now and help us make it even better","url":"https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2016.01251/full"},{"title":"pubmed 4989027","url":"https://ebusca.uv.mx/Record/pubmed-4989027"},{"title":"harpcolumn.com","url":"https://harpcolumn.com/?p=289056"},{"title":"Interleaved practice: the counterintuitive way to actually remember what you train","url":"https://fifths-marketing.pages.dev/blog/interleaved-practice-music/"}]

The Carter and Grahn study is real and easy to find. It's "Optimizing Music Learning: Exploring How Blocked and Interleaved Practice Schedules Affect Advanced Performance," published in Frontiers in Psychology on 18 August 2016 (vol. 7, article 1251). The authors are Christine E. Carter of Memorial University of Newfoundland and Jessica A. Grahn of Western University.

- **Design:** Ten clarinetists practiced two pairs of pieces. One concerto exposition and one technical excerpt were practiced in blocks of twelve minutes each, and a second pair was practiced in three-minute alternating segments. Ten clarinetists were given one concerto exposition and one technical excerpt to practice in a blocked schedule (twelve minutes per piece) and a second concerto exposition and technical excerpt to practice in an interleaved schedule (three minutes.
- **Findings:** Independent judges rated the recordings, and where the conditions differed, the interleaved schedule came out ahead, per the blog summary in the results. Questionnaires also indicated that the alternating approach helped with goal setting, focus, and spotting mistakes. The authors concluded that interleaving may be a more effective strategy than continuous repetition for music learning.
- **Background:** Motor-learning research has long found that interleaved practice can slow performance during training yet improve long-term retention. Earlier work by Stambaugh (2009) with beginner clarinetists also found an interleaving advantage, though other studies were less conclusive.

Links: [{"title":"Learning melodic musical intervals: To block or to interleave?","url":"https://ink.library.smu.edu.sg/soss_research/4316"},{"title":"sage.cnpereading.com","url":"https://sage.cnpereading.com/doi/10.1177/0305735620922595"},{"title":"nih.gov","url":"https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6384134"},{"title":"sciencegate.app","url":"https://www.sciencegate.app/keyword/265981"},{"title":"Modeling and optimizing forgetting and spacing effects during musical interval training","url":"https://digitalcommons.memphis.edu/facpubs/8219"},{"title":"Interleaved practice: the counterintuitive way to actually remember what you train","url":"https://fifths-marketing.pages.dev/blog/interleaved-practice-music/"},{"title":"solfege-pro.pages.dev","url":"https://solfege-pro.pages.dev/en/manual/interval/"},{"title":"pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov","url":"https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2797123"},{"title":"Unit 2: Intervals","url":"https://openbooks.library.baylor.edu/eartraining/?p=166"},{"title":"vufind-test.katalog.k.utb.cz","url":"https://vufind-test.katalog.k.utb.cz/SummonRecord/FETCH-LOGICAL-c375t-36be41554caec5dab53a3a85ec951f8bfa7b7149f1aeb1b236124e9a91b4c6683/Details"}]

The research on interleaving for interval identification is small but mostly favorable.

- **Wong, Chen & Lim (2021, *Psychology of Music*)** tested novices learning melodic ascending intervals. With reference songs and singing as aids, interleaved and blocked practice gave comparable results on a test with new examples. Without those aids, interleaving produced better interval identification. Most participants also wrongly believed blocking worked better. (Novices learned six interval types in an interleaved schedule and six in a blocked schedule within a single session. In the absence of reference songs and singing, a robust interleaving effect emerged.)
- **Pavlik et al. (2013, EDM conference)** found that performance was better for those who received an interleaving order of the practice trials when learners were taught to tell tritones from octaves.
- **Counterevidence:** A study on a nonnative speech contrast, not intervals, found blocked training was superior to interleaved training for both learning and retention. This suggests the benefit depends on how similar the items are.
- **Moderator evidence:** An app manual cites Brunmair & Richter's (2019) meta-analysis, which concerns similarity matters: a meta-analysis of interleaved learning and its moderators. I could not check that paper's findings directly.

Overall, the evidence supports interleaving for interval identification, especially when learners lack reference cues. Most of the direct evidence comes from small studies, and I found no large interval-specific trial.

Here's a summary of what the search turned up. Most results are blogs, forum threads, and commercial flashcard sites, so I'd treat the specifics as starting points rather than authoritative guidance.

**Anki decks for theory topics**
- A Memo.cards guide describes Anki as a flashcard program that uses spaced repetition, and notes that decks cover key signatures, intervals, and solfège. It also suggests key-signature images for quizzing yourself on a key's accidentals. (index 1-3, 1-7, 1-12)
- A free set from Girl in Blue Music includes ear-training decks, currently covering intervals from Do in major and minor keys. (index 16-3)
- A Gypsy Jazz forum user suggests keeping theory topics in a separate deck from repertoire material. (index 5-3, 5-4)

**Limits of Anki for music**
- A Medium post by a long-time user says Anki's algorithm fits memorization well but doesn't match how playing music works. (index 11-2)
- An Ankiweb forum thread makes a similar point and suggests shorter early review intervals might suit motor skills better than standard language-learning settings. (index 3-5, 3-7)

**Other options**
- A GitHub project (ts95/music-theory) is a React app built with Claude Code that runs spaced-repetition drills on keys, scales, and chords, including a 15-second key-signature drill. (index 6-1, 6-7)
- RemNote and Knowt offer AI-generated or prebuilt flashcards for key signatures and intervals, though these are commercial products. (index 2-7, 4-3)

2	/* Morse: see app.h. Part of fm1-base's unity build, after the platform (gfx.c, announce.c in scope).
3	 * The 1 kHz tick does what needs the millisecond: the key and the keyer, the two players, MIDI in and out, the
4	 * sidetone's gates; it leaves key-down / key-up events with their times in a ring. The main loop decodes them, runs
5	 * the pages (flash cards, listening, rhythm drills), talks to the host and draws.
6	 * Protocol with the host: PROTOCOL.md in github.com/daviddwlee84/M-VAVE_FM-1 host/morse (the numbers below match its host/morse/protocol.py). */

21	enum { T_HELLO = 0x41, T_HEARTBEAT, T_CHAR, T_PROG, T_PROG_DONE };
22	/* a progress backup on the wire: a format byte, ln_blob's bytes, a CRC-16/CCITT of both; cut into chunks of
23	 * PROG_CHUNK bytes, each frame <index> <count> and the chunk with its high bits gathered (8 bytes for each 7) */
24	#define PROG_FORMAT 1u
25	#define PROG_N (1u + LN_BLOB_N + 2u)
26	#define PROG_CHUNK 49u
27	#define PROG_FRAMES ((PROG_N + PROG_CHUNK - 1u) / PROG_CHUNK)

29	/* Vail's MIDI keying (vail-adapter docs/MIDI_INTEGRATION_SPEC.md): channel 1, note 0 a timed key-down */
30	#define MIDI_KEY_ON (0x09u | 0x90u << 8 | 0x00u << 16 | 0x7Fu << 24)
31	#define MIDI_KEY_OFF (0x08u | 0x80u << 8 | 0x00u << 16 | 0x00u << 24)
32	
33	/* the debounce keeps a key down ~8.8 ms after it opens and sees it ~1.6 ms after it closes: a straight key's marks
34	 * read ~7 ms long on the FM-1 (fm1-base bsp/boards/fm1/fm1_input.h; fm1-emu shows +3 / +10 ms); the host simulator
35	 * has no debounce */
36	#ifdef PLAT_HOST

44	#define REC_VER 1u                       /* 0.2 kept 0.1's layout: its spare bytes became look, send, prog */
45	enum { LM_SOUND, LM_VISUAL };            /* how to learn: by sound (recommended), by sight */
46	enum { KV_TEXT, KV_CODE, KV_TIMING, KV_N };   /* the KEY page's view */
47	enum { TL_ALPHA, TL_PIANO, TL_KOCH, TL_N };   /* the TYPE page's letters on the keys */
48	typedef struct {
49	    uint8_t wpm;                         /* hearing: character speed 5..40 */
50	    uint8_t eff;                         /* hearing: effective speed (Farnsworth) 5..wpm */
51	    uint8_t keyer;                       /* MO_STRAIGHT, MO_IAMBIC_A, MO_IAMBIC_B */
52	    uint8_t swap;                        /* paddles: 0 left half dit, 1 left half dah */
53	    uint8_t mute;
54	    uint8_t cards;                       /* per round 10..30 */

57	                                          * TYPE's layout (TL_*), bit 5 LISTEN hides the text, bit 6 TYPE composes

59	                                          * judges keyed answers strictly (by the send speed, as 0.3 did) */

I'm designing an open-source **music theory / ear training / scales-and-chords trainer firmware** for the M-VAVE FM-1 pocket synth (25 mini keys, small LCD, speaker, USB-MIDI, ~580 KB firmware slot, C code on a JieLi MCU, community firmware SDK "fm1-base"). Please find **similar existing projects** and **notation/representation options**, with links and licences:

A. **Similar projects**
1. FM-1 community firmwares: fetch https://thefirmwarehub.com/catalog.json and the awesome list (search "awesome-fm-1" on GitHub, and "aroum/fm1-custom-fw") — any firmware with chord modes, scale modes, ear training, music theory, practice/teaching features? Also the FM1 Developers' Wiki https://sbegueria.github.io/fm1-dev-wiki/ .
2. Hardware with built-in teaching/theory: e.g. ROLI LUMI keys (light-up learning), Casio/Yamaha light-guide keyboards, Arturia/Novation scale & chord modes (Launchkey "Scale mode", "Chord mode"), Teenage Engineering OP-1/OP-XY chord/scale features, Orba, "Chordie", Roland/Korg "chord trigger" features, Artiphon, any standalone "ear trainer" gadget. What interactions do they use that fit a 25-key, button-and-small-LCD device?
3. Apps: Functional Ear Trainer, EarMaster, Tenuto / musictheory.net, Teoria, Complete Ear Trainer, Perfect Ear, Melodics, Simply Piano, Flowkey, Yousician, Piano Marvel, Hooktheory (Hookpad, TheoryTab), Chordify, "Scales & Arpeggios" practice apps, Synthesia. Summarise each one's core loop in one line, especially the ones that use a connected MIDI keyboard for input.
4. **Open-source** ear trainers / theory trainers: e.g. "OpenEar" (Angular, MIT?), "Lenmus", "GNU Solfege", "ear-training" repos, Piano Booster, "Tonic" ... with licence. Any embedded/microcontroller (Arduino, ESP32, Teensy, Raspberry Pi Pico) ear-training or chord-trainer projects?

B. **Representation / notation**
1. Text music notations suitable for tiny embedded storage and/or authoring on a PC then compiling into C tables: **Alda** (https://alda.io — licence, does it have a parser library or MIDI export, is it practical to use as an authoring format and convert at build time?), ABC notation (abc2midi licence), MML (variants, very compact), RTTTL, LilyPond, Strudel/Tidal mini-notation, midicsv. Compare compactness, ease of hand-writing exercises, ability to express chords/polyphony and rhythm, and tooling licence.
2. **Music theory libraries** that generate scales/chords/progressions procedurally (so content can be generated rather than hard-coded): tonal.js (MIT?), music21 (BSD), mingus (GPL?), teoria.js, Python "pychord", C/C++ libs if any. Which would be good for a build-time generator, and are there tiny C implementations of chord/scale spelling (correct enharmonic spelling like F# vs Gb in each key)?
3. Any notes on correctly spelling notes in all keys with a compact algorithm (line of fifths, Tonal Pitch Class), since the device needs to display e.g. "F#" in D major and "Gb" in Db major.

Be concrete and cite URLs and licences. Mark anything unverified. Keep the report to roughly 1,200–1,800 words.

The search turned up a consistent picture: Creative Commons declared BY-SA 4.0 one-way compatible with GPLv3 on 8 October 2015, and the compatibility runs in only one direction.

- **Date and status:** CC's compatible-licenses page lists GPLv3 as a "BY-SA–Compatible License" for version 4.0 on 8 October 2015.
- **Direction:** CC's compatibility page notes that you may license your contributions to adaptations of BY-SA 4.0 materials under GPLv3, but you may not license your contributions to adaptations of GPLv3 projects under BY-SA 4.0. CC's wiki gives the reason: GPLv3 does not permit adapting a GPLv3 work and licensing the contributions under BY-SA, so the determination only allows movement one way, from BY-SA 4.0 to GPLv3.
- **Scope:** The declaration covers only GPL version 3. CC's wiki says reusers that adapt BY-SA 4.0 content and incorporate it into GPL-licensed projects are only able to use GPLv3 unless and until other GPL versions are declared compatible.
- **Intended use:** CC says the mechanism is meant for situations in which content is integrated into software code in a way that makes it difficult or impossible to distinguish the two. CC also advises that in most cases it makes sense to release adaptations under the same license as the original, so GPLv3 relicensing is not usually the default.
- **Source conditions:** CC's wiki says an adapter who cannot provide or make source available cannot take advantage of the one-way compatibility declaration and may not use GPLv3 for her contributions.

Caveat: several results are secondary (a Trisquel forum post, a martech.zone glossary, a Lemmy comment). The CC pages and the CC wiki are the authoritative sources here. I did not find the FSF's own statement in these results beyond a link to its 2015 blog post.

I found no standalone API terms of use or TheoryTab data license. The closest sources are the site Terms of Service and the Trends API docs.

- **Terms of Service (updated October 2025):** Third parties may not copy, scrape, bulk-download, text-and-data mine, or redistribute TheoryTab data unless Hooktheory allows it through a written data license or API terms. The terms reserve text-and-data-mining rights and warn that violations can lead to suspended access and injunctive relief. Terms of Service
- **Trends API docs:** The official API exposes the chord probability data behind the TheoryTab Search by Chords page. It has two endpoints, requires HTTPS, and uses OAuth 2 bearer tokens. The API exposes the chord probability data used in Hooktheory's TheoryTab Search by Chords page.
- **No full data access:** The docs say a full TheoryTab data dump for research is not currently available, and Hooktheory hopes to build a broader API someday. Not right now.
- **Forum posts (older):** One staff reply says the API returns analysis rather than raw song data, and that it covers only data up to 2015-03-20. Another user asked for API terms and said none could be found. These posts are dated, so treat them with caution.
- **Unofficial wrapper:** A third-party service on Parse.bot advertises song-level TheoryTab access and says that data is not part of the official API. I didn't verify its terms, and it isn't Hooktheory's own offering.
- **Aria terms:** Hooktheory's Aria beta terms are separate. They grant a license to use Aria inside Hookpad only, and not for integration into external services.

Bottom line: Hooktheory's official API covers Trends chord-probability data only. Bulk or song-level TheoryTab data needs a written license from Hooktheory, and I found no public pricing or license terms for that.

- **KARMA:** KARMA is free, open-source firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1.
- **JIANT FM:** a free, open-source alternative firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1, made for playing live and building whole songs without a computer.
- **Official firmware:** M-VAVE released firmware V15 with a few updates, including note-on velocity and a MIDI CC guide (M-VAVE has just released firmware V15 with some great additions and improvements.).

Some tools are also available: a browser-based patch librarian by Benny Sparra (github: benny-sparra/fm1-dx7-patch-importer) and a web-based FM-1 Helper for sysex preset banks.

To find an "awesome-fm-1" list specifically, a search of GitHub directly for that name would be the next step.


REMINDER: You MUST include the sources above in your response to the user using markdown hyperlinks.

This is the home page of the **FM-1 Firmware Developers' Wiki**, an unofficial community knowledge base for writing firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1 pocket synthesizer and its sibling, the SMK-37 Pro/Elite keyboard. Both use a JieLi AC791N chip. **Community firmware:** This page names no specific firmware. It mentions "dozens of firmwares" and points to the Known Projects page for their notes. **Chord modes, scale modes, ear training, music theory, teaching or practice features:** None are mentioned. 1063	static uint16_t crc16(const uint8_t *p, uint32_t n)   /* CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE */
1064	{
1065	    uint16_t c = 0xFFFFu;
1066	    uint32_t k;
1067	    while (n--) {
1068	        c ^= (uint16_t)(*p++ << 8);
1069	        for (k = 0; k < 8u; k++)
1070	            c = (uint16_t)(c & 0x8000u ? (c << 1) ^ 0x1021u : c << 1);
1071	    }
1072	    return c;
1073	}
1074	
1075	static void prog_fill(uint8_t *b)        /* PROG_N bytes: the format, the record, the CRC */
1076	{
1077	    uint16_t c;
1078	    b[0] = PROG_FORMAT;
1079	    ln_blob(&rec.ln, b + 1);
1080	    c = crc16(b, 1u + LN_BLOB_N);
1081	    b[1u + LN_BLOB_N] = (uint8_t)c;
1082	    b[2u + LN_BLOB_N] = (uint8_t)(c >> 8);
1083	}
1084	
1085	static uint32_t pack7(const uint8_t *in, uint32_t n, uint8_t *out)   /* each 7 bytes: their high bits, then them */
1086	{
1087	    uint32_t i, j, k = 0;
1088	    for (i = 0; i < n; i += 7u) {
1089	        uint32_t m = n - i < 7u ? n - i : 7u;
1090	        uint8_t hi = 0;
1091	        for (j = 0; j < m; j++)
1092	            hi |= (uint8_t)((in[i + j] >> 7) << j);
1093	        out[k++] = hi;
1094	        for (j = 0; j < m; j++)
1095	            out[k++] = in[i + j] & 0x7Fu;
1096	    }
1097	    return k;
1098	}
1099	
1100	static uint32_t unpack7(const uint8_t *in, uint32_t n, uint8_t *out, uint32_t max)
1101	{
1102	    uint32_t i = 0, j, k = 0;
1103	    while (i < n) {
1104	        uint8_t hi = in[i++];
1105	        for (j = 0; j < 7u && i < n && k < max; j++)
1106	            out[k++] = (uint8_t)(in[i++] | ((hi >> j) & 1u) << 7);
1107	    }
1108	    return k;
1109	}
1110	
1111	static void prog_pump(void)              /* the backup out, a frame each main-loop pass while the USB takes them */
1112	{
1113	    uint8_t b[PROG_N], f[2u + PROG_CHUNK + PROG_CHUNK / 7u + 1u];
1114	    uint32_t off, m, k;
1115	    if (!prog.tx_on)
1116	        return;
1117	    prog_fill(b);
1118	    off = prog.tx_i * PROG_CHUNK;
1119	    m = PROG_N - off < PROG_CHUNK ? PROG_N - off : PROG_CHUNK;
1120	    f[0] = prog.tx_i;
1121	    f[1] = (uint8_t)PROG_FRAMES;
1122	    k = 2u + pack7(b + off, m, f + 2);
1123	    if (hl_send(&link, T_PROG, f, k) == 0 && ++prog.tx_i >= PROG_FRAMES)
1124	        prog.tx_on = 0;
1125	}
1126	
1127	static void prog_in(const uint8_t *d, uint32_t len)   /* a chunk of a backup to load */
1128	{
1129	    uint32_t i, off;
1130	    uint16_t c;
1131	    if (len < 3u || d[1] != PROG_FRAMES || d[0] >= PROG_FRAMES) {
1132	        prog_done(PD_BAD);
1133	        return;
1134	    }
1135	    if (d[0] == 0u)
1136	        prog.rx_next = 0;
1137	    if (d[0] != prog.rx_next) {          /* one missed: start again */
1138	        prog.rx_next = 0;
1139	        prog_done(PD_BAD);
1140	        return;
1141	    }
1142	    off = d[0] * PROG_CHUNK;
1143	    (void)unpack7(d + 2, len - 2u, prog.buf + off, PROG_N - off < PROG_CHUNK ? PROG_N - off : PROG_CHUNK);
1144	    prog.rx_next++;
1145	    if (prog.rx_next < PROG_FRAMES)
1146	        return;
1147	    prog.rx_next = 0;
1148	    c = crc16(prog.buf, 1u + LN_BLOB_N);
1149	    if (pg.ask && pg.ask != ASK_LOAD) {  /* another question is up: answer that first */
1150	        prog_done(PD_DECLINED);
1151	        return;
1152	    }
1153	    if (pg.edit)

1157	    if (!i) {
1158	        prog_done(PD_BAD);
1159	        app_say("BACKUP REFUSED", "IT DOES NOT CHECK OUT");
1160	        return;
1161	    }
1162	    pg.ask = ASK_LOAD;

Web search results for query: "Hooktheory most common chord progressions statistics I V vi IV"

Links: [{"title":"chord progression analysis report","url":"https://salu133445.github.io/pdf/chord_progression_analysis_report.pdf"},{"title":"hooktheory.com","url":"https://hooktheory.com/blog/?p=121"},{"title":"hooktheory.com","url":"https://hooktheory.com/blog/?p=245"},{"title":"www.hooktheory.com","url":"https://www.hooktheory.com/blog/music-theory-analysis-1300-songs-for-songwriting-part2/index.html"},{"title":"www.hooktheory.com","url":"https://www.hooktheory.com/blog/i-analyzed-the-chords-of-1300-popular-songs-for-patterns-this-is-what-i-found/index.html"},{"title":"i analyzed the chords of 1300 popular songs for patterns this is what i found","url":"https://www.hooktheory.com/blog/i-analyzed-the-chords-of-1300-popular-songs-for-patterns-this-is-what-i-found/"},{"title":"flowingdata.com","url":"https://flowingdata.com/?p=25279"},{"title":"hooktheory analyzes chords of 1300 songs","url":"https://rekkerd.org/hooktheory-analyzes-chords-of-1300-songs/"},{"title":"• They Analyzed 1,300 Songs & Here’s What They Found","url":"https://www.hearandplay.com/main/they-analyzed-1300-songs-heres-what-they-found"},{"title":"Analysis of chords used in popular songs","url":"https://flowingdata.com/2012/06/20/analysis-of-chords-used-in-popular-songs/"}]

The top result is a Hooktheory blog post, and it confirms that I–V–vi–IV is the most common four-chord progression in their database. I didn't find a usage percentage for it.

- **Ranking:** A 2012 Hooktheory analysis of about 1,300 popular songs names I → V → vi → IV (C → G → Am → F in C) as the most frequent four-chord progression in the database. The most popular four-chord progression that shows up in the database is in fact the I → V → vi → IV (or C → G → am → F in the key of C). The same post notes it uses IV rather than V to return to I. This, by the way, is a great example of a progression that uses the IV instead of V to get back to I.
- **Independent dataset:** A separate analysis of over ten thousand HookTheory songs, which is a different dataset from the blog's, reached a similar conclusion. Its four-gram results put C-G-Am-F at the top, along with C-F-G-C. C-G-Am-F and C-F-G-C are indeed the two most frequently used chord progressions.
- **Common chords:** In songs transposed to C, the I, IV, and V chords appear about equally often, and the vi chord (Am) comes next. F major and G major (the IV and V respectively) are used just as often. The A minor chord is the next most popular, but after that there is a significant drop off in use.
- **Dataset size:** The original analysis covered about 1,300 songs. The database has since grown, and you can browse over 50,000 chord and melody analyses on the site.

1	# 摩斯電碼機（Morse）
2	
3	把 FM-1 變成隨身的摩斯電碼機：琴鍵當電鍵發報、即時解碼成文字、琴鍵當字母鍵盤把文字播成摩斯、用閃卡隨身練習，也能接電腦和 [Vail](https://vailmorse.com/) 跟網路上的人互傳。韌體在獨立的 repo [fm1-morse](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/fm1-morse)（GPL-3.0-or-later，以 submodule 放在本 repo 的 `firmware/morse/`），電腦端在本 repo 的 `host/morse/`（MIT）。
4	
5	**狀態（2026-11-18）：機器上是韌體 0.3（02:12 刷入）。0.1 時已在實機確認發報、解碼、TYPE、PRACTICE、和電腦連線；0.2 的 RHYTHM、KEY 三種顯示、TYPE、LISTEN、PRESET 本人試過覺得不錯，升級後學習進度也還在 `[實機]`。0.3 修了 TYPE 鍵上點劃的排版。** 操作方式見[操作速查](morse-cheatsheet.md)。
6	
7	## 有沒有人做過 { #prior-art }
8	
9	2026-11-17 查過，**沒有**找到 FM-1 上的摩斯作品，也沒有讓兩台 FM-1 互傳訊息的韌體 `[調研]`：
10	
11	- [Firmware Hub catalog](https://thefirmwarehub.com/catalog.json) 的 244 個套件裡沒有 Morse、CW、keyer（電報意義的）、trainer。
12	- [FM1 Developers' Wiki](https://sbegueria.github.io/fm1-dev-wiki/) 沒有相關頁面。
13	- GitHub 搜尋 `fm1 morse`、`m-vave morse`、`fm1-base morse` 都沒有結果（code search 只涵蓋 default branch，可能漏掉）。
14	
15	相近的作品：SPELLBOX 把琴鍵當 A–Z 鍵盤；MIDIMON（fm1-base）同時當 BLE peripheral、central 與 USB host，作者說用它來 debug 另一台 FM-1。設計時參考的是其他平台的摩斯機：[Morserino-32](https://github.com/oe1wkl/Morserino-32)（模式分類、收發用不同音高）、[LCWO](https://lcwo.net/)（Koch 順序）、Vail（MIDI 格式）。只參考做法，沒有複製程式碼。
16	
17	## 功能
18	
19	| 頁面 | 做什麼 | 版本 |
20	|---|---|---|
21	| **PRACTICE** | 開機直接進來。一回合 20 張閃卡（10–30 可調），幾分鐘做完 | 0.1 |
22	| **LISTEN** | 一直播下去：你開放的 Koch 字組、常用英文字、QSO 範例、縮寫和意思、諺語。可以顯示正在播的字，或隱藏起來當抄收練習 | 0.2 |
23	| **KEY** | 自由發報：琴鍵是電鍵，解出來的字、你的速度、dah:dit 比例、字內停頓。三種顯示：TEXT（字）、CODE（每個字下面是你實際打的點劃）、TIMING（每一下照實際長短畫成條） | 0.1；顯示方式 0.2 |
24	| **RHYTHM** | 練長短：只打 dit、只打 dah、交替、SOS、自由按。每一下和目標長度比對，給提示和建議的發報速度 | 0.2 |
25	| **TYPE** | 琴鍵是字母，`OCT-`／`OCT+` 翻三頁：字母、數字和符號、片語。鍵上可以顯示點劃；LIVE（按一個字送一個）或 COMPOSE（打好一行再送） | 0.1；翻頁、片語、COMPOSE 0.2 |
26	| **CHART** | 像五十音表的字表，依熟練度上色 | 0.1 |
27	| **SETTINGS** | 速度組合（PRESET）、聽的速度、間隔、發報速度、音高、keyer（直鍵、iambic A、iambic B）、paddle 左右、聲音、每回合張數、學習方式、TYPE 的排列 | 0.1；PRESET、發報速度 0.2 |
28	
29	電鍵有兩種：**直鍵**是任一琴鍵按下就發；**iambic paddle** 是左半邊琴鍵（F3–F4）發 dit、右半邊（F#4–G5）發 dah，兩邊同時按會交替（squeeze）。Mode B 會記住在一個 element 中途按的另一邊，放開後補發一個。
30	
31	聲音是兩個 sine voice：自己發的用設定的音高（預設 600 Hz），收到的高一個大三度，聽得出是誰在發。靜音時所有琴鍵的燈會跟著節奏亮（自己發的全亮、收到的半亮），畫面上也有一條燈號。
32	
33	## 速度：WPM 是什麼、該設多少 { #speed }
34	
35	WPM 是每分鐘幾個字，以 PARIS 這個字（50 個單位）為準：**dit 的長度 = 1200 ÷ WPM 毫秒**。摩斯沒有規定一定要多快，重要的是比例：
36	
37	| 元素 | 長度 |
38	|---|---|
39	| dit | 1 單位 |
40	| dah | 3 單位 |
41	| 字裡面的停頓 | 1 單位 |
42	| 字和字之間 | 3 單位 |
43	| 字詞之間 | 7 單位 |
44	
45	| WPM | dit | dah | 大概是 |
46	|---|---|---|---|
47	| 5 | 240 ms | 720 ms | 很慢，看得清楚每一下 |
48	| 10 | 120 ms | 360 ms | 新手手打 |
49	| 13 | 92 ms | 277 ms | 以前美國業餘無線電 General 考試的速度 |
50	| 20 | 60 ms | 180 ms | Koch 建議的字元速度 |
51	| 25 | 48 ms | 144 ms | 熟練的通聯 |
52	
53	0.2 起分成兩個速度（0.1 只有一個）：
54	
55	- **聽的速度**（K1，加上 K2 的間隔）：FM-1 播給你聽的速度。Koch 的做法是字本身用 20 WPM 左右播，聽起來是一整個聲音；字和字之間用 **Farnsworth** 拉開（例如「20/8」是字用 20 WPM，整體像 8 WPM），讓你有時間想。
56	- **發報速度**（K4）：你手打的速度，用來設定 iambic keyer 的節奏、KEY 頁解碼器的起點、RHYTHM 頁和 TIMING 檢視的目標長度。新手的手通常比耳朵慢，所以這個要另外設低一點。0.4 起 PRACTICE 的打碼卡不再用它判斷（見[判定](#judging)）。
57	
58	**推薦的組合**（SETTINGS 最上面的 PRESET，轉的時候畫面會說明）：
59	
60	| PRESET | 聽 | 發 | 適合 |
61	|---|---|---|---|
62	| START（預設） | 20/8 | 10 | 剛開始 |
63	| BUILDING | 20/13 | 13 | 認得大部分的字之後 |
64	| QSO | 22/18 | 18 | 能和人一般通聯 |
65	| FAST | 25/25 | 22 | 熟練 |
66	
67	自己調的方法：到 TYPE 頁按幾個字聽聽看，轉 K1、K2 找到「字聽得出是一整個聲音、字和字之間來得及想」的組合；發報速度到 RHYTHM 頁打幾組 dit，它會依你的 dit 平均長度建議一個 K4 值。這些組合是我依 Koch／Farnsworth 的做法和常見的考試、通聯速度整理的建議 `[調研]`，不是哪個教材的固定值。
68	
69	## 學習：閃卡和間隔複習
70	
71	體驗參考背單字和學五十音：
72	
73	- **一個字兩張卡**：「認得它」（聽到或看到，說出是哪個字）和「打得出它」（看到字母，用電鍵打出來）。
74	- **Leitner 盒**：每張卡在 0–5 號盒。答對升一盒，答錯回 0 號，盒 n 每 2ⁿ 個回合複習一次。答錯的卡會在同一回合最後再問一次，這次答對也不升盒。
75	- **一回合怎麼出題**（0.4）：先排新字和到期的卡（盒號低、等最久的優先）。其中盒號 0–1 的弱卡（包括剛介紹的新字）會在回合後半再出一次，重複那次答對不會再升盒。還有空位，才用沒到期的卡補滿，最弱的優先。0.3 每張卡一回合只出一次，空位直接用熟字補，所以新的一組開放後，一回合裡大部分還是 K U R E 這些熟字（2026-11-18 試用時的回饋 `[實機]`）。
76	- **新字一次介紹幾個**：開放一組 5 個字時，每回合最多介紹 3 個，所以會分兩回合介紹完。後一回合又出現 NEW LETTER，是同一組剩下的字，不是又開了一組。
77	- **回合數**：做完一回合，或答過題後中途離開（`HOME`、換頁），都算一回合。
78	- **用回合數，不用日期**：FM-1 沒有關機後還在走的時鐘，所以排程數的是「做了幾回合」。之後接電腦時可以讓 host 送日期，改成真正的天數，但還沒做。
79	- **新字按 Koch 順序**（LCWO 的 41 字：K M U R E S N A P T L W I . J Z = F O Y , V G 5 / Q 9 2 H 3 8 B ? 4 7 C 1 D 6 0 X），5 個一組，像五十音的一「行」。一回合最多 3 個新字，每個新字先播兩次給你聽，然後才考。開著的字全部「認得」到 2 號盒以上、「打得出」到 1 號盒以上，才開下一組。
80	- **先選擇，後回想**：「認得」的卡在 0–2 號盒是聽完從四個裡選（四個選項對應 E4 F4 G4 A4 四個亮燈的鍵，干擾選項挑碼型相近的），3 號盒以上改成聽完直接打出來。
81	- 回合結束顯示答對、答錯、升了幾盒，以及連續幾回合正確率 80% 以上（streak）。中途按 `HOME` 離開，已答的部分照樣存。
82	
83	### 打碼卡怎麼判 { #judging }
84	
85	0.3 以前，打碼卡（看字打碼、聽了照打）是用**發報速度**判斷長短：解碼器從 SEND 的 dit 起算，長過 2 個 dit 才算 dah。預設 SEND 10 WPM 時，dah 要按到 240 ms 以上。但 PRACTICE 播給你聽的是 20 WPM，dah 只有 180 ms。照著聽到的節奏打，劃就被當成點：M（−−）讀成 I、T 讀成 E。
86	
87	這個情況 2026-11-18 在實機上碰到 `[實機]`：打到 ROUND 14 還停在 K M U R E。開下一組要每個字的「打得出」至少到 1 號盒，可是這些卡一直被判錯、回到 0 號盒。
88	
89	0.4 改成**看答案自己的節奏**（SET 頁 `JUDGING: BY RHYTHM`，預設）：
90	
91	- **點和劃都有的字**（A、K、R…）：答案裡應該是劃的那幾下，最短的一個至少要是應該是點的最長那一下的 1.5 倍。只比相對長短，快慢都可以。
92	- **只有一種元素的字**（E T I M S O H 5 0）：答案裡沒有東西可以比，所以和「你的手速」比：劃至少 1.6 個 dit，點最多 2.4 個 dit。手速從前幾張卡延續下來，答對時會往你的實際長度修正。每回合第一張卡還沒有手速可參考，就用聽的速度和發報速度兩個 dit 的中間值（START 是 90 ms）。
93	- **數量要對**：K 打成 −··（D）一樣判錯。
94	- **差一點（ALMOST）**：比例在 1.2 到 1.5 倍之間（只有一種元素的字則是界線外 20% 以內），盒號不升也不歸零，回合最後再問一次。
95	- **字中間停太久**：還沒打滿就停頓時，會多等一下（至少 900 ms）才判斷，不會被切成兩個字。停頓超過 2.5 個點長，最多只算 ALMOST，並提示「run it together」。
96	- **評級**：每張打碼卡都有，0–100 分，依劃點比是否接近 3:1、字內間隔是否接近 1 個點、同種元素長度是否一致來算。GREAT ≥ 85，GOOD ≥ 65，CLOSE ≥ 40，其餘是 OFF。評級和對錯分開算。
97	- **結果頁**：SHOULD 是照你這次的點長排出的標準節奏，YOU 是你實際按的，兩列用同一個比例尺。判反的那一下標紅，停太久的間隔畫紅底線。下面一行提示要改什麼。結果頁另外顯示解碼器讀成的字（`READ AS`）。
98	
99	`JUDGING: STRICT` 是 0.3 的判法（解碼器照 SEND 的速度讀，讀出的字對了才算對），適合想練固定速度的人。
100	
101	### 先用聽的：學習方式設定 { #by-sound }
102	
103	**預設是「SOUND」**：出題只用聲音，畫面上**不畫點劃**，字表只顯示熟練度，靜音時燈號照真實節奏閃，也不畫成 ·−。
104	
105	原因：Koch 法、LCWO、CW Academy 這類教學都主張把每個字的聲音當成一個整體記，不要看點劃圖。看圖學的人聽到訊號時會先數幾點幾劃再查表，速度常卡在每分鐘 10–15 字，之後得花時間改掉。`[調研]`（這是教學界的普遍說法，我還沒找到量化研究。）同樣的理由，字元速度預設 20 WPM，用 Farnsworth 把字和字之間拉開到有效 8 WPM，而不是把每個字放慢。
106	
107	這是「學認字」的規則。「練發報」時看自己打出的長短是有用的回饋，所以 KEY 頁的 CODE／TIMING 檢視、RHYTHM 頁、TYPE 頁的「鍵上點劃」都和這個設定分開，用的時候自己打開。
108	
109	0.4 起 SOUND 模式也能偷看：新字和答案畫面按 `SEQ` 顯示點劃，換卡就藏回去。這是 2026-11-18 試用時的需求：新字只聽一兩次，怕把相近的字聽錯 `[實機]`。考「認得」的題目時不能看，不然就變成看圖選字。footer 也改成寫出 `PLAY again`（0.3 寫「any key: next」，但 `PLAY` 其實一直可以重播）。
110	
111	「SIGHT」是另一個選項：顯示點劃，閃卡在低盒號時用「看碼選字」，KEY 頁畫出正在打的碼。切過去時畫面會提示「SOUND FIRST IS FASTER LATER」。
112	
113	| | SOUND（預設） | SIGHT |
114	|---|---|---|
115	| 認得的卡，0–2 號盒 | 聽 → 四選一 | 看點劃 → 四選一 |
116	| 認得的卡，3 號盒以上 | 聽 → 打出來 | 聽 → 打出來 |
117	| 打得出的卡 | 看字母 → 打出來 | 同左 |
118	| 靜音時認得的卡 | 看燈號節奏 → 四選一 | 看點劃 → 四選一 |
119	| 畫面上的點劃 | 不顯示 | 新字、答案、KEY 頁、字表都顯示 |
120	
121	### 進度：跳過、退回、歸零 { #progress }
122	
123	**手動修改都要確認才寫入**：螢幕會問「SAVE CHANGES?」「MARK THESE KNOWN?」「LOAD THIS BACKUP?」，只有按 `PLAY` 才寫入，按 `HOME` 就放棄。問的時候其他鍵和旋鈕都沒作用，也不會把琴鍵當成電鍵。
124	
125	- **CHART 編輯**：在 CHART 按 `REC` 進入 EDIT。所有改動先存在一份副本，標題會顯示 `EDIT *`。
126	    - `OCT-`／`OCT+` 或 `K1`：游標所在字的等級（兩個方向的盒號一起改）。降到 0 就是「忘了」，那個字會重新當新字出現。在還沒開放的字上調高，會一路開放到它那一組。
127	    - `K2`：開放的組數 ±1。新開放的字直接放在解鎖門檻（認得 2 號盒、打得出 1 號盒）；關掉的字變回新字。
128	    - `FX`：全部退一盒，覺得生疏時用，每個字都會早點回來複習。
129	    - 按住 `SEL` 2 秒：全部歸零。
130	    - `PLAY` 或 `REC`：問要不要存；`HOME` 不存就離開。編輯中 `ALGO` 不能換頁。
131	- **分級測驗**：PRACTICE 開始畫面轉 `SELECT` 選 TEST，`PLAY` 開始。還沒開放的下兩組（10 個字）各考一次「聽了選」。結束時列出答對的字，問要不要標成已會（認得 3 號盒、打得出 2 號盒）。整組都答對就開放那一組。測驗不算回合，也不影響 streak。
132	- **開始畫面的提示**：`NEXT GROUP WAITS ON …` 列出還沒到門檻、擋住下一組的字。
133	
134	### 備份與還原 { #backup }
135	
136	進度存在 FM-1 的 `0xDA000`（見[存檔](#flash)）。換韌體時不一定保得住：2026-11-18 實測從 SLOOP 2.8.5 切回來時還在，刷回原廠 V15 就沒了 `[實機]`。換韌體前先備份。0.4 起有兩種方式：
137	
138	| 方式 | 怎麼做 |
139	|---|---|
140	| 網頁（Chrome、Edge） | [MORSE on the web](https://daviddwlee84.github.io/fm1-morse/web/)（fm1-morse 的 `web/index.html`，舊網址 `web/progress.html` 會轉過去）：Connect、Download the progress；還原時選檔案、Send it to the FM-1 |
141	| 指令列 | `just morse-backup FILE.json`、`just morse-restore FILE.json` |
142	
143	檔案是 JSON，列出每個字兩個方向的盒號（0–5）和最後作答的回合，可以手改。FM-1 收到後先檢查 CRC 和內容是否合理，再顯示回合數、開放幾個字、答過幾題，按 `PLAY` 才載入。協定見 [`host/morse/PROTOCOL.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/M-VAVE_FM-1/blob/main/host/morse/PROTOCOL.md) 的 Progress 一節。
144	
145	- **只走 USB**：0.4 的韌體沒有開藍牙，所以網頁和指令列都要接 USB 線。網頁找機器時不看 port 名稱，而是看哪個 port 在送 HELLO，因為 macOS 會沿用這個 USB 裝置第一次接上時的名字（這台叫 `Felucca`）`[實機]`。
146	- **藍牙之後**：0.5 開 own BLE stack 後，hostlink 本來就能走藍牙收發 SysEx。macOS 在「音訊 MIDI 設定」配對 BLE-MIDI 裝置後，會把它當成一般的 MIDI port，Chrome 的 Web MIDI 應該也看得到，網頁程式不用改。這點還沒驗證 `[調研]`。
147	- **入口**：fm1-morse README 的最上面，以及 Hub 卡片：`fmhub.json` 的 `editor` 欄位（「a web editor for its sounds or settings」`[上游]`）2026-11-18 填了這個網址。
148	- **Live**（2026-11-18 加入，不需要新韌體）：網頁顯示 FM-1 讀到的字（`T_CHAR`，在 KEY 頁發報或在 TYPE 頁打字）和按鍵燈號（note 0），也能送字給 FM-1 播（`T_TEXT`、`T_STOP`），等於網頁版的 `morse-send`，加上只顯示、不打進系統的 `morse-type`。網頁會回應 HELLO，所以 FM-1 會顯示 `PC`。送字在實機上試過 `[實機]`。
149	
150	## 練長短：RHYTHM 頁 { #rhythm }
151	
152	給還分不出長短的人。每按一下，畫面會畫出目標長度的框和你實際按的長度，顏色是綠（好）、黃（偏了）、紅（變成另一種了），並寫出「DIT 1.3（130 MS）A BIT LONG」這樣的數字：1.3 表示是目標 dit 的 1.3 倍。
153	
154	| 練習 | 目標 |
155	|---|---|
156	| DITS | 五個 dit |
157	| DAHS | 五個 dah |
158	| DIT DAH | 交替三次 |
159	| SOS | `... --- ...` |
160	| FREE | 自由按，看每一下被當成什麼 |
161	
162	判斷標準（以發報速度的 dit 為 1）：dit 在 0.5–1.5 算好、1.6–2.0 偏長、超過 2.0 就會被當成 dah；dah 在 2.2–4.0 算好、低於 1.8 會被當成 dit；1.6–2.1 是兩邊都不像的「中間地帶」。最近 16 下的平均會產生一條提示：dit 太長（附上適合你的 K4 速度）、dah 太短或太長、字內停頓太長（超過 1.8）、長短不穩（平均差 0.3 個 dit 以上）、或「GOOD RHYTHM」。
163	
164	## 收聽：LISTEN 頁 { #listen }
165	
166	一直播下去，適合放著聽。播的內容都是韌體裡現場組出來的，沒有使用任何人的教材：
167	
168	| 節目 | 內容 |
169	|---|---|
170	| KOCH GROUPS | 你已經開放的字，隨機五個一組，一行五組 |
171	| WORDS | 最常用的 100 個英文字，一行六個 |
172	| QSO | 兩個隨機呼號從 CQ、報訊號和名字、地點，到 73、`<SK>` 結束，六行一輪 |
173	| ABBREVIATIONS | 一個縮寫播兩次，畫面顯示意思（例如 QTH：my location is） |
174	| SAYINGS | 英文諺語，加上 1844 年第一封電報 WHAT HATH GOD WROUGHT |
175	
176	`SEQ` 切換「顯示」和「隱藏」。隱藏時只看得到播到第幾個字，這一行播完、下一行開始時才顯示答案，等於抄收練習；`SEL` 可以偷看。更長的教材可以從電腦用 `just morse-send -` 把文字一行一行送進來播，例如 Project Gutenberg 上公有領域的書。
177	
178	被動地一直聽能幫忙熟悉聲音，但教學上普遍認為主動抄收、回打進步比較快 `[調研]`，所以 LISTEN 是 PRACTICE 的補充。
179	
180	## 片語、prosign 和實際的用法 { #phrases }
181	
182	業餘無線電用摩斯通聯（QSO）時，有一套固定的縮寫和 **prosign**。prosign 是幾個字母連在一起當成一個符號打，中間沒有字間停頓，寫成 `<SK>` 這樣。TYPE 頁第三頁的 27 個片語鍵：
183	
184	| 片語 | 意思 | 片語 | 意思 |
185	|---|---|---|---|
186	| CQ | 呼叫任何電台 | GM / GE | 早安 / 晚安 |
187	| DE | 這裡是 | FB | fine business：很好 |
188	| K | 換你說 | R | 收到 |
189	| `<KN>` | 換你說，只限你 | QRZ? | 誰在呼叫我？ |
190	| `<AR>` | 訊息結束 | QSL | 我確認收到 |
191	| `<SK>` | 通聯結束 | `<BK>` | 換手（back to you） |
192	| `<BT>` | 停頓、換段 | HW? | 收得清楚嗎？ |
193	| 73 | 祝好、再見 | PSE | 請 |
194	| TU | 謝謝 | AGN | 再一次 |
195	| RST | 訊號報告 | QRS | 請發慢一點 |
196	| 5NN | 599 報告的簡寫 | QTH | 我的位置是 |
197	| NAME | 我的名字是 | OP | 操作員 |
198	| UR | 你的 | ES | 和 |
199	
200	**實際上大家怎麼用**：大部分人仍然是**用手即時發**（直鍵或 paddle），對方**用耳朵抄**，這是這項技能的核心。另外也很常見：
201	
202	- 電腦或「CW 鍵盤」：先打好字放在緩衝區，機器用固定速度送出，一邊送一邊還可以繼續打（type-ahead）。
203	- 比賽軟體：用 F 鍵送 `CQ TEST`、報告這類事先寫好的片語（macro）。
204	- 收的一方：有人用軟體解碼（fldigi、CW Skimmer，比賽和 Reverse Beacon Network 大量使用），但通聯本身多半還是靠人耳。`[調研]`
205	
206	TYPE 頁的 LIVE 對應「打一個送一個」，COMPOSE 對應「先打好再送」，片語鍵對應 macro。
207	
208	## 和 Vail 搭配 { #vail }
209	
210	單字、呼號、Q code、QSO 模擬、長篇抄收、和人互傳，這些深度訓練交給 Vail，不在韌體裡重做。FM-1 接上電腦就是一個 Vail 認得的 MIDI 電鍵：
211	
212	- **格式** `[上游]`：channel 1、note 0 是「已經排好時序的按鍵」，按下 `90 00 7F`、放開 `80 00 00`（[vail-adapter 的 MIDI spec](https://github.com/Vail-CW/vail-adapter/blob/master/docs/MIDI_INTEGRATION_SPEC.md)）。FM-1 的 iambic keyer 在機器上就把時序排好，所以一律送 note 0。
213	- **Vail 網頁怎麼讀** `[上游]`：[vail_web_repeater](https://github.com/Vail-CW/vail_web_repeater) 的 `static/scripts/inputs.mjs` 把 note 0 當直鍵；它只看指令（note on / note off），**不看 velocity**，所以 `90 00 00` 在 Vail 會被當成按下。我們放開一律送 `80 00 00`。Vail 打開頁面時會對所有 MIDI 輸出送 `B0 00 00`、`B0 01 xx`、`C0 xx`（給 Vail adapter 的設定），FM-1 會忽略。
214	- **Vail 的訓練工具** `[上游]`：[training.vailmorse.com](https://training.vailmorse.com/) 有 Vail CW School（進度統計、遊戲）、Hear It Type It、Send Practice（明寫支援 USB CW key 和 MIDI adapter）、Free Practice、Morse Mailbox（和朋友非同步互傳）、QSO Simulator 等。
215	- **驗證狀態**：位元組在 host simulator 和 fm1-emu 都確認過 `[模擬]`；**還沒有實際在瀏覽器裡用 FM-1 開 Vail 測過。**
216	
217	## 電腦端（host）
218	
219	`host/morse/`（Python，mido + python-rtmidi），協定見 [`host/morse/PROTOCOL.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/M-VAVE_FM-1/blob/main/host/morse/PROTOCOL.md)：
220	
221	| 指令 | 做什麼 |
222	|---|---|
223	| `just morse-type` | 在 FM-1 的 KEY 頁發報（或在 TYPE 頁打字），解出的字打進 Mac 目前的視窗。要給終端機 Accessibility 權限；`--dry-run` 只印出來 |
224	| `just morse-send 文字` | FM-1 把文字當成「收到的」播出來，用來練抄收。`-` 從 stdin 一行一行送 |
225	| `just morse-sim` | 不接 FM-1，用文字模擬 |
226	| `just morse-backup FILE`、`just morse-restore FILE` | 學習進度的備份與還原（韌體 0.4 起，見[備份與還原](#backup)） |
227	
228	解碼在 FM-1 上做，host 只收結果（`T_CHAR`），所以畫面上看到的和打進電腦的一定一樣。host 每收到一次 HEARTBEAT 就回一個 HELLO_ACK；FM-1 超過 10 秒沒收到 host 的東西就當成斷線。
229	
230	## 兩台互傳
231	
232	現況和選項見[接口與連線](../hardware/io.md#two-units)。這台軟體的設計是**線路上傳按鍵動作（note on / off），不傳文字**，收的一方自己解碼，像真的電報線。好處是同一套格式可以走 USB、兩種藍牙 stack、USB host、經電腦轉送，Vail 也聽得懂。
233	
234	我手上只有一台，所以直連排在下一版（見[路線圖](#roadmap)），先用電腦和 Vail 跟人互傳。
235	
236	## 藍牙方案（0.5 研究） { #bluetooth }
237	
238	2026-11-18 的研究，還沒實作。
239	
240	### 要做到什麼
241	
242	| 用途 | 怎麼連 |
243	|---|---|
244	| Mac 上的 Vail、MORSE on the web、`just morse-*`，不接線 | FM-1 當 BLE-MIDI peripheral，Mac 在「音訊 MIDI 設定」的藍牙視窗連上 |
245	| iPad、手機 | 同上（但見下面「瀏覽器」） |
246	| 兩台 FM-1 互打 | 一台當 central，連上另一台（`ble_central`） |
247	
248	### 已經有的
249	
250	- **Conductor 已經在這台機器上走通** `[實機]`：fm1-base 的 own stack（`ble_stack = "own"`），2026-11-17 Mac 不用配對碼就連上 `FM-1 3399`，port 叫 `FM-1 3399 Bluetooth`，daemon 經藍牙收發 SysEx。做法見 [Conductor 的藍牙](../agentic/conductor.md)：
251	    - `hostlink` 會自己把 BLE 的 SysEx 封包組回 frame；
252	    - 藍牙的紀錄由 app 接管（`APP_BLE_STORE`），只放 RAM，不寫 flash；
253	    - fm1-emu 兩種晶片都是 0 次寫入。
254	- **MORSE 的程式本來就分得開傳輸**：`hostlink` 支援 USB 和 BLE 兩條路；按鍵用 Vail 格式的 note 0，走哪條路都一樣。
255	- **fm1-base own stack 的時間戳記** `[上游]`（`docs/bt/BLE-STACK.md` §6）：
256	    - **送出**時帶真實的 13-bit 毫秒時間戳記（JieLi 原本的 stack 都送 `80 80`）。
257	    - **收進**時有 `ble_midi_time`：照送出端的時間戳記排時間，把同一個 connection event 擠在一起的訊息拉開。
258	    - `plat_midi_send` 可以在 1 kHz tick 裡呼叫，所以按鍵的時間戳記是按下的那一刻。
259	
260	### MORSE 要改的地方
261	
262	1. `fm1.toml`：`ble = true`、`ble_stack = "own"`、`ble_diag = false`（省 2.4 KB RAM）、`ble_midi_time = true`。
263	2. `app.h` 定義 `APP_BLE_STORE`，`app.c` 實作 `app_ble_load` / `app_ble_save`，只放 RAM（照 Conductor）。沒有這一步 build 會失敗（缺 `OBJ_BLE`），2026-11-18 試過。
264	3. 主迴圈：`plat_midi_in` 從 `PORT_BLE` 來的封包，SysEx 交給 `hl_sx_packet` 組回 frame，note 0 交給收訊解碼器，時間用 `plat_midi_in_t24`。
265	4. 按鍵：`plat_midi_send(…, TO_USB | TO_BLE_HOST)`。
266	5. 設定頁加 BLUETOOTH 開關（Conductor 是 `OCT+`），header 顯示 `BT`。
267	6. 兩台互打再加 `ble_central = true`，以及「掃描、選一台、連上」的畫面。
268	
269	### 時間準不準
270	
271	這是摩斯特有的問題：點在 20 WPM 只有 60 ms。BLE 的 connection interval 大約 7.5–15 ms，按鍵事件會晚 0–15 ms 才送到，**誤差可能達到一個點的 25%**。
272	
273	- **送出**：own stack 帶了真實的時間戳記。接收端照時間戳記排，抖動就會消失；照到達時間算，就會抖。CoreMIDI 會把 BLE-MIDI 的時間戳記換成封包時間 `[調研]`，但 Chrome 的 Web MIDI 和 Vail 網頁用的是哪一個，要實測。
274	- **收進**：開 `ble_midi_time` 後，FM-1 會照送出端的時間解碼，另一台 FM-1 或 Vail 送來的按鍵不會被擠在一起。
275	- **真的抖的話**：照原本的構想，用 note 的 velocity 帶上這個 mark 的長度（10 ms 一格），收的一方用長度而不是到達時間。只有收方也是 MORSE 才有用，Vail 不懂。
276	
277	### 瀏覽器
278	
279	| 平台 | 網頁（Vail、MORSE on the web）走藍牙 |
280	|---|---|
281	| macOS Chrome / Edge | 在「音訊 MIDI 設定」連上後，藍牙 MIDI 就是一般的 CoreMIDI port，Web MIDI 應該看得到 `[調研]`。MORSE on the web 靠 HELLO 找 port，程式不用改 |
282	| Android Chrome | 有 Web MIDI；藍牙 MIDI 裝置要先由系統或某個 app 連上 `[調研]` |
283	| iPad / iPhone | Safari 沒有 Web MIDI，網頁用不了；要用支援藍牙 MIDI 的 app `[調研]` |
284	
285	### 已知的限制
286	
287	- **一次只連一個 host**：own stack 同時只有一條連到電腦的 BLE MIDI 連線 `[上游]`。iPad 連著時，Mac 就要走 USB。
288	- **macOS 不會自己連回來** `[實機]`：FM-1 重開後要到藍牙 MIDI 視窗再按一次 Connect（Conductor 的經驗；它的 daemon 會自動彈出那個視窗）。
289	- **大小**：0.4 是 138 KB。own stack 大約多 41–46 KB，central 再多 13–22 KB（fm1-base 的數字）。Conductor 開藍牙後是 122 KB、RAM 38 KB。上限 581 KB、RAM 96 KB，都很寬裕。
290	- **電池**：藍牙開著的耗電還沒量。
291	- **模擬器沒有無線電**：藍牙只能在實機上測。
292	
293	### 驗證計畫
294	
295	1. host simulator：BLE 替身送 HELLO（傳輸 `01`）、BLUETOOTH 開關、0 次 store 寫入（照 Conductor 的測試）。
296	2. fm1-emu 兩種晶片：開機、存檔、重開，USB 照常、0 次多餘寫入。
297	3. 實機（要你核准刷機）：
298	    - Mac 藍牙連上，`just morse-send`、MORSE on the web、Vail 都能用；
299	    - **量抖動**：同一串按鍵分別走 USB 和藍牙，記下 Mac 收到的時間（CoreMIDI 封包時間和 Web MIDI 的 `timeStamp`），比較兩者的差；
300	    - 拔線後只用電池，連著打 10 分鐘看會不會斷。
301	4. 兩台互打：等有第二台。
302	
303	## 設計
304	
305	### 時序
306	
307	- **1 kHz tick**（`APP_TICK`，timer interrupt）：讀琴鍵 → keyer → 開關 sidetone 的 gate、送 MIDI、讀 MIDI in，按鍵變化連同時間戳放進 ring buffer。main loop 解碼、跑頁面和閃卡、畫畫面。
308	- **Sidetone 的抖動**：gate 每個 audio block 讀一次（256 frames = 5.8 ms），按下到出聲最多差一個 block。
309	- **琴鍵的 debounce**：按下約 1–2 ms 後看到、放開約 9 ms 後看到，所以直鍵的每個 mark 會被量長約 7 ms（fm1-base `bsp/boards/fm1/fm1_input.h`）。韌體在實機 build 時從直鍵的 mark 扣掉 7 ms 再解碼。fm1-emu 裡看到的是按下 +3 ms、放開 +10 ms，和預期一致 `[模擬]`。
310	- **解碼器**：分別追蹤 dit、dah 和字間間隔的平均，取中間當門檻，所以跟得上偏離設定 ±30% 的發報速度，也能讀 Farnsworth 拉開的間隔（單元測試：5／15／25／35 WPM 加 ±20% 抖動全對）。0.2 起，同一個字裡出現兩下長度差 2 倍以上時，會直接把它們當成一個 dit 一個 dah，並回頭修正前一下的判斷：新手太慢的 dit 被當成 dah，遇到第一個真正的 dah 就會改回來。但如果手打得比發報速度慢很多，連字裡的停頓都會超過切字的門檻，所以發報速度還是要設得接近你的手。
311	- **實機上看到的** `[實機]`：手打的 O（三個 dah）一次被讀成 M + T，因為 dah 之間停了 146、175 ms，和那次字與字之間的 169–224 ms 一樣長；字裡面的間隔應該只有一個 dit。另一次 dah 之間 124、133 ms 就讀對。也看到一次 9 ms 的按鍵彈跳：解碼器扣掉 debounce 偏差後當成雜訊忽略，但 MIDI 照送（Vail 會看到一下極短的按下）。
312	
313	### 存檔 { #flash }
314	
315	一筆紀錄（設定 + 學習進度，約 280 bytes）放在 `0xDA000`–`0xDBFFF`，透過 fm1-base 的 storage 層存（A/B 兩份、CRC）。在回合結束或離開、改設定 3 秒後才寫。不碰 SLOOP、Agent Deck、CTL-1 共用的 `0xFC000`。這台機器所有備份的 `0xDA000`–`0xDBFFF` 都是空的。
316	
317	0.2 沿用 0.1 的紀錄格式：0.1 留下的空位改放 KEY／TYPE／LISTEN 的顯示選項、發報速度、LISTEN 的節目。從 0.1 升級時設定和進度都保留，發報速度從 0 補成預設的 10（fm1-emu 兩種晶片驗證過 `[模擬]`）。
318	
319	預演 `[模擬]`：把 `firmware/morse/build/morse.fwsc` 疊在 `backups/2026-11-17-2052-pre-conductor/` 上開機、改一個設定、玩完一回合：
320	
321	| | sector |
322	|---|---|
323	| 安裝（和目前機上的 Conductor 不同的部分） | `0x04000`–`0x1EFFF`，27 個；套件映像範圍是 `0x04000`–`0x92FFF` |
324	| 執行時寫入 | `0xDA000`–`0xDBFFF`，只有這 2 個 |
325	
326	### 大小
327	
328	`just fw-build morse`（2026-11-17）：
329	
330	| 版本 | app | `.data+.bss` |
331	|---|---|---|
332	| 0.1 | 109,508 B | 27,180 / 98,304 B |
333	| 0.2 | 127,712 B | 28,444 / 98,304 B |
334	| 0.3 | 127,880 B | 28,444 / 98,304 B |
335	| 0.4 | 138,076 B（release） | 29,084 / 98,304 B |
336	
337	上限是 581,564 B；RAM code 5,100 / 32,768 B；套件 616,003 B，開發版 identity `FM-1_4100`。目前都沒有開藍牙；加上 own BLE stack 和 central 大約再多 55–70 KB，仍然很寬裕。
338

351	| 刷進實機 | `just fm1-switch firmware/morse/build/morse.fwsc` | 寫入 30 個 sector（`0x04000`–`0x21FFF`），和預演一致 `[實機]` |

384	## 獨立 repo 和上架 { #release }
385	
386	2026-11-18 為了上架 [The Firmware Hub](../firmware/hub.md#listing)，韌體搬到 [daviddwlee84/fm1-morse](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/fm1-morse)（用 `git subtree split` 保留歷史），在本 repo 以 submodule 引回 `firmware/morse`。
387	
388	- **授權**：2026-11-18 從 MIT 改成 GPL-3.0-or-later，讓拿去改的人分享出來的版本也要開源。fm1-base 的 MPL-2.0 和 `common/` 的 MIT 都可以併入 GPL 作品；SLOOP 就是 GPL-3.0 加 felucca-bsp 的前例。之後的藍牙用 fm1-base 自己的 stack，不會連結 JieLi 的閉源函式庫，所以避開了 GPL 不能連結閉源庫的問題。`57ea786` 以前的版本以 MIT 公開，仍可依 MIT 使用。套件內容不受影響（改授權前後的 `.fwsc` 完全相同）。
389	- **新 repo 的內容**：根目錄有 GPL-3.0 `LICENSE`、`fmhub.json`（`kinds: other`、`sounds: none`，卡片圖是 `docs/screen.png`）、英文 README（含 Hub 要求說明的「其他韌體的資料」）、鎖定版本的 fm1-base submodule，以及自帶一份 `common/`（hostlink、ledfx）。
390	- **identity 前綴改成 `FM-1_41`**：原本的 `FM-1_13` 和 Hub 上 FM-1 Midi-Mania 的 `FM-1_137` 開頭相同。目錄裡沒有任何 `FM-1_41x`，但送審前仍要用 Hub 的 #check 確認。開發版是 `FM-1_4100`，release 版是 `FM-1_41` 加 XXYYZZ（0.3 是 `FM-1_41000300`）。存檔位置不變，進度會保留。
391	- **build**：在本 repo 用 `third_party/fm1-base` build（`just fw-test morse`、`just morse-release 0.3`）。子 repo 裡的那份 fm1-base 是給它單獨 build 用的，`fw-setup` 不會去抓。
392	- **改程式的流程**：在 `firmware/morse` 裡 commit 並推到 fm1-morse，再到本 repo commit 新的 submodule 指標。**要先 commit 指標，再 build**：`just fw-build`、`just morse-release` 都會先跑 `fw-setup`，而它的 `git submodule update` 會把 `firmware/morse` 切回本 repo 記錄的 commit（detached HEAD）。2026-11-18 就因為這樣，build 出來的 0.4 套件裡是舊的出題邏輯，在模擬器裡看到第一回合只有 6 張卡才發現。

28	## 學習曲線
29	
30	- **排程用 FSRS-6**。把 [py-fsrs](https://github.com/open-spaced-repetition/py-fsrs)（MIT）的 scheduler 移植成 C，數百行，只需要 `expf`、`powf`（FPU 是單精度，夠用），用 py-fsrs 產生的參考數據測試。官方沒有嵌入式 C 版 `[上游]`。
31	- **每張卡的狀態約 8 B**：stability、difficulty 量化成 16 bit，加上狀態與到期日。3,000 張卡約 24 KB。
32	- **畫面上畫遺忘曲線**：評分後顯示這張卡的 R(t) 曲線和下次複習日；統計頁顯示每天複習量與各狀態的卡數。
33	- **沒有 RTC**：FM-1 關機後不知道過了幾天（只有 179 秒就繞回來的計時器）。接電腦時由電腦送日期；離線時沿用最後一次同步的日期，提供手動「換到下一天」。Morse 用「回合」代替天數，也是同一個原因。

46	## Anki 匯入 {#anki}
47	
48	- **`.apkg` 是 zip** `[上游]`。有 `meta`（protobuf）時是新格式：zstd 壓縮的 `collection.anki21b`，媒體檔也壓縮；沒有 `meta` 時是舊格式 `collection.anki21` 或 `collection.anki2`（SQLite，不壓縮）。
49	- **欄位**：`notes.flds`，以 `0x1f` 分隔；欄位名稱在 `fields` 表（新）或 `col.models` JSON（舊）。
50	- **既有排程**：`cards` 的 `ivl`、`factor`、`due`、`reps`、`lapses`；FSRS 的記憶狀態在 `cards.data` 的 JSON（`s`、`d`）。匯入時直接拿來當 FM-1 上的初始狀態。
51	- **讀取方式**：自己寫一個 MIT 的小 reader（`zipfile` + `zstandard` + `sqlite3` + 很小的 protobuf 解碼）。官方的 `anki` 套件是 AGPL，只能當選用依賴。
52	- **雙向同步**：Anki Desktop 開著時用 [AnkiConnect](https://git.sr.ht/~foosoft/anki-connect)（GPL，HTTP API）：`cardsInfo` 讀、`answerCards` 或 `insertReviews` 把 FM-1 上的複習寫回去。`answerCards` 會不會把時間記成同步當下，還沒驗證 `[調研]`。
