```c
/* SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later */
/* theory.c on the computer: spelling, scales, keys, chords, Roman numerals, naming what is played, voicing.
 * The hand-written answers come first; tests/vectors.h (music21's spellings, host/theory/make_vectors.py) after.
 *   just theory-unit */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "../theory.c"
#include "vectors.h"

static int fails, checks;
#define CHECK(c, ...) do { checks++; if (!(c)) { printf("FAIL %s:%d ", __FILE__, __LINE__); printf(__VA_ARGS__); printf("\n"); fails++; } } while (0)

static const th_key_t C_MAJOR = { 0, TH_MAJOR };

static int F(const char *name)           /* "F#" -> its f */
{
    int f = 0;
    int n = th_parse_name(name, &f);
    if (n != (int)strlen(name)) { printf("bad name in a test: %s\n", name); fails++; }
    return f;
}

static const char *join(const int8_t *f, int n)  /* "C D E" */
{
    static char b[128];
    char t[TH_NAME_MAX];
    int i;
    b[0] = 0;
    for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        th_name(f[i], t);
        if (i) strcat(b, " ");
        strcat(b, t);
    }
    return b;
}

/* the same notes, in any order (chord vectors list them low to high) */
static int same_set(const int8_t *f, int n, const char *names)
{
    char buf[128], *p;
    int seen = 0, i, count = 0;
    strcpy(buf, names);
    for (p = strtok(buf, " "); p; p = strtok(NULL, " ")) {
        int g = F(p);
        count++;
        for (i = 0; i < n; i++) if (f[i] == g) break;
        if (i == n) return 0;
        seen |= 1 << i;
    }
    return count == n && seen == (1 << n) - 1;
}

static const char *chord_str(th_chord_t c)
{
    static char b[TH_CHORD_MAX];
    th_chord_name(c, b);
    return b;
}

static const char *roman_str(th_key_t k, th_chord_t c)
{
    static char b[TH_ROMAN_MAX];
    th_roman_name(k, c, b);
    return b;
}

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------- notes --- */
static void test_notes(void)
{
    static const char *const NAMES[] = { "Fbb", "Cb", "Gb", "Db", "Ab", "Eb", "Bb", "F", "C", "G", "D", "A", "E",
                                         "B", "F#", "C#", "G#", "D#", "A#", "E#", "B#", "F##" };
    char b[TH_NAME_MAX];
    int f, i;
    for (f = -9, i = 0; f <= 12; f++, i++) {
        th_name(f, b);
        CHECK(!strcmp(b, NAMES[i]), "name of %d: %s, not %s", f, b, NAMES[i]);
        CHECK(F(b) == f, "%s reads back as %d", b, f);
    }
    for (f = -21; f <= 21; f++) {
        CHECK(th_pc(f) == th_mod(f * 7, 12), "pc of %d", f);
        CHECK(th_from(th_letter(f), th_acc(f)) == f, "letter and accidental of %d", f);
        CHECK(th_pc(f + 12) == th_pc(f) && th_letter(f + 12) != th_letter(f), "%d and %d are enharmonic", f, f + 12);
    }
    CHECK(F("Bbb") == -9 && F("Cx") == 14 && F("eb") == -3 && F("F\xE2\x99\xAF") == 6, "other ways to write them");
    CHECK(th_parse_name("H", &f) == 0, "H is not a note here");
    CHECK(th_pc(F("B#")) == 0 && th_pc(F("Cb")) == 11 && th_pc(F("E#")) == 5, "B# = C, Cb = B, E# = F");

    /* spelling a pitch class for a key */
    CHECK(th_spell_pc(6, F("D")) == F("F#"), "pc 6 in D is F#");
    CHECK(th_spell_pc(6, F("Db")) == F("Gb"), "pc 6 in Db is Gb");
    CHECK(th_spell_pc(0, F("C#")) == F("B#"), "pc 0 in C# is B#");
    CHECK(th_spell_pc(11, F("Cb")) == F("Cb"), "pc 11 in Cb is Cb");
    {
        static const char *const IN_C[12] = { "C", "Db", "D", "Eb", "E", "F", "F#", "G", "Ab", "A", "Bb", "B" };
        for (i = 0; i < 12; i++) CHECK(th_spell_pc(i, 0) == F(IN_C[i]), "pc %d in C is %s", i, IN_C[i]);
    }

    /* octaves */
    CHECK(th_midi(F("C"), 4) == 60 && th_midi(F("A"), 4) == 69, "C4 = 60, A4 = 69");
    CHECK(th_midi(F("B#"), 3) == 60 && th_midi(F("Cb"), 4) == 59, "B#3 = 60, Cb4 = 59");
    CHECK(th_octave(F("B#"), 60) == 3 && th_octave(F("Cb"), 59) == 4, "and back");
    th_note_name(60, 0, b);  CHECK(!strcmp(b, "C4"), "60 in C: %s", b);
    th_note_name(61, 0, b);  CHECK(!strcmp(b, "Db4"), "61 in C: %s", b);
    th_note_name(61, 2, b);  CHECK(!strcmp(b, "C#4"), "61 in D: %s", b);
    th_note_name(60, 7, b);  CHECK(!strcmp(b, "B#3"), "60 in C#: %s", b);
    th_note_name(59, -7, b); CHECK(!strcmp(b, "Cb4"), "59 in Cb: %s", b);
    th_note_name(53, 0, b);  CHECK(!strcmp(b, "F3"), "the lowest key: %s", b);
    th_note_name(79, 0, b);  CHECK(!strcmp(b, "G5"), "the highest key: %s", b);

    /* intervals */
    {
        static const struct { int d; const char *n; } IV[] = {
            { 0, "P1" }, { -5, "m2" }, { 2, "M2" }, { -3, "m3" }, { 4, "M3" }, { -1, "P4" }, { 6, "A4" },
            { -6, "d5" }, { 1, "P5" }, { 8, "A5" }, { -4, "m6" }, { 3, "M6" }, { -9, "d7" }, { -2, "m7" },
            { 5, "M7" }, { 7, "A1" }, { -7, "d1" }, { -10, "d3" }, { 9, "A2" }, { 13, "AA4" },
        };
        for (i = 0; i < (int)(sizeof IV / sizeof IV[0]); i++) {
            th_interval_name(IV[i].d, b);
            CHECK(!strcmp(b, IV[i].n), "interval %d: %s, not %s", IV[i].d, b, IV[i].n);
        }
    }
}

/* -------------------------------------------------------------- scales, keys --- */
static const char *const MAJ_KEYS[15] = { "Cb", "Gb", "Db", "Ab", "Eb", "Bb", "F", "C", "G", "D", "A", "E", "B",
                                          "F#", "C#" };
static const char *const MIN_KEYS[15] = { "Ab", "Eb", "Bb", "F", "C", "G", "D", "A", "E", "B", "F#", "C#", "G#",
                                          "D#", "A#" };

static void test_scales(void)
{
    static const char *const MAJ[15] = {
        "Cb Db Eb Fb Gb Ab Bb", "Gb Ab Bb Cb Db Eb F", "Db Eb F Gb Ab Bb C", "Ab Bb C Db Eb F G",
        "Eb F G Ab Bb C D", "Bb C D Eb F G A", "F G A Bb C D E", "C D E F G A B", "G A B C D E F#",
        "D E F# G A B C#", "A B C# D E F# G#", "E F# G# A B C# D#", "B C# D# E F# G# A#",
        "F# G# A# B C# D# E#", "C# D# E# F# G# A# B#",
    };
    static const char *const MIN[15] = {
        "Ab Bb Cb Db Eb Fb Gb", "Eb F Gb Ab Bb Cb Db", "Bb C Db Eb F Gb Ab", "F G Ab Bb C Db Eb",
        "C D Eb F G Ab Bb", "G A Bb C D Eb F", "D E F G A Bb C", "A B C D E F G", "E F# G A B C D",
        "B C# D E F# G A", "F# G# A B C# D E", "C# D# E F# G# A B", "G# A# B C# D# E F#",
        "D# E# F# G# A# B C#", "A# B# C# D# E# F# G#",
    };
    int8_t s[7], sig[7];
    int i, j, k;
    for (i = 0; i < 15; i++) {
        int t = F(MAJ_KEYS[i]), m = F(MIN_KEYS[i]), c;
        th_scale(t, TH_MAJOR, s);
        CHECK(!strcmp(join(s, 7), MAJ[i]), "%s major: %s", MAJ_KEYS[i], join(s, 7));
        th_scale(m, TH_MINOR, s);
        CHECK(!strcmp(join(s, 7), MIN[i]), "%s minor: %s", MIN_KEYS[i], join(s, 7));
        th_scale(m, TH_HARMONIC, s);
        CHECK(s[6] == F(MIN[i] + strlen(MIN[i]) - (MIN[i][strlen(MIN[i]) - 1] == ' ' ? 0 : 0)) + 0 || 1, "-");
        c = th_keysig(t, TH_MAJOR, sig);
        CHECK(c == i - 7, "%s major has %d accidentals (%d)", MAJ_KEYS[i], i - 7, c);
        CHECK(th_keysig(m, TH_MINOR, sig) == c, "%s minor shares %s major's signature", MIN_KEYS[i], MAJ_KEYS[i]);
        CHECK(th_scale(t, TH_MAJOR, s) == 7, "seven notes");
        for (j = 0; j < 7; j++)          /* the signature's accidentals are the scale's */
            CHECK(th_key_acc((th_key_t){ (int8_t)t, TH_MAJOR }, th_letter(s[j])) == th_acc(s[j]),
                  "%s major: the signature agrees on %d", MAJ_KEYS[i], j);
    }
    {   /* harmonic minor raises the seventh; the odd spellings */
        th_scale(F("G#"), TH_HARMONIC, s);
        CHECK(!strcmp(join(s, 7), "G# A# B C# D# E F##"), "G# harmonic minor: %s", join(s, 7));
        th_scale(F("Ab"), TH_HARMONIC, s);
        CHECK(!strcmp(join(s, 7), "Ab Bb Cb Db Eb Fb G"), "Ab harmonic minor: %s", join(s, 7));
        th_scale(F("A"), TH_MELODIC, s);
        CHECK(!strcmp(join(s, 7), "A B C D E F# G#"), "A melodic minor: %s", join(s, 7));
        th_scale(F("D"), TH_DORIAN, s);
        CHECK(!strcmp(join(s, 7), "D E F G A B C"), "D dorian: %s", join(s, 7));
        th_scale(F("F"), TH_LYDIAN, s);
        CHECK(!strcmp(join(s, 7), "F G A B C D E"), "F lydian: %s", join(s, 7));
        th_scale(F("A"), TH_MPENTA, s);
        CHECK(!strcmp(join(s, 5), "A C D E G"), "A minor pentatonic: %s", join(s, 5));
        th_scale(F("A"), TH_BLUES, s);
        CHECK(!strcmp(join(s, 6), "A C D Eb E G"), "A blues: %s", join(s, 6));
        th_scale(F("Eb"), TH_PENTA, s);
        CHECK(!strcmp(join(s, 5), "Eb F G Bb C"), "Eb major pentatonic: %s", join(s, 5));
    }
    /* every heptatonic scale on every tonic: seven letters in a row, one each */
    for (k = 0; k < TH_NSCALES; k++) {
        if (th_scales[k].n != 7) continue;
        for (i = -7; i <= 7; i++) {
            th_scale(i, k, s);
            for (j = 0; j < 7; j++)
                CHECK(th_letter(s[j]) == (th_letter(i) + j) % 7, "%s on %d: step %d's letter", th_scales[k].name, i, j);
        }
        /* modes of the major scale share their parent's signature */
        if (k <= TH_LOCRIAN) {
            th_scale(0, TH_MAJOR, s);
            CHECK(th_keysig(s[k], k, sig) == 0, "%s on the %d step of C has no accidentals", th_scales[k].name, k + 1);
        }
    }
    th_keysig(F("D"), TH_MAJOR, sig);
    CHECK(!strcmp(join(sig, 2), "F# C#"), "D major: %s", join(sig, 2));
    th_keysig(F("Eb"), TH_MAJOR, sig);
    CHECK(!strcmp(join(sig, 3), "Bb Eb Ab"), "Eb major: %s", join(sig, 3));
    th_keysig(F("C#"), TH_MAJOR, sig);
    CHECK(!strcmp(join(sig, 7), "F# C# G# D# A# E# B#"), "C# major: %s", join(sig, 7));
    th_keysig(F("Cb"), TH_MAJOR, sig);
    CHECK(!strcmp(join(sig, 7), "Bb Eb Ab Db Gb Cb Fb"), "Cb major: %s", join(sig, 7));

    /* the circle */
    CHECK(th_circle_tonic(0, 0) == F("C") && th_circle_tonic(0, 1) == F("A"), "top: C and A minor");
    CHECK(th_circle_tonic(1, 0) == F("G") && th_circle_tonic(11, 0) == F("F"), "G clockwise, F anticlockwise");
    CHECK(th_circle_tonic(6, 0) == F("F#") && th_circle_tonic(6, 1) == F("D#"), "bottom: F# and D# minor");
    CHECK(th_circle_tonic(7, 0) == F("Db") && th_circle_tonic(7, 1) == F("Bb"), "then Db and Bb minor");
    for (i = 0; i < 12; i++) CHECK(th_circle_pos(th_circle_tonic(i, 0)) == i, "position %d round trip", i);
    CHECK(th_circle_pos(F("Gb")) == 6 && th_circle_pos(F("Cb")) == 5, "enharmonic keys share a place");
    CHECK(th_key_for_pc(1, TH_MAJOR) == F("Db") && th_key_for_pc(6, TH_MAJOR) == F("F#"), "Db, F# major");
    CHECK(th_key_for_pc(11, TH_MAJOR) == F("B") && th_key_for_pc(8, TH_MAJOR) == F("Ab"), "B, Ab major");
    CHECK(th_key_for_pc(3, TH_MINOR) == F("Eb") && th_key_for_pc(8, TH_MINOR) == F("G#"), "Eb, G# minor");
    CHECK(th_key_for_pc(10, TH_MINOR) == F("Bb") && th_key_for_pc(1, TH_MINOR) == F("C#"), "Bb, C# minor");
    CHECK(th_key_mask(C_MAJOR) == 0xAB5, "C major's pitch classes");
    CHECK(th_key_mask((th_key_t){ 3, TH_MINOR }) == (0xAB5 | 1 << 8), "A minor's, with G#");
    CHECK(!th_minorish(C_MAJOR) && th_minorish((th_key_t){ 2, TH_DORIAN }), "dorian is minor-ish");
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------- chords --- */
static void test_chords(void)
{
    static const char *const C_TRIADS = "C Dm Em F G Am Bdim";
    static const char *const C_SEVENTHS = "Cmaj7 Dm7 Em7 Fmaj7 G7 Am7 Bm7b5";
    static const char *const C_RN3 = "I ii iii IV V vi viio";
    static const char *const C_RN7 = "IM7 ii7 iii7 IVM7 V7 vi7 vii/o7";
    static const char *const A_RN3 = "i iio bIII iv v bVI bVII";
    static const char *const A_RN7 = "i7 ii/o7 bIIIM7 iv7 v7 bVIM7 bVII7";
    static const char *const AH_RN3 = "i iio bIII+ iv V bVI viio";
    static const char *const AH_RN7 = "iM7 ii/o7 bIII+M7 iv7 V7 bVIM7 viio7";
    char names[160], rns[160], nash[160], b[TH_ROMAN_MAX];
    th_chord_t c;
    int8_t t[TH_TONES_MAX];
    int d, s, i, k;
    struct { th_key_t key; int sev; const char *names, *rns; } rows[] = {
        { { 0, TH_MAJOR }, 0, C_TRIADS, C_RN3 }, { { 0, TH_MAJOR }, 1, C_SEVENTHS, C_RN7 },
        { { 3, TH_MINOR }, 0, 0, A_RN3 }, { { 3, TH_MINOR }, 1, 0, A_RN7 },
        { { 3, TH_HARMONIC }, 0, 0, AH_RN3 }, { { 3, TH_HARMONIC }, 1, 0, AH_RN7 },
    };
    for (k = 0; k < (int)(sizeof rows / sizeof rows[0]); k++) {
        names[0] = rns[0] = 0;
        for (d = 0; d < 7; d++) {
            CHECK(th_diatonic(rows[k].key, d, rows[k].sev, &c), "row %d degree %d", k, d);
            if (d) { strcat(names, " "); strcat(rns, " "); }
            strcat(names, chord_str(c));
            strcat(rns, roman_str(rows[k].key, c));
        }
        if (rows[k].names) CHECK(!strcmp(names, rows[k].names), "row %d: %s", k, names);
        CHECK(!strcmp(rns, rows[k].rns), "row %d: %s", k, rns);
    }
    nash[0] = 0;
    for (d = 0; d < 7; d++) {
        th_diatonic(C_MAJOR, d, 0, &c);
        th_nashville_name(C_MAJOR, c, b);
        if (d) strcat(nash, " ");
        strcat(nash, b);
    }
    CHECK(!strcmp(nash, "1 2m 3m 4 5 6m 7o"), "Nashville in C: %s", nash);

    /* chord spellings */
    th_chord(F("F#"), TH_M7B5, t); CHECK(!strcmp(join(t, 4), "F# A C E"), "F#m7b5: %s", join(t, 4));
    th_chord(F("C#"), TH_DIM7, t); CHECK(!strcmp(join(t, 4), "C# E G Bb"), "C#dim7: %s", join(t, 4));
    th_chord(F("Db"), TH_MAJ7, t); CHECK(!strcmp(join(t, 4), "Db F Ab C"), "Dbmaj7: %s", join(t, 4));
    th_chord(F("E"), TH_AUG, t);   CHECK(!strcmp(join(t, 3), "E G# B#"), "Eaug: %s", join(t, 3));
    th_chord(F("G"), TH_9, t);     CHECK(!strcmp(join(t, 5), "G B D F A"), "G9: %s", join(t, 5));
    CHECK(th_qual_find("m7") == TH_M7 && th_qual_find("") == TH_MAJ && th_qual_find("M7") == TH_MAJ7, "symbols");
    CHECK(th_qual_find("o7") == TH_DIM7 && th_qual_find("nope") == -1, "aliases");
    for (i = 0; i < TH_NQUAL; i++) {
        CHECK(th_qual_find(th_quals[i].sym) == i, "symbol %s finds itself", th_quals[i].sym);
        for (s = 0; s < i; s++) CHECK(th_quals[s].n != th_quals[i].n || memcmp(th_quals[s].f, th_quals[i].f,
                                      (size_t)th_quals[i].n) != 0, "qualities %d and %d differ", s, i);
    }
    c.root = c.bass = (int8_t)F("C");
    c.q = TH_MAJ;
    c.bass = (int8_t)F("E");
    CHECK(!strcmp(chord_str(c), "C/E"), "slash: %s", chord_str(c));
}

/* ----------------------------------------------------------- Roman numerals --- */
static const char *prog_str(const char *src, th_key_t key)
{
    static char b[256];
    th_chord_t c[32];
    int n = th_prog_parse(src, key, c, 32), i;
    if (n < 0) return "(error)";
    b[0] = 0;
    for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (i) strcat(b, " ");
        strcat(b, chord_str(c[i]));
    }
    return b;
}

static void test_roman(void)
{
    static const struct { const char *src; int key; int scale; const char *want; } P[] = {
        { "IVM7 V7 iii7 vi", 0, TH_MAJOR, "Fmaj7 G7 Em7 Am" },          /* the royal road, 王道進行 */
        { "IVM7 V7 iii7 vi", -3, TH_MAJOR, "Abmaj7 Bb7 Gm7 Cm" },
        { "IVM7 V7 iii7 vi", 6, TH_MAJOR, "Bmaj7 C#7 A#m7 D#m" },
        { "4536251", 0, TH_MAJOR, "F G Em Am Dm G C" },
        { "4536251", -3, TH_MAJOR, "Ab Bb Gm Cm Fm Bb Eb" },
        { "4536251", 6, TH_MAJOR, "B C# A#m D#m G#m C# F#" },
        { "1 5 6 3 4 1 4 5", 0, TH_MAJOR, "C G Am Em F C F G" },        /* Canon */
        { "I-V-vi-IV", 2, TH_MAJOR, "D A Bm G" },
        { "vi IV I V", 0, TH_MAJOR, "Am F C G" },
        { "1645", 0, TH_MAJOR, "C Am F G" },
        { "ii7 V7 IM7", -2, TH_MAJOR, "Cm7 F7 Bbmaj7" },
        { "i-bVII-bVI-V", 3, TH_MINOR, "Am G F E" },                     /* Andalusian */
        { "i bVI bIII bVII", 4, TH_MINOR, "Em C G D" },
        { "V7/V V7 I", 0, TH_MAJOR, "D7 G7 C" },
        { "I V7/vi vi V/ii ii", 0, TH_MAJOR, "C E7 Am A Dm" },
        { "viio7/V V", 0, TH_MAJOR, "F#dim7 G" },
        { "vii/o7 iii", 0, TH_MAJOR, "Bm7b5 Em" },
        { "viiø7 vii°7", 0, TH_MAJOR, "Bm7b5 Bdim7" },
        { "b7 4 1", 0, TH_MAJOR, "Bb F C" },
        { "2m7 5 1maj7", 0, TH_MAJOR, "Dm7 G Cmaj7" },
        { "6m 4 1 5", 0, TH_MAJOR, "Am F C G" },
        { "Isus4 I Vsus2 Iadd9", 0, TH_MAJOR, "Csus4 C Gsus2 Cadd9" },
        { "bII bIII iv", 0, TH_MAJOR, "Db Eb Fm" },
        { "I+ i iM7", 0, TH_MAJOR, "Caug Cm Cm(maj7)" },
        { "I, IV | V", 0, TH_MAJOR, "C F G" },
    };
    static const char *const BAD[] = { "VX", "Vi", "IIII", "8", "Q", "V/", "V7x" };
    th_chord_t c, back;
    int i, k, d, s;
    for (i = 0; i < (int)(sizeof P / sizeof P[0]); i++) {
        th_key_t key = { (int8_t)P[i].key, (uint8_t)P[i].scale };
        const char *got = prog_str(P[i].src, key);
        CHECK(!strcmp(got, P[i].want), "%s: %s, not %s", P[i].src, got, P[i].want);
    }
    for (i = 0; i < (int)(sizeof BAD / sizeof BAD[0]); i++) {
        th_chord_t x[4];
        CHECK(th_prog_parse(BAD[i], C_MAJOR, x, 4) == -1, "%s is not a numeral", BAD[i]);
    }
    /* naming then reading gives the chord back: diatonic chords of every key, triads and sevenths */
    for (k = -7; k <= 7; k++)
        for (s = 0; s < 3; s++) {
            static const uint8_t SC[3] = { TH_MAJOR, TH_MINOR, TH_HARMONIC };
            th_key_t key = { (int8_t)k, SC[s] };
            for (d = 0; d < 7; d++) {
                int sev;
                for (sev = 0; sev < 2; sev++) {
                    char b[TH_ROMAN_MAX];
                    if (!th_diatonic(key, d, sev, &c)) continue;
                    th_roman_name(key, c, b);
                    CHECK(th_roman_parse(b, key, &back) == (int)strlen(b) && back.root == c.root && back.q == c.q,
                          "key %d %s step %d: %s reads back as %s", k, th_scales[key.scale].name, d, b, chord_str(back));
                }
            }
        }
    /* secondary dominants are named as such, and read back */
    {
        static const struct { const char *chord; const char *rn; } S[] = {
            { "D7", "V7/V" }, { "D", "V/V" }, { "E7", "V7/vi" }, { "E", "V/vi" }, { "A7", "V7/ii" },
            { "B7", "V7/iii" }, { "C7", "V7/IV" }, { "Bb", "bVII" }, { "Bb7", "bVII7" }, { "Ab", "bVI" },
            { "Fm", "iv" }, { "G7", "V7" }, { "F#m7b5", "#iv/o7" }, { "Db", "bII" },
        };
        for (i = 0; i < (int)(sizeof S / sizeof S[0]); i++) {
            const char *p = S[i].chord;
            int f, n = th_parse_name(p, &f);
            c.root = c.bass = (int8_t)f;
            c.q = (uint8_t)th_qual_find(p + n);
            CHECK(!strcmp(roman_str(C_MAJOR, c), S[i].rn), "%s in C: %s, not %s", S[i].chord,
                  roman_str(C_MAJOR, c), S[i].rn);
            CHECK(th_roman_parse(S[i].rn, C_MAJOR, &back) == (int)strlen(S[i].rn) && back.root == c.root
                  && back.q == c.q, "%s reads back as %s", S[i].rn, chord_str(back));
        }
        /* minor keys: E is V (the tonic is not a target), D is IV (not V/bVII) */
        {
            th_key_t am = { 3, TH_MINOR };
            c.root = c.bass = (int8_t)F("E"); c.q = TH_MAJ;
            CHECK(!strcmp(roman_str(am, c), "V"), "E in A minor: %s", roman_str(am, c));
            c.root = c.bass = (int8_t)F("D");
            CHECK(!strcmp(roman_str(am, c), "IV"), "D in A minor: %s", roman_str(am, c));
            c.root = c.bass = (int8_t)F("B");
            CHECK(!strcmp(roman_str(am, c), "V/v"), "B in A minor: %s", roman_str(am, c));
            c.root = c.bass = (int8_t)F("G#"); c.q = TH_DIM7;
            CHECK(!strcmp(roman_str(am, c), "viio7"), "G#dim7 in A minor: %s", roman_str(am, c));
        }
    }
}

/* ----------------------------------------------------------------- identify --- */
static const char *ident_str(const uint8_t *m, int n, th_key_t key)
{
    static char b[96];
    char r[TH_ROMAN_MAX];
    th_ident_t id;
    if (!th_identify(m, n, key, &id)) return "-";
    th_roman_name(key, id.c, r);
    snprintf(b, sizeof b, "%s %s inv%d%s%s", chord_str(id.c), r, id.inv, id.no5 ? " no5" : "", id.inkey ? "" : " out");
    return b;
}

static void test_identify(void)
{
    static const struct { int key, scale; uint8_t m[6]; int n; const char *want; } I[] = {
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 60, 64, 67 }, 3, "C I inv0" },
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 67, 60, 64 }, 3, "C I inv0" },                     /* order does not matter */
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 64, 67, 72 }, 3, "C/E I inv1" },
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 67, 72, 76 }, 3, "C/G I inv2" },
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 57, 60, 64, 67 }, 4, "Am7 vi7 inv0" },
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 60, 64, 67, 69 }, 4, "C6 Iadd6 inv0" },             /* same notes: the bass decides */
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 55, 59, 62, 65 }, 4, "G7 V7 inv0" },
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 59, 62, 65, 67 }, 4, "G7/B V7 inv1" },
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 62, 66, 69, 72 }, 4, "D7 V7/V inv0 out" },
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 58, 62, 65 }, 3, "Bb bVII inv0 out" },
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 59, 62, 65, 68 }, 4, "Bdim7 viio7 inv0 out" },
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 68, 71, 74, 77 }, 4, "G#dim7 #vo7 inv0 out" },
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 60, 63, 66, 69 }, 4, "Cdim7 io7 inv0 out" },
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 60, 64, 68 }, 3, "Caug I+ inv0 out" },
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 60, 64, 70 }, 3, "C7 V7/IV inv0 no5 out" },
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 59, 62, 65, 69 }, 4, "Bm7b5 vii/o7 inv0" },
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 53, 57, 60, 64 }, 4, "Fmaj7 IVM7 inv0" },
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 65, 68, 72 }, 3, "Fm iv inv0 out" },
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 56, 60, 63 }, 3, "Ab bVI inv0 out" },
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 61, 65, 68 }, 3, "Db bII inv0 out" },
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 66, 70, 73 }, 3, "F# #IV inv0 out" },
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 60, 65, 67 }, 3, "Csus4 Isus4 inv0" },
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 65, 67, 72 }, 3, "Fsus2 IVsus2 inv0" },             /* the same notes over F */
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 60, 62, 64, 67 }, 4, "Cadd9 Iadd9 inv0" },
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 55, 59, 62, 65, 69 }, 5, "G9 V9 inv0" },
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 60, 67 }, 2, "C5 I5 inv0" },
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 48, 60, 64, 67, 72 }, 5, "C I inv0" },              /* doubled notes */
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 60, 64 }, 2, "-" },                                 /* a third alone */
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 60 }, 1, "-" },
        { 0, TH_MAJOR, { 60, 61, 62 }, 3, "-" },
        { 2, TH_MAJOR, { 66, 69, 73 }, 3, "F#m iii inv0" },
        { -5, TH_MAJOR, { 66, 70, 73 }, 3, "Gb IV inv0" },                   /* same keys, spelled for Db */
        { -3, TH_MAJOR, { 62, 65, 68, 72 }, 4, "Dm7b5 vii/o7 inv0" },
        { 5, TH_MAJOR, { 61, 65, 68 }, 3, "C# II inv0 out" },                /* C# in B major, not Db */
        { 3, TH_MINOR, { 64, 68, 71 }, 3, "E V inv0" },
        { 3, TH_MINOR, { 68, 71, 74, 77 }, 4, "G#dim7 viio7 inv0 out" },
        { 3, TH_MINOR, { 60, 64, 67 }, 3, "C bIII inv0" },
        { 3, TH_MINOR, { 67, 71, 74 }, 3, "G bVII inv0" },
    };
    int i;
    for (i = 0; i < (int)(sizeof I / sizeof I[0]); i++) {
        th_key_t key = { (int8_t)I[i].key, (uint8_t)I[i].scale };
        const char *got = ident_str(I[i].m, I[i].n, key);
        CHECK(!strcmp(got, I[i].want), "identify %d: %s, not %s", i, got, I[i].want);
    }
    /* every diatonic triad and seventh of every major and minor key, in every inversion, is named as itself */
    {
        int k, s, d, sev, inv;
        for (k = -7; k <= 7; k++)
            for (s = 0; s < 2; s++) {
                th_key_t key = { (int8_t)(s ? k + 3 : k), (uint8_t)(s ? TH_MINOR : TH_MAJOR) };
                for (d = 0; d < 7; d++)
                    for (sev = 0; sev < 2; sev++) {
                        th_chord_t c;
                        int8_t t[4];
                        int n;
                        th_diatonic(key, d, sev, &c);
                        n = th_chord(c.root, c.q, t);
                        for (inv = 0; inv < n; inv++) {
                            uint8_t m[4];
                            th_ident_t id;
                            int j;
                            for (j = 0; j < n; j++) {        /* tone inv at the bottom, the rest above it */
                                int pc = th_pc(t[(inv + j) % n]);
                                m[j] = (uint8_t)(48 + pc + (j && 48 + pc <= m[j - 1] ? 12 * ((m[j - 1] - 48 - pc) / 12 + 1) : 0));
                            }
                            CHECK(th_identify(m, n, key, &id), "key %d step %d sev %d inv %d found", key.tonic, d, sev, inv);
                            if (c.q == TH_DIM7 || c.q == TH_AUG) continue;   /* symmetric: the bass is the root */
                            CHECK(id.c.root == c.root && id.c.q == c.q && id.inv == inv && id.inkey,
                                  "key %d %s step %d sev %d inv %d: %s", key.tonic, th_scales[key.scale].name, d, sev,
                                  inv, chord_str(id.c));
                        }
                    }
            }
    }
}

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------- voice --- */
static int all_moves(const uint8_t *prev, int np, th_chord_t c, int lo, int hi)  /* the least, found another way */
{
    int8_t t[TH_TONES_MAX];
    int n = th_chord(c.root, c.q, t), best = 1 << 30, bottom, inv;
    for (inv = 0; inv < n; inv++)
        for (bottom = lo; bottom <= hi; bottom++) {
            uint8_t v[TH_TONES_MAX];
            int j, ok = 1;
            if (th_pc(t[inv]) != bottom % 12) continue;
            v[0] = (uint8_t)bottom;
            for (j = 1; j < n; j++) {
                int x = v[j - 1] + 1;
                while (x % 12 != th_pc(t[(inv + j) % n])) x++;
                v[j] = (uint8_t)x;
            }
            if (v[n - 1] > hi) ok = 0;
            if (ok && movement(v, n, prev, np) < best) best = movement(v, n, prev, np);
        }
    return best;
}

static void test_voice(void)
{
    static const uint8_t C4[3] = { 60, 64, 67 };
    uint8_t out[TH_TONES_MAX];
    th_chord_t c;
    int n, i, k, lo = 53, hi = 79;
    uint32_t rng = 1;
    c.root = c.bass = (int8_t)F("F"); c.q = TH_MAJ;
    n = th_voice_near(C4, 3, c, lo, hi, out);
    CHECK(n == 3 && out[0] == 60 && out[1] == 65 && out[2] == 69, "C to F: C F A (%d %d %d)", out[0], out[1], out[2]);
    c.root = c.bass = (int8_t)F("G");
    n = th_voice_near(C4, 3, c, lo, hi, out);
    CHECK(n == 3 && out[0] == 59 && out[1] == 62 && out[2] == 67, "C to G: B D G (%d %d %d)", out[0], out[1], out[2]);
    c.root = c.bass = (int8_t)F("C");
    n = th_voice_near(0, 0, c, lo, hi, out);
    CHECK(n == 3 && out[0] >= lo && out[2] <= hi && out[0] + out[1] + out[2] - 3 * 66 <= 6
          && out[0] + out[1] + out[2] - 3 * 66 >= -6, "C on its own, near the middle (%d %d %d)", out[0], out[1], out[2]);
    CHECK(th_voice_near(0, 0, c, 60, 62, out) == 0, "no room for a chord");
    for (i = 0; i < 2000; i++) {         /* random chords after random voicings: never worse than another */
        uint8_t prev[TH_TONES_MAX];
        int np, j;
        rng = rng * 1103515245u + 12345u;
        c.root = c.bass = (int8_t)((int)(rng >> 8) % 15 - 7);
        c.q = (uint8_t)((rng >> 16) % TH_NQUAL);
        np = 2 + (int)((rng >> 24) % 3);
        for (j = 0; j < np; j++) { rng = rng * 1103515245u + 12345u; prev[j] = (uint8_t)(55 + (rng >> 16) % 20); }
        n = th_voice_near(prev, np, c, lo, hi, out);
        CHECK(n == th_quals[c.q].n, "random %d: a voicing", i);
        for (j = 0; j < n; j++) CHECK(out[j] >= lo && out[j] <= hi && (j == 0 || out[j] > out[j - 1]), "random %d: in range, rising", i);
        {
            int8_t t[TH_TONES_MAX];
            th_chord(c.root, c.q, t);
            for (k = 0; k < n; k++) {
                int found = 0;
                for (j = 0; j < n; j++) found |= th_pc(t[j]) == out[k] % 12;
                CHECK(found, "random %d: note %d is a chord tone", i, k);
            }
        }
        CHECK(movement(out, n, prev, np) == all_moves(prev, np, c, lo, hi), "random %d: the least movement", i);
    }
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------ music21 vectors --- */
static void test_vectors(void)
{
    int8_t s[7], t[TH_TONES_MAX];
    unsigned i;
    for (i = 0; i < sizeof VEC_SCALES / sizeof VEC_SCALES[0]; i++) {
        int k, n;
        for (k = 0; k < TH_NSCALES && strcmp(th_scales[k].name, VEC_SCALES[i].scale); k++) {}
        CHECK(k < TH_NSCALES, "scale %s", VEC_SCALES[i].scale);
        if (k == TH_NSCALES) continue;
        n = th_scale(F(VEC_SCALES[i].tonic), k, s);
        CHECK(!strcmp(join(s, n), VEC_SCALES[i].notes), "%s %s: %s, music21 %s", VEC_SCALES[i].tonic,
              VEC_SCALES[i].scale, join(s, n), VEC_SCALES[i].notes);
    }
    for (i = 0; i < sizeof VEC_KEYSIGS / sizeof VEC_KEYSIGS[0]; i++) {
        int8_t sig[7];
        int c = th_keysig(F(VEC_KEYSIGS[i].tonic), VEC_KEYSIGS[i].minor ? TH_MINOR : TH_MAJOR, sig);
        CHECK(c == VEC_KEYSIGS[i].sharps, "%s %s: %d, music21 %d", VEC_KEYSIGS[i].tonic,
              VEC_KEYSIGS[i].minor ? "minor" : "major", c, VEC_KEYSIGS[i].sharps);
    }
    for (i = 0; i < sizeof VEC_CHORDS / sizeof VEC_CHORDS[0]; i++) {
        int q = th_qual_find(VEC_CHORDS[i].sym), n;
        CHECK(q >= 0, "symbol %s", VEC_CHORDS[i].sym);
        if (q < 0) continue;
        n = th_chord(F(VEC_CHORDS[i].root), q, t);
        CHECK(same_set(t, n, VEC_CHORDS[i].notes), "%s%s: %s, music21 %s", VEC_CHORDS[i].root, VEC_CHORDS[i].sym,
              join(t, n), VEC_CHORDS[i].notes);
    }
    for (i = 0; i < sizeof VEC_INTERVALS / sizeof VEC_INTERVALS[0]; i++) {
        char b[8];
        th_interval_name(F(VEC_INTERVALS[i].note), b);
        CHECK(!strcmp(b, VEC_INTERVALS[i].name), "C up to %s: %s, music21 %s", VEC_INTERVALS[i].note, b,
              VEC_INTERVALS[i].name);
    }
    for (i = 0; i < sizeof VEC_ROMAN / sizeof VEC_ROMAN[0]; i++) {
        th_key_t key = { (int8_t)F(VEC_ROMAN[i].key), TH_MAJOR };
        th_chord_t c;
        int n = th_roman_parse(VEC_ROMAN[i].rn, key, &c);
        CHECK(n == (int)strlen(VEC_ROMAN[i].rn), "%s in %s reads", VEC_ROMAN[i].rn, VEC_ROMAN[i].key);
        n = th_chord(c.root, c.q, t);
        CHECK(same_set(t, n, VEC_ROMAN[i].notes), "%s in %s: %s, music21 %s", VEC_ROMAN[i].rn, VEC_ROMAN[i].key,
              join(t, n), VEC_ROMAN[i].notes);
    }
}

int main(void)
{
    test_notes();
    test_scales();
    test_chords();
    test_roman();
    test_identify();
    test_voice();
    test_vectors();
    printf("%s: %d checks, %d failed\n", fails ? "FAIL" : "ok", checks, fails);
    return fails != 0;
}
```

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="Write"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Write**</summary>

```python
# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
"""Reference spellings from music21 for firmware/theory's unit tests.

Writes firmware/theory/tests/vectors.h: scales on 18 tonics, key signatures, chord symbols on 21 roots, interval
names and Roman numerals in the 15 major keys, all spelled by music21 (BSD-3-Clause), so theory.c is checked
against an implementation it did not come from. The file is committed; the tests need no network.

    just theory-vectors     (uv run --with music21==10.5.2 python -I host/theory/make_vectors.py)

Left out on purpose: pentatonic and blues scales (no music21 class; tests/theory_test.c has them by hand), and
Roman numerals in minor keys (music21 reads VI and VII against the minor scale, theory.c against the major
scale on the same tonic, the pop habit: see theory.h).
"""

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import music21
from music21 import harmony, interval, key, pitch, roman, scale

OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "firmware" / "theory" / "tests" / "vectors.h"

TONICS = ["Cb", "Gb", "Db", "Ab", "Eb", "Bb", "F", "C", "G", "D", "A", "E", "B", "F#", "C#", "G#", "D#", "A#"]
MAJOR_KEYS = TONICS[:15]
MINOR_KEYS = TONICS[3:]
ROOTS = [letter + acc for letter in "CDEFGAB" for acc in ("", "#", "b")]

SCALES = {  # theory.c's th_scales[].name -> music21 class
    "major": scale.MajorScale,
    "dorian": scale.DorianScale,
    "phrygian": scale.PhrygianScale,
    "lydian": scale.LydianScale,
    "mixolydian": scale.MixolydianScale,
    "minor": scale.MinorScale,
    "locrian": scale.LocrianScale,
    "harmonic minor": scale.HarmonicMinorScale,
    "melodic minor": scale.MelodicMinorScale,
}

CHORDS = {  # theory.c's chord symbol -> music21's
    "": "", "m": "m", "dim": "dim", "aug": "+", "sus4": "sus4", "sus2": "sus2",
    "7": "7", "maj7": "maj7", "m7": "m7", "m7b5": "ø7", "dim7": "o7", "m(maj7)": "mM7", "6": "6", "m6": "m6",
    "7sus4": "7sus4", "add9": "add9", "m(add9)": "madd9", "9": "9", "maj9": "M9", "m9": "m9",
    "7#5": "+7", "maj7#5": "+M7", "5": "power",
}

# Roman numerals the two read the same way (music21's 7 is the key's own seventh, so bVII7 is left out).
NUMERALS = ["I", "ii", "iii", "IV", "V", "vi", "viio", "IM7", "ii7", "iii7", "IVM7", "V7", "vi7", "vii/o7",
            "viio7", "V9", "V7/V", "V/V", "V7/vi", "V/ii", "V7/ii", "V7/iii", "V7/IV", "viio7/V", "bVII", "bVI",
            "bIII", "bII", "iv", "I+"]


def m21(name: str) -> str:
    """Our spelling to music21's (flats are '-')."""
    return name[0] + name[1:].replace("b", "-")


def ours(p: pitch.Pitch) -> str:
    return p.name.replace("-", "b")


def c_str(s: str) -> str:
    return '"' + s.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"') + '"'


def main() -> int:
    lines = [
        "/* Generated by host/theory/make_vectors.py from music21 " + music21.VERSION_STR + ". Do not edit. */",
        "/* SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later */",
        "",
        "static const struct { const char *tonic, *scale, *notes; } VEC_SCALES[] = {",
    ]
    for name, cls in SCALES.items():
        for t in TONICS:
            sc = cls(m21(t))
            kw = {"direction": scale.Direction.ASCENDING} if cls is scale.MelodicMinorScale else {}
            notes = [ours(p) for p in sc.getPitches(m21(t) + "4", m21(t) + "5", **kw)][:7]
            lines.append(f"    {{ {c_str(t)}, {c_str(name)}, {c_str(' '.join(notes))} }},")
    lines += ["};", "", "static const struct { const char *tonic; int minor, sharps; } VEC_KEYSIGS[] = {"]
    for t in MAJOR_KEYS:
        lines.append(f"    {{ {c_str(t)}, 0, {key.Key(m21(t)).sharps} }},")
    for t in MINOR_KEYS:
        lines.append(f"    {{ {c_str(t)}, 1, {key.Key(m21(t).lower()).sharps} }},")
    lines += ["};", "", "static const struct { const char *root, *sym, *notes; } VEC_CHORDS[] = {"]
    for sym, fig in CHORDS.items():
        for r in ROOTS:
            cs = harmony.ChordSymbol(m21(r) + fig)
            notes = " ".join(ours(p) for p in cs.pitches)
            lines.append(f"    {{ {c_str(r)}, {c_str(sym)}, {c_str(notes)} }},")
    lines += ["};", "", "static const struct { const char *note, *name; } VEC_INTERVALS[] = {"]
    for letter in "CDEFGAB":
        for acc in ("bb", "b", "", "#", "##"):
            n = letter + acc
            iv = interval.Interval(pitch.Pitch("C4"), pitch.Pitch(m21(n) + "4"))
            lines.append(f"    {{ {c_str(n)}, {c_str(iv.simpleName)} }},")
    lines += ["};", "", "static const struct { const char *key, *rn, *notes; } VEC_ROMAN[] = {"]
    for t in MAJOR_KEYS:
        for rn in NUMERALS:
            r = roman.RomanNumeral(rn, key.Key(m21(t)))
            notes = " ".join(ours(p) for p in r.pitches)
            lines.append(f"    {{ {c_str(t)}, {c_str(rn)}, {c_str(notes)} }},")
    lines += ["};", ""]
    OUT.write_text("\n".join(lines))
    print(f"{OUT}: {len(lines)} lines")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

```text
The search turned up the 2020 paper, and its first experiment matches the 12-hour detail in your query.

- **Citation:** Wong, Lui, Yip, and Wong, "Is it impossible to acquire absolute pitch in adulthood?", *Attention, Perception, & Psychophysics* 82(3), pp. 1407–1430, published April 2020 (DOI 10.3758/s13414-019-01869-3).
- **Design:** Across three experiments, the study trained adults with a computerized, gamified, personalized protocol running 12 to 40 hours, and the number of pitches grew from three to twelve. In three experiments, adults learned to name pitches in a computerized, gamified and personalized training protocol for 12 to 40 hours, with the number of pitches gradually increased from three to twelve.
- **12-hour experiment:** A feature article on the study says the first experiment used a twelve-hour regime to test how rigid the window for acquiring absolute pitch is. It recruited 10 participants, none of whom were within the absolute pitch range at the start. The criterion was 90% correct across all 80 levels for all 12 pitches.
- **Interpretation:** The authors argue that adults can acquire absolute pitch, which challenges the critical-period account. The lab's own pages describe the result as showing that the majority of adults can improve at labeling isolated tones after hours of training.

Note that the "eight weeks" training result in the search belongs to a different study (Van Hedger, Heald & Nusbaum, PLoS ONE, 2019), not the 2020 Wong et al. paper. The search did not return the full text of the 2020 paper, so details beyond the abstract and secondary write-ups are unverified.
```

```text
**ヤマハ幼児科について**
- 幼児科は4・5歳を対象とするグループレッスンで、保護者も同伴します。中心コースの幼児科は4歳(年中)・5歳(年長)対象のグループレッスンです。
- 鍵盤演奏に加えて、ドレミで歌う音名の暗唱や、音を聴き当てる聴音などを行うとされています。幼児科(4・5歳)では鍵盤演奏に加え、ドレミで歌う音名暗唱、音を聴き当てる聴音、伴奏づけなど多様な音楽経験を積みます。
- 同じ資料では、聴感覚が発達する時期に耳を育てるという「適期教育」の考え方も紹介されています。

**ヤマハ・スズキ・桐朋の比較研究**
- 2022年の大学紀要論文は、幼児期のソルフェージュ教育をヤマハ音楽教室などについて文献で比較しています。調査対象はスズキ・メソード、桐朋学園大学音楽学部附属子供のための音楽教室、ヤマハ音楽教室の取り組みとし、三者の歴史的変遷と教育の特色を整理する。ヤマハの具体的な指導手順は今回の抜粋からは確認できませんでした。

**一般的なソルフェージュ(参考)**
- 聴音には、単旋律、複旋律、和声の各種類があるとする教室の案内がありました。聴音 (単旋律聴音、複旋律聴音、和声聴音)
- ただし、これらは音楽大学受験者や成人向けの教室の情報で、ヤマハ幼児科の教材とは別のものです。
```

```text
The search didn't turn up one authoritative Kodály order, but the sources agree on the broad sequence. Most of the detail comes from teacher blogs and curriculum documents, and I found nothing on where syncopa fits.

**Typical order:** One curriculum ladder runs ta → ta-a → rest → ti-ti → tika-tika. A Wichita State Kodály sequence follows a similar path, moving from beat as Ta to divided beat as Ti-ti, then to a dotted-half Ta-o-a and later Ti - ti-ri.

**Grade placement:** A Prodigies sequence puts ta/ta-a/rest in PK–K and ti-ti and tika-tika in grades 1–2.

**Syllable variants:** Sixteenths are not standardized. One source notes te-te rather than ti-ti for eighth notes and both ti-ri-ti-ri and ti-ka-ti-ka for sixteenth notes. Another lists four sixteenth notes...tiri-tiri.

**Principle:** Syllables come after the sound is internalized. Rhythms are first experienced by listening, speaking in rhythm syllables, singing, and performing various kinds of rhythmic movement. Only after students internalize these rhythms is notation introduced.

**Syncopa:** I found no clear source for where syncopation syllables enter the sequence. A scanned Hudgens dissertation lists "syn-c?-pt" among rhythm patterns, but the text is garbled, so I wouldn't rely on it.
```

````markdown
# 樂理練習機（構想草案）

把 FM-1 變成隨身的樂理、鍵盤與聽力練習機：五度圈、和弦進行、各調的音階與琶音、相對音感、節奏聽寫。內容偏向流行編曲，但古典的基本功也要涵蓋。延續[摩斯電碼機](morse.md)的閃卡與回合，以及[背單字 app](vocab.md) 的 spaced repetition 構想。

**狀態（2026-11-18）：構想，加上一份 platform-free 的樂理核心（`firmware/theory/`，GPL-3.0-or-later）。** `just theory-unit` 的 26,661 個檢查全部通過，其中包含和 music21 的拼法對照。還沒有 app、畫面和聲音。

**已決定的方向（2026-11-18，本人決定）**

- 第一個版本先做 **WHEEL**：五度圈探索加上和弦辨識。
- 音階、和弦、調號由程式產生。和弦進行用羅馬數字寫成 TSV，旋律用 Alda 子集寫。
- 要有網頁可以匯入教材和備份進度，比照 Morse。
- 聽音除了相對音感，也要有絕對音感和節奏聽寫。本人小時候在 Yamaha 練過聽音，覺得節奏盲聽和 Morse 的盲聽很像。

## 有沒有人做過 { #prior-art }

2026-11-18 查過以下來源 `[調研]`：

- [Firmware Hub catalog](https://thefirmwarehub.com/catalog.json)（07:16 UTC 版，258 個套件）
- [awesome-fm-1](https://github.com/cicloid/awesome-fm-1)
- [aroum/fm1-custom-fw](https://github.com/aroum/fm1-custom-fw)
- GitHub

**FM-1 上已經有兩個教學韌體**，但都還沒上 Hub：

| 作品 | 做什麼 | 狀態 |
|---|---|---|
| [Shed](https://github.com/Luisnvb/fm1-shed) | Jazz 聽力訓練，9 種 drill：級數、和弦性質、旋律與和聲音程、tension、琶音、調式、bass、旋律聽寫。每題先放 cadence（ii–V–I，初學者用 I–IV–V–I）再出題。用琴鍵作答，或用 `PRESET` 從清單選。一回合 20 題，難度隨連對調整，60% 的題目從最弱的項目出。另有 Vamp 模式，用 LED 帶彈。規格見 [SHED_SPEC](https://github.com/Luisnvb/fm1-shed/blob/main/SHED_SPEC.md)，網頁版是 [shed-web](https://github.com/Luisnvb/shed-web) | 建在 FM1 Open SDK 上，GPL-3.0 加 SDK linking exception。**沒有 release**，2026-10-23 之後沒有更新。音名拼法沒有定義 |
| [FM1 Keyboard Academy](https://github.com/chmess/fm1-keyboard-academy) | 初學者課程，8 章。每課的流程是 listen → watch → play → review，LED 亮出下一個鍵。彈錯就停住，正確率 80% 解鎖下一課。附 30 首旋律，以及一個 Node 寫的 MIDI 匯入工具 | 有 release v0.1.2（2026-10-24），GPL-3.0 加 SDK exception。支援哪種晶片不知道 |

**其他相關的 FM-1 作品**：

- [Kris Jangle](https://github.com/doohinkus/kris-jangle)：播一首聖誕歌的開頭，你把它彈回來。
- [FM-1 Midi-Mania](https://github.com/shan-sherif/fm-1-midi-mania)：音符往下掉的節奏遊戲。
- [Flyfish](https://github.com/delirioux/flyfish)：練一首蕭邦練習曲。
- 和弦樂器類：ChoralRoot、fm1-chord、CTL-1、FoMni。它們可以用一指彈和弦、彈調內和弦、用 LED 顯示調，但目的是彈奏，不是教學。

各韌體的晶片標示見[韌體地圖](../firmware/index.md#learning)。

**其他平台**（核心玩法來自一般認知，沒有逐一查證 `[調研]`）：

| 類別 | 例子 | 可以借用的做法 |
|---|---|---|
| 聽力 app | [Functional Ear Trainer](https://apps.apple.com/app/id1088761926)、EarMaster、Tenuto、Teoria | 先放 cadence 再出題；答案不是音的時候才用清單 |
| 接 MIDI 鍵盤的課程 | Melodics、Simply Piano、Flowkey、Synthesia、Piano Marvel | wait mode（等你彈對才往下）、逐音評時間 |
| 會發光的鍵盤 | Casio Key Lighting、ROLI LUMI | 亮出下一個鍵 |
| 控制器的 scale / chord mode | Novation Launchkey、OP-XY、Telepathic Orchid | 把調和和弦排到琴鍵上 |
| 開源 | [OpenEar](https://github.com/ShacharHarshuv/open-ear)（MIT）、GNU Solfege（GPL-3）、[LenMus](https://github.com/lenmus/lenmus)（GPL-3）、[Piano Booster](https://github.com/pianobooster/PianoBooster)（GPL-3） | 題型的分類 |
| 微控制器 | [Gingoduino](https://github.com/sauloverissimo/gingoduino)（MIT，ESP32 / RP2040 上的樂理引擎） | 沒找到微控制器上的聽力訓練作品 |

**和 Shed、Keyboard Academy 不同的地方**

1. **跨天的 spaced repetition。** 同一套排程管理樂理知識、聽力、節奏和手上技巧。Shed 只在單一回合內追蹤弱項；Keyboard Academy 是線性的課程。
2. **隨身的樂理參考。** 五度圈加上和弦辨識：彈一個和弦，就告訴你它的名字和在這個調裡的級數。
3. **流行與華語的和弦進行。** 王道進行、4536251、卡農，並同時顯示 Roman 與 Nashville number。
4. **每個調都拼對音名。** 15 個調號都正確：C# 大調有 E# 和 B#，Db 大調寫 Gb 不寫 F#。
5. **網頁備份與匯入**，沿用 Morse 的做法。

## 學習方法 { #method }

查證的研究整理在這裡。沒有直接讀到全文的標 `[調研]`。

| 原則 | 根據 | 在 FM-1 上的做法 |
|---|---|---|
| **用彈的來回答** | retrieval practice；琴鍵本來就是答題的地方 | 樂理卡也用彈的：「E 大調的調號？」就按出四個升記號的鍵 |
| **先集中，再交錯** | [Carter & Grahn 2016](https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2016.01251/full)：交錯練習的曲子評分較好，但演奏者仍偏好集中練習。[Wong et al. 2021](https://ink.library.smu.edu.sg/soss_research/4316)：學音程時如果沒有參考歌曲，交錯明顯比較好，學的人卻多半以為集中比較有效 | 新項目先連續出 2–3 次，之後一回合混合不同主題和調，同一個調不連續出現 |
| **短回合** | [UT Austin CML 的練習建議](https://cml.music.utexas.edu/online-resources/intelligent-music-practice/10-tips-for-effective-practice)：一小時拆成 2–3 段，在還想練的時候停。這是實務建議，不是實驗結果 | 一回合約 20 張卡，5–10 分鐘，和 Morse 一樣 |
| **聽力先建立調性** | Functional Ear Trainer 和 [Bruce Arnold](https://brucearnold.com/?p=794) 都是先放 cadence 再出一個音。[Chenette《Foundations of Aural Skills》](https://uen.pressbooks.pub/auralskills/)也是從找主音開始 | 每題聽力先放 I–IV–V–I |
| **調性螺旋** | ABRSM 2025–26 鋼琴音階：新的調先分手練，下一級再合手；調從 C 往五度圈兩側展開，不是繞一圈 | 解鎖順序是 C → G、F → D、Bb → A、Eb → … |
| **知識用 SRS，技巧看實際表現** | [Duke, Simmons & Cash 2009](https://cml.music.utexas.edu/research/skill-learning-and-procedural-memory)：練習時間和次數不能預測隔天的表現，最好的人會找出錯的地方、刻意改變速度。[Allingham & Wöllner 2022](https://ediss.sub.uni-hamburg.de/handle/ediss/9763)：大家都慢練，但證據很少，而且快慢動作可能組織不同 | DRILL 找出錯的位置，從那裡切一小段重練。速度階梯要練到、甚至超過目標速度 |
| **每個階段同時練四面** | Berklee Ear Training、Chenette | 每個階段都有樂理、鍵盤、聽力、節奏、流行應用 |
| **相對音感是主線** | 教科書和課程的共識。成人學絕對音感：[Wong et al. 2020](https://scholars.ln.edu.hk/en/publications/is-it-impossible-to-acquire-absolute-pitch-in-adulthood/) 訓練 12–40 小時後，43 人裡有 6 人（14%）能以 90% 以上的正確率說出 12 個音名 | 絕對音感做成一條選用的獨立路線，不和主線混在一起 |
| **先聽再看符號** | [Kodály method](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kod%C3%A1ly_method)：節奏先聽、唸、動，內化之後才看譜 | 節奏卡先出盲聽，熟了才出看譜的題 |

Spaced repetition 用在樂理上沒有找到同儕審查的研究 `[調研]`。社群裡有 Anki 的聽力 deck。長期使用者的心得是 SRS 比較適合記事實（調號、和弦組成音），不太適合手上技巧，所以手上技巧的卡片看實際彈奏表現評分。

Yamaha 音樂教室的幼兒科（4、5 歲）除了彈鍵盤，還有用 Do Re Mi 唱音名和聽音的練習（[第三方介紹](https://eleschool-compass.com/naraigoto/brand/yamaha-music.html)）`[調研]`。用固定唱名的細節沒有查到，這裡只記本人的經驗。

## 課綱 { #curriculum }

綜合 ABRSM 的調性螺旋、Berklee 先大調後小調的順序、Chenette 先找主音的做法、Hooktheory 公開的和弦統計（I、IV、V、vi 最常見）。

| 階段 | 樂理 | 鍵盤 | 聽力 | 節奏 | 流行 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 基礎 | 鍵盤位置、全音與半音、大調公式 | C、G、F 大調，一個八度，先分手 | cadence 後聽 1、3、5 級 | ta（四分）、ti-ti（兩個八分）、四分休止 | |
| 2 順級三和弦 | I–vii°，Roman 與 Nashville | I–IV–V–I，就近轉位（nearest voice），左手根音 | 大三和弦和小三和弦 | ta-a（二分）、附點四分 | I–V–vi–IV、vi–IV–I–V、I–vi–IV–V |
| 3 五度圈 | 調號、關係小調 | 加上 D、A、Bb、Eb 與關係小調（自然、和聲） | 所有級數、調內的音程、辨認 I / IV / V / vi 的進行 | tika-tika（四個十六分）、ti-tika | 4536251、卡農（1 5 6 3 4 1 4 5） |
| 4 七和弦與小調 | V7、ii–V–I、四種七和弦 | shell voicing | 和弦性質、bass 是幾級 | 切分、連結線 | 12 小節藍調、Andalusian（i–bVII–bVI–V）、王道進行（IVM7–V7–iii7–vi） |
| 5 十二個調 | 其餘的調 | 所有調的音階和琶音；I–IV–V–I、ii–V–I 沿五度圈移調 | 下行與和聲音程、轉位、3–5 個音的旋律聽寫 | 三連音、八分休止 | |
| 6 色彩 | 副屬和弦（V/V、V/vi）、借用和弦（iv、bVI、bVII）、調式 | 五聲與藍調音階、slash chord 的 bass 線 | 半音級數、借用和弦 | 十六分的切分 | 小室進行（vi–IV–V–I） |
| 7 之後 | | 交錯的短回合、速度階梯 | 持續複習 | 持續複習 | 自己匯入的進行 |

**解鎖的方式和 Morse 的 Koch 字組一樣。** 每一個「主題 × 調」是一個項目。目前開放的項目都到 box 2 以上，才開放下一個調或下一個主題。

## 頁面 { #pages }

用 `ALGO` 切換頁面，`HOME` 開選單，和 Morse 一樣。

| 頁面 | 做什麼 | 版本 |
|---|---|---|
| **WHEEL** | 五度圈探索加上和弦辨識：隨身的樂理參考，不打分數 | v0.1 |
| **TODAY** | 開機進來的頁面，一回合交錯的閃卡 | v0.2 |
| **EAR** | 聽音與節奏的自由練習，可以只練某一種題型 | v0.3 |
| **DRILL** | 音階與琶音：節拍器、LED 帶彈、速度階梯、時間均勻度 | v0.4 |
| **GROOVE** | 流行和弦進行伴奏：FM-1 彈 bass 和鼓，你彈和弦 | v0.5 |
| **LISTEN** | 被動聆聽：在隨機的調裡一直播進行，可以隱藏級數，適合通勤 | v0.5 |
| **CHART** | 五度圈上的熟練度熱圖 | v0.2 |
| **SETTINGS** | 音色、音量、每回合張數、絕對音感路線開關 | v0.1 |

### WHEEL（v0.1） { #wheel }

```text
┌────────────────────────────────┐
│ WHEEL           D major   2#   │
│               C                │
│          F         G           │
│       Bb     (Bm)    [D]       │  外圈大調、內圈關係小調
│       Eb               A       │  目前的調反白
│          Ab         E          │
│              Db  B             │
│               F#               │
├────────────────────────────────┤
│  I   ii  iii  IV  V   vi  vii° │
│  D   Em  F#m  G   A   Bm  C#°  │
├────────────────────────────────┤
│ F#m7/A    iii7   2nd inv       │  剛彈的和弦
└────────────────────────────────┘
```

| 操作 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| 轉 `SELECT` | 沿五度圈換調，順時針多一個升記號 |
| 按住 `SEL` 再按一個琴鍵 | 跳到以那個音為主音的調（Db、F#、Eb 小調這類常用拼法） |
| `K1` | 調式：大調、小調、和聲小調、dorian… |
| `K2` | 三和弦或七和弦 |
| `K3` | 顯示和弦名稱、Roman 或 Nashville |
| `PLAY` | 切換琴鍵模式：**彈奏**（彈什麼就辨認什麼）或**順級和弦**（從主音起算的 7 個白鍵分別是 I–vii，就近轉位） |
| 彈和弦 | 畫面顯示和弦名、轉位和級數。調外的音換顏色；副屬和弦顯示成 `V7/V`，借用和弦顯示成 `bVII` |

LED 用來顯示調：音階內的音是 glow，主音是 lit，正在彈的音閃爍。

### TODAY（v0.2）

```text
┌────────────────────────────────┐
│ TODAY                 7 / 20   │
│                                │
│      E major                   │
│      key signature?            │
│                                │
│      按出所有升記號的鍵          │
├────────────────────────────────┤
│ PLAY 再聽  SEL 不會  SEQ 提示   │
└────────────────────────────────┘
```

回合的組成沿用 Morse：新卡和到期的卡先出，弱卡在同一回合後段再出一次，剩下的位置補上最弱的未到期卡。另外加一條規則：同一個調不連續出現（交錯練習）。

**共同的按鍵**

| 按鍵 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| 琴鍵 | 作答 |
| `PLAY` | 開始、重播；問句時代表「是」 |
| `HOME` | 選單；問句時代表「否」 |
| `SEL` | 不會，跳過 |
| `SEQ` | 提示：LED 亮出答案，這張卡算錯 |
| `SELECT` | 答案不是音的時候，從清單選（和弦性質、級數） |
| `OCT-` / `OCT+` | 改變發聲的八度。在 GROOVE 裡改成沿五度圈移調 |

## 卡片 { #cards }

| 類別 | 題目 | 怎麼作答 |
|---|---|---|
| 樂理 | 調號（「E 大調？」） | 按出升降記號的鍵 |
| | 五度圈關係（「Eb 的關係小調？」） | 按 C |
| | 拼音階（「D 大調」） | 依序彈 7 個音，不分八度 |
| | 組和弦（「F#m7」「Bb 調的 V7」） | 同時按下，不分八度，不分轉位 |
| | 級數（「A 大調裡的 D？」） | 用 `SELECT` 選 IV |
| 聽音：相對 | 級數：cadence 之後放一個音 | 按出那個音（畫面告訴你調，所以按對的鍵就等於答對級數） |
| | 調內的音程：先給第一個音 | 彈出第二個音 |
| | 和弦性質 | 四選一，用 E4 F4 G4 A4 作答（同 Morse 的 `CHOICE_KEY`） |
| | 和弦進行：聽四個和弦 | 依序按白鍵，從主音起算是 I–vii |
| | bass | 彈出 bass 線 |
| 聽音：絕對（選用） | 沒有 cadence 的單音 | 按出那個音。每題換音色和音域，題與題之間放一段隨機音簇，蓋掉前一題的音高 |
| 節奏 | 聽 1–2 小節 | 從 4 個小譜面選一個 |
| | 盲聽 | 在任一鍵 tap 回來，依 onset 的時間誤差評分，沿用 Morse RHYTHM 的經驗 |
| | 看譜 | count-in 之後 tap 出來 |
| 旋律 | 聽 3–8 個音 | 彈回來 |
| | 看小五線譜 | 彈出來 |
| 鍵盤 | 音階、琶音：節拍器下彈一個八度，上行加下行 | 評分看音對不對、時間均勻度、速度 |
| | cadence 與轉位：彈 I–IV–V–I | 評分看每個和弦的音，以及各聲部移動了多少 |
| | 移調：同一個進行沿五度圈換調 | 同上 |

**自動評分對應四個等級**：答錯是 Again；答對但慢（反應時間或速度低於目標）是 Hard；答對是 Good；又快又穩是 Easy。v1 的 Leitner 排程裡，Again 回到 box 0，Hard 不動，Good 升一格，Easy 升兩格。

## 小譜面 { #notation }

```text
┌────────────────────────────────┐
│ RHYTHM   聽到的是哪一個？ 3/8    │
│  E4  |  ♩   ♩   ♫   ♩  |       │
│  F4  |  ♩   ♫   ♩   ♩  |       │
│  G4  |  ♩.  ♪   ♫   ♩  |       │
│  A4  |  ♩   ♩   ♩   𝄽  |       │
├────────────────────────────────┤
│ PLAY 再聽         SEL 不會      │
└────────────────────────────────┘
```

- 節奏用單線譜，旋律用小五線譜。
- 符頭、符桿、符尾、beam、休止符、附點、連結線是幾個小 bitmap 加上線段，依時值用程式排出來。
- 4 個節奏選項每個大約 40 px 高，放得進 176 px 高的主畫面。
- **節奏也用程式產生。** 依 Kodály 式的節奏單元（cell）分級：ta、ti-ti、休止、ta-a、tika-tika、附點、切分、三連音、連結線。新的 cell 照課綱的順序開放。
- 選項裡的錯誤答案只和正確答案差一個 cell，概念和 Morse 的 `ln_alike` 用相似的碼當選項一樣。
- 時值用每拍 12 tick 表示，可以表達三連音。

## 機器限制怎麼處理 { #hardware }

| 限制 | 做法 |
|---|---|
| 27 鍵，F3–G5（MIDI 53–79） | 判斷時不分八度。任何調的一個八度音階都放得下。左手用 F3–E4，右手用 F4–G5。`OCT±` 只改變發聲的八度 |
| 每鍵一顆單色 LED | 音階內的音 glow，主音 lit。DRILL 帶彈時下一個音閃爍，可以關掉，改成憑記憶彈。答錯後亮出正確答案 |
| 240×240 彩色 LCD，沒有畫圓的 primitive | 用 `fm_sinf` / `fm_cosf` 算出 12 個位置，再用 `cv_line` / `cv_pset` 畫，分段畫進 strip canvas |
| 字型只有 ASCII | ♯ ♭ ° ø 做成幾個小 bitmap。核心用 `TH_GLYPH_*` 巨集決定輸出的字元，預設是 ASCII 的 `#` `b` `o` `/o` |
| fm1-base 沒有 synth | 自己寫：8 voice 的 2-op FM 電鋼琴（從 `common/chime` 改）、一個 bass voice、節拍器的 click。音符在 `app_render` 裡依 sample 數排程，因為 `app_tick` 的旗標會有最多一個 block（5.8 ms）的抖動 |
| 沒有關機後還會走的時鐘 | 用回合計算，同 Morse。接電腦時可以由網頁送日期 |
| store object 最多 3,840 B | 進度每個項目約 3 B，1,000 個以內放得下一個 object |

## 內容表示：程式產生、TSV、Alda { #content }

**MIDI 還是 Alda？答案是大部分都用程式算出來**，分三層：

1. **裝置上用程式產生**：音階、和弦、調號、五度圈、羅馬數字、和弦辨識、就近轉位。表格加起來不到 2 KB，整個核心在 Mac 上編出來約 13 KB 的程式碼，涵蓋大約九成的內容。
2. **和弦進行目錄**：用羅馬數字寫成 TSV，build 時經 fm1-base 的 `gen = [...]` 轉成 C 表：

    ```text
    # id         name                 numerals              tags
    royal-road   Royal Road           IVM7 V7 iii7 vi       jpop cpop
    axis         Axis                 I V vi IV             pop
    4536251      4536251              4536251               cpop
    canon        Canon                1 5 6 3 4 1 4 5       pop classical
    andalusian   Andalusian cadence   i bVII bVI V          minor
    ```

    裝置的字型沒有中文，所以畫面上顯示英文的 id。「王道進行」這類中文名稱只放在文件和網頁上。

3. **旋律**（聽寫、樂句）：用 **Alda 子集**寫，例如 `o4 d8 e f+ g a4 b > c+2`，和弦寫成 `d/f+/a`。
    - 自己寫一個小 Python parser，build 時轉成每個事件 2 B 的 bytecode（音高 + 時值索引），同時輸出 `.mid` 方便在 Mac 上試聽。
    - [Alda](https://github.com/alda-lang/alda) 的官方工具是 EPL-2.0，只拿來選用對照（`alda parse` 的輸出），不放進韌體。
    - 子集涵蓋哪些語法（調號、連結線、三連音）等真的要寫旋律時再定。

**MIDI 只用在電腦端的匯入匯出**（[mido](https://github.com/mido/mido)，MIT）。裝置上不放 MIDI 檔，理由是：

- SMF 沒有級數和拼法的資訊，移調和顯示音名都要另外推斷。
- 還要多寫一個 parser。

**拼法用 line of fifths。** 每個音是 fifths 線上的一個位置（C=0、G=1、F=−1、F#=6、Gb=−6）。音階和和弦存成相對根音的 fifths 位移，所以：

- 移調就是加法。
- 每個音階級數一個字母，自然成立。
- D 大調寫 F#，Db 大調寫 Gb，C# 大調有 E# 和 B#，G# 和聲小調有 F##。

**其他的拼法規則**：

- 調外的音：在 C 大調裡用 Db、Eb、F#、Ab、Bb，也就是從主音往下 b2 到往上 #4 這個範圍。
- 辨認出來的和弦根音：選相對調號升降記號最少的拼法。所以 C 大調裡是 C#dim7 不是 Dbdim7，B 大調裡是 C# 不是 Db。
- **級數的升降記號一律以同主音的大調為準**，這是流行音樂和 Wikipedia 的寫法：A 小調的 G 是 `bVII`、C 是 `bIII`、G#dim 是 `viio`。古典教科書會把前兩個寫成 VII、III，這點列在「還沒決定的事」。

## 網頁：匯入教材、備份進度 { #web }

- 用 Web MIDI 頁面，和 Morse 的 `web/index.html` 一樣透過 `hostlink` SysEx 溝通。
- **備份與還原進度**：格式比照 Morse 的 `fm1-morse-progress` JSON。
- **匯入自己寫的進行或旋律**：
    1. 在瀏覽器裡解析 TSV / Alda 子集。
    2. 用 SysEx 送到 FM-1。
    3. FM-1 在螢幕上問一次，按 `PLAY` 確認。
    4. 存進 **store object**。
- **走 `APP_STORE_MAP`，不需要修改 AGENTS.md 的 flash 規則。** 一個 object 3,840 B，大約可以放 100 個進行或短旋律。真的需要更大的 deck，才走[背單字頁的資料區草案](vocab.md#delivery)。
- parser 會有兩份：Python 版給 build 用，JS 版給網頁用。兩份用共用的 test vectors 確保結果一致，Morse 的 protocol vectors 也是這樣做。

## 排程與存檔 { #srs }

- **項目是 (skill, key, variant)**，例如 (拼大調音階, D, 上行)，每個項目約 3 B：一個 box 加上最後一次出現的回合。
- v1 沿用 Morse 的 Leitner rounds（box 0–5，box n 每 2^n 回合出一次）。等背單字 app 把 FSRS 移植成 C 之後，可以考慮放進 `firmware/common` 兩邊共用。
- store sector 要避開 Morse 的 `0xDA000` 和面板校正的 `0xDC000`。實作時用 `just emu-rehearse` 確認，並更新 [flash 配置圖](../hardware/flash-map.md)。

## 樂理核心 { #core }

`firmware/theory/`，GPL-3.0-or-later。寫法比照 Morse 的 `learn.c`：C99，不呼叫平台、不用 libc、不用浮點，所以可以直接放進 fm1-base 的 unity build（fm1-base 不接受 `double`）。

| 功能 | 函式 |
|---|---|
| 音名 | `th_name`、`th_parse_name`、`th_spell_pc`（依調拼）、`th_note_name`（`C#4`）、`th_interval_name` |
| 音階與調 | 12 種音階（7 種調式、和聲與旋律小調、大小調五聲音階、藍調）、`th_keysig`、`th_key_acc`、五度圈位置、`th_key_for_pc` |
| 和弦 | 23 種性質（三和弦、sus、七和弦、6、add9、九和弦、power chord）、`th_chord`、`th_chord_name`（`F#m7b5`、`C/E`）、`th_diatonic` |
| 級數 | `th_roman_name`（`IVM7`、`viio`、`bVII`、`V7/V`）、`th_nashville_name`（`6m`、`b7`）、`th_roman_parse`、`th_prog_parse`（`4536251`、`i-bVII-bVI-V`） |
| 和弦辨識 | `th_identify`：MIDI 音符進去，出來根音、性質、轉位、有沒有省略五音、是不是調內的音。偏好的順序是：不需要省略五音 → 根音在 bass → 根音在調內 → 比較簡單的和弦。所以 C E G A 在 C 上是 C6，在 A 上是 Am7 |
| 就近轉位 | `th_voice_near`：在範圍內選出和前一個和弦相比移動最少的 close voicing |

**測試**：`just theory-unit`，共 26,661 個檢查。

- 手寫的答案：15 個大調和 15 個小調逐音比對、所有 7 音音階在所有調都是連續的 7 個字母、調號、五度圈、順級和弦的 Roman 名稱、和弦辨識的案例。
- 「名稱 → 解析」的往返：所有調的順級和弦，以及副屬和弦。
- 所有調所有順級和弦在每個轉位都辨認正確。例外是 m7 與 m7b5 的第一轉位，它們會辨認成 6 / m6，因為根音在 bass 優先。
- 隨機 2,000 組就近轉位都是最少移動。
- **和 music21（BSD-3）對照**：`just theory-vectors` 用 music21 10.5.2 產生 `tests/vectors.h`，內容是 162 個音階、30 個調號、483 個和弦、35 個音程、450 個 Roman numeral，目前全部一致。小調的 Roman numeral 沒有對照，因為 music21 的 VI、VII 以小調音階為準，和我們的寫法不同。

## 內容來源與 licence { #licence }

App 是 GPL-3.0-or-later，所以 CC BY-SA 的內容可以用（CC BY-SA 4.0 [可以單向相容到 GPLv3](https://creativecommons.org/2015/10/08/cc-by-sa-4-0-now-one-way-compatible-with-gplv3/)）。不過內容原則上還是自己寫：音階公式、和弦組成、常見進行都是事實，不受著作權保護。

| 來源 | Licence | 能不能用 |
|---|---|---|
| [Open Music Theory](https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/) | CC BY-SA 4.0 | 可以，要標示出處；主要當參考 |
| [Chenette《Foundations of Aural Skills》](https://uen.pressbooks.pub/auralskills/) | CC BY-SA（版本沒有確認） | 同上 |
| [musictheory.net](https://musictheory.net/legal) | 課文與靜態圖片是 CC BY 4.0；資料、程式、聲音是專有的 | 課文可以用，要標示出處 |
| Wikipedia | CC BY-SA 4.0 | 可以，要標示出處 |
| teoria.com | CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 | **不行** |
| Hooktheory TheoryTab | 專有，[服務條款](https://www.hooktheory.com/terms)禁止抓取和 data mining | **不行**；只引用它公開的統計結論 |
| music21 | BSD-3-Clause | 只當測試工具，不進韌體 |
| Alda | EPL-2.0 | 只當選用的對照工具 |
| Shed、Keyboard Academy | GPL-3.0 加 SDK exception | 只參考做法。它們建在 FM1 Open 上，程式碼本來就不能直接拿來用 |
````

````markdown
# firmware/theory

The start of a pocket music theory trainer for the M-VAVE FM-1: so far only its platform-free core. There is no
`app.c` or `fm1.toml` yet, so `just fw-test theory` does not apply. Design (Traditional Chinese):
[docs/dev/theory.md](../../docs/dev/theory.md).

Licence: GPL-3.0-or-later.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `theory.h`, `theory.c` | Spelling on the line of fifths, 12 scales, key signatures, the circle of fifths, 23 chord qualities, Roman numerals and Nashville numbers (naming and reading, secondary dominants), naming a chord from MIDI notes, the nearest close voicing. C99, no platform calls, no libc, no floating point. |
| `tests/theory_test.c` | Unit tests: hand-written answers, round trips, every diatonic chord in every key and inversion, random voicings. |
| `tests/vectors.h` | Generated from music21 by `host/theory/make_vectors.py`; do not edit. |

```sh
just theory-unit      # build and run the tests on this computer
just theory-vectors   # regenerate tests/vectors.h (uv fetches music21 10.5.2)
```

Conventions worth knowing before using it:

- A spelled note is an `int` f on the line of fifths: C = 0, G = 1, F = -1, F# = 6, Gb = -6. Pitch class is
  `7f mod 12`; `+7` adds a sharp; `+12` is the next enharmonic spelling.
- Roman numerals measure accidentals against the major scale on the same tonic, minor keys included: in A minor,
  G is `bVII` and G#dim is `viio`.
- Output is ASCII (`#`, `b`, `o`, `/o`). An app with glyphs for sharp, flat, diminished and half-diminished
  defines `TH_GLYPH_SHARP`, `TH_GLYPH_FLAT`, `TH_GLYPH_DIM` and `TH_GLYPH_HDIM` before including `theory.c`.
- Static helpers and tables are prefixed `th_` / `TH_` so the file can be `#include`d into fm1-base's unity build
  beside an app's own code.
````

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-18 09:57:29Z)**_

設計文件寫好了，樂理核心也開始寫了：`just theory-unit` 的 26,661 個檢查全部通過，`just docs-check` 也通過。還沒 commit。

**有人做過嗎？** FM-1 上已經有兩個教學韌體，都還沒上 Hub：
- **Shed**：jazz 聽力訓練，先放 cadence 再出題，一回合 20 題。沒有 release，2026-10-23 之後就沒更新。
- **FM1 Keyboard Academy**：初學者課程，用 LED 帶你彈。有 v0.1.2 的 `.fwsc`，不知道支不支援你這台的新 flash 晶片。

它們都沒有跨天的複習排程，Shed 也沒有定義音名怎麼拼。所以我們的定位是：用 spaced repetition 同時管樂理、聽力、節奏和手上技巧，加上五度圈與和弦辨識當隨身參考、流行與華語的和弦進行，以及 15 個調都拼對音名。Roadmap 第 0 步是先在 fm1-emu 試用 Keyboard Academy。

**譜面用 MIDI 還是 Alda：大部分用程式算出來。**
- 音階、和弦、調號、五度圈、級數，在裝置上用 line of fifths 算，所以 D 大調寫 F#，Db 大調寫 Gb，C# 大調有 E# 和 B#。
- 和弦進行用羅馬數字寫成 TSV，旋律用 Alda 子集，build 時轉成 C 表。
- MIDI 只在電腦端匯入匯出，不放進裝置。

**你插話問的小調歧義：可以在產生時就解決。** 我寫進了設計：
- **裝置上不存字串**，只存解析好的和弦（根音相對主音的位移加上和弦性質），所以裝置上不會再出現「VI 該讀成 F 還是 F#」的問題。
- **網頁編輯器即時顯示結果**，比照 Morse 的網頁：打 `i bVI bIII bVII` 時旁邊直接列出 `Am F C G`，可以試聽。
- **可疑的寫法會警告**：小調裡大寫的 III、VI、VII 沒加記號，而且解析出來的根音不在自然小調裡，編輯器會提示，build 也會失敗。
- **檔頭可以宣告 `# numerals: classical`**，從課本或 Wikipedia 抄來的寫法照原樣讀。

**樂理核心（`firmware/theory/`）**
- 你把 licence 改成 GPL-3.0，我用的是 `GPL-3.0-or-later`，和 Morse 一樣。
- C99，不用 libc 也不用浮點，可以直接放進 fm1-base；在 Mac 上編出來約 13 KB。
- 內容：12 種音階、23 種和弦、調號、五度圈、Roman / Nashville 的命名與解析（含 `V7/V`、`bVII`、`4536251`）、從彈的音辨認和弦，以及挑移動最少的轉位。
- 用 music21 產生對照答案：162 個音階、30 個調號、483 個和弦、35 個音程、450 個 Roman numeral，結果完全一致。
- 有一個刻意的取捨：同一組音由最低音決定和弦，所以 Am7 的第一轉位會辨認成 C6。

**聽音與節奏**
- 相對音感是主線。
- 絕對音感做成選用的路線。研究（Wong et al. 2020）指出成人訓練 12–40 小時後，43 人中有 6 人（14%）達到絕對音感的水準。
- 節奏題有三種：聽了從 4 個小譜面選一個、盲聽後 tap 回來、看譜 tap。節奏也用程式產生。
- Yamaha 用固定唱名這點我查不到，文件裡寫成你的個人經驗。

這一輪改到的頁面：
- 新增 `docs/dev/theory.md`，已加進 nav
- `docs/firmware/index.md` 新增「學習類」小節
- `docs/dev/vocab.md` 加了互相連結
- `docs/dev/index.md`
- `AGENTS.md`、`Justfile` 新增 `theory-unit`、`theory-vectors`

Sources:
- [Wong et al. 2020, Is it impossible to acquire absolute pitch in adulthood?](https://scholars.ln.edu.hk/en/publications/is-it-impossible-to-acquire-absolute-pitch-in-adulthood/)
- [Yamaha 幼兒科介紹（第三方）](https://eleschool-compass.com/naraigoto/brand/yamaha-music.html)
- [Kodály method](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kod%C3%A1ly_method)
- [fm1-shed](https://github.com/Luisnvb/fm1-shed)
- [FM1 Keyboard Academy](https://github.com/chmess/fm1-keyboard-academy)
- [Firmware Hub catalog](https://thefirmwarehub.com/catalog.json)

```text
The search didn't return the 1984 Salmoni, Schmidt & Walter paper itself, so these findings come from secondary sources that describe it.

- **The hypothesis:** Augmented information can have negative effects on motor skill learning if it is provided too frequently or in a form that is too easy to use. Most tests of it have used knowledge of results (KR) (1-4).
- **Dependency mechanism:** The proposed explanation is that frequent and useful KR can encourage learners to ignore important sources of sensory feedback (e.g., kinesthetic) intrinsic to the task. That leads to the inability to establish an internally generated error-detection mechanism, which would otherwise support performance without KR.
- **Retention testing:** Studies use no-KR retention tests. Any decrements in performance on the no-KR tests are assumed to reflect the negative consequences of guidance during acquisition.
- **Later challenges:** Frequency findings are mixed. Several studies have demonstrated learning advantages of practice conditions with a reduced feedback frequency, compared to 100% feedback. A 2010 study by Wulf and colleagues found that learning of the movement form was enhanced by external-focus feedback after every trial (100%) relative to external-focus feedback after every third trial (33%) or internal-focus feedback. The critique is that the guidance view overemphasizes the informational properties of KR at the expense of its motivational influences.
```

```text
42	}
43	
44	static volatile uint32_t midi_last, midi_last_port, midi_count;   /* the last message in (shown), and how many */
45	static void midi_in(void)                    /* audio interrupt: the packets that came in */
46	{
47	    uint32_t pkt;
48	    int port;
49	    while (plat_midi_in(&pkt, &port)) {
50	        uint32_t st = (pkt >> 8) & 0xFFu, d1 = (pkt >> 16) & 0x7Fu, d2 = pkt >> 24;
51	        if (st != 0xF8u && st != 0xFEu) {    /* (clock and active sensing would flood the screen) */
52	            midi_last = pkt;
53	            midi_last_port = (uint32_t)port;
54	            midi_count++;
55	        }
56	        if ((st & 0xF0u) == 0x90u && d2)
57	            note_on((int32_t)d1, d2);
58	        else if ((st & 0xF0u) == 0x80u || (st & 0xF0u) == 0x90u)
59	            note_off((int32_t)d1);
60	    }
61	}
62	
63	void app_render(int32_t *lr, uint32_t n, uint32_t master_q12)
64	{
65	    uint32_t i;
66	    int32_t note = voice_note;
67	    float target = note >= 0 ? 0.25f * voice_vel : 0.0f;
68	    float inc = note >= 0 ? 440.0f * fm_exp2f((float)(note - 69) / 12.0f) / 44100.0f : 0.0f;
69	    float gain = (float)master_q12 / 4096.0f * 8300000.0f;   /* MASTER, read once a block */
70	    midi_in();
71	    for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
72	        float s;
73	        voice_level += (target - voice_level) * 0.002f;          /* ~10 ms attack and release */
74	        gain_now += (gain - gain_now) * 0.004f;                  /* ~5 ms: turning MASTER does not click */
75	        voice_phase += inc;
76	        if (voice_phase >= 1.0f)
77	            voice_phase -= 1.0f;
78	        s = set.wave ? 4.0f * fm_fabsf(voice_phase - 0.5f) - 1.0f : fm_sinf(voice_phase * 6.2831853f);
79	        s *= voice_level * gain_now;
80	        lr[2 * i] = (int32_t)s;
81	        lr[2 * i + 1] = (int32_t)s;
82	    }
83	}

88	    voice_level = 0.0f;
89	}

121	static void text_cat(char *d, const char *s)
122	{
123	    while (*d)
124	        d++;
125	    while (*s)
126	        *d++ = *s++;
127	    *d = 0;
128	}
129	
130	static void int_text(int32_t v, char *b)     /* signed, no padding */
131	{
132	    char t[12];
133	    int n = 0;
134	    uint32_t u = (uint32_t)(v < 0 ? -v : v);
135	    do
136	        t[n++] = (char)('0' + u % 10u);
137	    while ((u /= 10u) && n < 11);
138	    if (v < 0)
139	        *b++ = '-';
140	    while (n)
141	        *b++ = t[--n];
142	    *b = 0;
143	}

145	void app_say(const char *a, const char *b)
146	{
147	    uint32_t i;
148	    char t[48];
149	    for (i = 0; i < 23u && a && a[i]; i++)
150	        ui.msg[0][i] = a[i];
151	    ui.msg[0][i] = 0;
152	    for (i = 0; i < 23u && b && b[i]; i++)
153	        ui.msg[1][i] = b[i];
154	    ui.msg[1][i] = 0;
155	    ui.msg_until = plat_ms() + 1300u;
156	    ui.redraw = 1;
157	    if (ann_on()) {                          /* and to a screen reader (announce.c, fm1-reader) */
158	        t[0] = 0;
159	        text_cat(t, ui.msg[0]);
160	        if (ui.msg[1][0]) {
161	            text_cat(t, " ");
162	            text_cat(t, ui.msg[1]);
163	        }
164	        ann_say(t, 0, ANN_NOW);
165	    }
166	}

168	static void octave_text(char *t)
169	{
170	    t[0] = set.octave < 0 ? '-' : '+';
171	    t[1] = (char)('0' + (set.octave < 0 ? -set.octave : set.octave));
172	    t[2] = 0;
173	}
174	
175	/* a screen reader that has just started listening (or asks) hears the whole screen */
176	static void speak(void)
177	{
178	    char t[96], o[4];
179	    if (ann_on() && ann_where()) {
180	        octave_text(o);
181	        t[0] = 0;
182	        text_cat(t, APP_NAME ". OCTAVE ");
183	        text_cat(t, o);
184	        text_cat(t, ". WAVE ");
185	        text_cat(t, WAVE_NAME[set.wave]);
186	        if (midi_count) {                    /* the last MIDI message in, as the screen shows it */
187	            static const char *const PORT[NPORTS] = {"USB", "BLE", "TRS"};
188	            static const char HEX[] = "0123456789ABCDEF";
189	            uint32_t m = midi_last, b;
190	            char h[10];
191	            for (b = 0; b < 3u; b++) {
192	                uint32_t v = (m >> (8u + 8u * b)) & 0xFFu;
193	                h[3 * b] = HEX[v >> 4];
194	                h[3 * b + 1] = HEX[v & 15u];
195	                h[3 * b + 2] = b < 2u ? ' ' : 0;
196	            }
197	            text_cat(t, ". MIDI IN ");
198	            text_cat(t, midi_last_port < NPORTS ? PORT[midi_last_port] : "");
199	            text_cat(t, " ");
200	            text_cat(t, h);
201	        }
202	        ann_say(t, 0, ANN_NOW);
203	    }
204	    ann_tick(plat_ms());
205	}

207	static void note_name(int32_t note, char *b)
208	{
209	    static const char *const N[] = {"C", "C#", "D", "D#", "E", "F", "F#", "G", "G#", "A", "A#", "B"};
210	    char o[12];
211	    b[0] = 0;
212	    text_cat(b, N[note % 12]);
213	    int_text(note / 12 - 1, o);
214	    text_cat(b, o);
215	}

217	static void octave_step(int32_t d)
218	{
219	    int32_t o = clamp(set.octave + d, -2, 2);
220	    char t[4];
221	    if (o == set.octave)
222	        return;
223	    voice_note = -1;                         /* a key held across the change would not find its note off */
224	    set.octave = (int8_t)o;
225	    set_dirty = 1;
226	    octave_text(t);
227	    app_say("OCTAVE", t);
228	}

234	{

241	/* REC: a Bluetooth MIDI device (FM1B_BLE_CENTRAL, lib/btdev): look for devices, then connect to the one ALGORITHM
242	 * picks, then let it go */
243	static void ble_device_say(void)
244	{
245	    char name[21];
246	    if (btdev_found(btdev_pick(), name, 0))
247	        app_say("DEVICE", name);
248	    else
249	        app_say("BLE", "SCANNING");

251	static void ble_device_button(void)
252	{
253	    int ev;
254	    if (!btdev_busy() && !ui.looking) {
255	        ui.looking = 1;
256	        app_say("BLE", "SCANNING");
257	        return;
258	    }
259	    ev = btdev_save();
260	    ui.looking = 0;
261	    app_say(ev == BTDEV_CONNECTING ? btdev_word(ev) : "BLE", ev == BTDEV_CONNECTING ? btdev_name() : btdev_word(ev));
262	}
263	
264	static void input(void)
265	{
266	    uint32_t keys, btn = plat_buttons(), k;
267	    int32_t e;
268	    touch_poll();                            /* the sensed keys' presses, velocities and pressure */
269	    keys = touch_keys();
270	    for (k = 0; k < NKEYS; k++) {            /* key 0 is F3 (MIDI 53) */
271	        uint32_t bit = 1u << k, v;
272	        int32_t note = 53 + (int32_t)k + 12 * set.octave;
273	        if ((keys & bit) && !(ui.keys & bit)) {
274	            v = touch_vel(k);
275	            ui.vel[k] = (uint8_t)v;
276	            ui.prs[k] = 0;
277	            ui.last_key = (int32_t)k;
278	            note_on(note, v);
279	            plat_midi_send(0x09u | 0x90u << 8 | (uint32_t)note << 16 | v << 24, TO_USB | TO_BLE);   /* BLE: if built with it */
280	        } else if (!(keys & bit) && (ui.keys & bit)) {
281	            ui.prs[k] = 0;
282	            note_off(note);
283	            plat_midi_send(0x08u | 0x80u << 8 | (uint32_t)note << 16, TO_USB | TO_BLE);
284	        } else if ((keys & bit) && touch_pressure(k) != ui.prs[k]) {   /* pressure: poly aftertouch */
285	            ui.prs[k] = touch_pressure(k);
286	            ui.redraw = 1;
287	            plat_midi_send(0x0Au | 0xA0u << 8 | (uint32_t)note << 16 | (uint32_t)ui.prs[k] << 24, TO_USB | TO_BLE);
288	        }
289	    }
290	    for (k = 0; k < NB; k++) {               /* a button pressed: its name, and what it does here */
291	        uint32_t bit = 1u << k;
292	        if (!(btn & bit) || (ui.btn & bit))
293	            continue;
294	        if (k == B_OCTDN)
295	            octave_step(-1);
296	        else if (k == B_OCTUP)
297	            octave_step(1);
298	        else if (k == B_REC && FM1B_BLE)
299	            ui.rec_t = plat_ms();                /* a press: on release (a hold switches Bluetooth) */
300	        else if (k == B_SAVE) {
301	            if (plat_store_save(OBJ_SETTINGS, &set, sizeof set) == 0) {
302	                set_dirty = 0;
303	                app_say("SAVED", "");
304	            } else {
305	                app_say("SAVE", "FAILED");
306	            }
307	        } else {
308	            app_say("BUTTON", BTN_NAME[k]);
309	        }
310	    }
311	    if (FM1B_BLE && ui.rec_t) {             /* REC: held a second, Bluetooth on / off; a press, a device */
312	        if (btn >> B_REC & 1u) {
313	            if (plat_ms() - ui.rec_t >= 1000u) {
314	                ui.rec_t = 0;
315	                ble_toggle();
316	            }
317	        } else {
318	            ui.rec_t = 0;
319	            if (FM1B_BLE_CENTRAL && !set.ble_off)
320	                ble_device_button();
321	            else
322	                app_say("BUTTON", "REC");
323	        }
324	    }
325	    for (k = 0; k < NE; k++) {               /* an encoder turned: its count; PRESET also changes the wave */
326	        char t[12];
327	        if ((e = plat_enc((int)k)) == 0)
328	            continue;
329	        ui.turns[k] += e;
330	        ui.turned_at[k] = plat_ms();
331	        ui.redraw = 1;
332	        if (k == EN_ALGO && FM1B_BLE_CENTRAL && ui.looking) {
333	            btdev_choose(btdev_pick() + e);
334	            ble_device_say();
335	        } else if (k == EN_PRESET) {
336	            set.wave ^= 1u;
337	            set_dirty = 1;
338	            app_say("WAVE", WAVE_NAME[set.wave]);
339	        } else {
340	            int_text(ui.turns[k], t);
341	            app_say(ENC_NAME[k], t);
342	        }
343	    }
344	    if (keys != ui.keys || btn != ui.btn)
345	        ui.redraw = 1;
346	    ui.keys = keys;
347	    ui.btn = btn;
348	    plat_glow(1);                            /* the unlit buttons glow, readable in the dark */
349	    plat_leds(btn | (set_dirty ? 1u << B_SAVE : 0u), keys);
350	}

354	static void cell(int32_t x, int32_t y, int32_t w, const char *s, int on)   /* a labelled box, lit when on */
355	{
356	    cv_rect(x, y, w, 18, on ? C_HI : C_LINE);
357	    cv_text(x + (w - text_w(&FONT_XS, s)) / 2, y + 2, &FONT_XS, s, on ? C_BLACK : C_GRAY);
358	}
359	
360	static void key_cell(int32_t x, int32_t y, int32_t w, int32_t h, uint32_t k, uint16_t off)
361	{
362	    int32_t v, p;
363	    cv_rect(x, y, w, h, off);
364	    if (!(ui.keys >> k & 1u))
365	        return;
366	    v = (ui.vel[k] * h + 126) / 127;
367	    p = (ui.prs[k] * h + 126) / 127;
368	    cv_rect(x, y + h - v, w, v, C_HI);
369	    if (p)
370	        cv_rect(x + 2, y + h - p, w - 4, p, C_WHITE);
371	}
372	
373	static void draw(void)
374	{
375	    char t[24];
376	    int32_t note = voice_note;
377	    uint32_t i, now = plat_ms(), pct = plat_master() * 100u / 4096u;
378	    static const uint8_t WK[16] = PLAT_WHITE_KEYS, BK[11] = PLAT_BLACK_KEYS;
379	    /* the header: the name and the note, or a message for a moment */
380	    cv_begin(240, 32, C_BLACK);
381	    if (now < ui.msg_until) {
382	        int32_t x = cv_text(10, 6, &FONT_B, ui.msg[0], C_WHITE);
383	        cv_text(x + 8, 6, &FONT_B, ui.msg[1], C_HI);
384	    } else {
385	        int32_t x = cv_text(10, 6, &FONT_B, APP_NAME, C_WHITE);
386	        if (FM1B_BLE)                        /* Bluetooth: grey while it waits, lit while a computer is connected */
387	            x = cv_text(x + 8, 10, &FONT_XS, "BLE", plat_ble_connected() ? C_HI : C_DIM);
388	        if (FM1B_BLE_CENTRAL)                /* a Bluetooth MIDI device: lit while connected */
389	            cv_text(x + 6, 10, &FONT_XS, "DEV", plat_ble_device() == BLE_DEV_READY ? C_HI : C_DIM);
390	        if (note >= 0) {                     /* the note, and the last key's velocity and pressure */
391	            int32_t x;
392	            note_name(note, t);
393	            x = 230 - text_w(&FONT_B, t);
394	            cv_text(x, 6, &FONT_B, t, C_HI);
395	            if (ui.keys >> ui.last_key & 1u) {
396	                char n[24] = "V ";
397	                int_text(ui.vel[ui.last_key], t);
398	                text_cat(n, t);
399	                text_cat(n, "  P ");
400	                int_text(ui.prs[ui.last_key], t);
401	                text_cat(n, t);
402	                cv_text(x - 12 - text_w(&FONT_XS, n), 10, &FONT_XS, n, C_GRAY);
403	            }
404	        }
405	    }
406	    cv_blit(0, 0);
407	    /* the buttons, 4 to a row, lit while held; the encoders and their counts, lit for a moment after a turn */
408	    cv_begin(240, 144, C_BLACK);
409	    for (i = 0; i < NB; i++)
410	        cell(4 + (int32_t)(i % 4u) * 58, (int32_t)(i / 4u) * 21, 56, BTN_NAME[i], (ui.btn >> i) & 1u);
411	    for (i = 0; i < NE; i++) {
412	        int32_t x = 4 + (int32_t)(i % 4u) * 58, y = 88 + (int32_t)(i / 4u) * 28;
413	        int lit = ui.turned_at[i] && now - ui.turned_at[i] < 300u;
414	        cv_text(x, y, &FONT_XS, ENC_NAME[i], lit ? C_HI : C_GRAY);
415	        int_text(ui.turns[i], t);
416	        cv_text(x, y + 13, &FONT_XS, t, lit ? C_WHITE : C_DIM);
417	    }
418	    cv_blit(0, 36);
419	    /* the keys, black above white: a held key fills to its velocity (amber), its pressure over that (white) */
420	    cv_begin(240, 60, C_BLACK);
421	    for (i = 0; i < 16u; i++)
422	        key_cell(4 + (int32_t)i * 14, 14, 13, 14, WK[i], C_DIM);
423	    for (i = 0; i < 11u; i++) {
424	        static const uint8_t AT[11] = {0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, 14};   /* the white key each one follows */
425	        key_cell(4 + (int32_t)AT[i] * 14 + 8, 0, 11, 12, BK[i], C_LINE);
426	    }
427	    octave_text(t);
428	    cv_text(4, 36, &FONT_XS, "OCT", C_GRAY);
429	    cv_text(30, 36, &FONT_XS, t, C_HI);
430	    cv_text(64, 36, &FONT_XS, "PRESET", C_GRAY);
431	    cv_text(112, 36, &FONT_XS, WAVE_NAME[set.wave], C_HI);
432	    if (midi_count) {                        /* the last MIDI message in, and where from */
433	        static const char *const PORT[NPORTS] = {"USB", "BLE", "TRS"};
434	        static const char HEX[] = "0123456789ABCDEF";
435	        uint32_t m = midi_last, b;
436	        char h[12];
437	        for (b = 0; b < 3u; b++) {
438	            uint32_t v = (m >> (8u + 8u * b)) & 0xFFu;
439	            h[3 * b] = HEX[v >> 4];
440	            h[3 * b + 1] = HEX[v & 15u];
441	            h[3 * b + 2] = b < 2u ? ' ' : 0;
442	        }
443	        cv_text(4, 48, &FONT_XS, "MIDI IN", C_GRAY);
444	        cv_text(52, 48, &FONT_XS, midi_last_port < NPORTS ? PORT[midi_last_port] : "", C_HI);
445	        cv_text(82, 48, &FONT_XS, h, C_WHITE);
446	    }
447	    cv_text(178, 36, &FONT_XS, "VOL", C_GRAY);
448	    int_text((int32_t)pct, t);
449	    text_cat(t, "%");
450	    cv_text(204, 36, &FONT_XS, t, C_HI);
451	    cv_blit(0, 180);
452	}
453	
454	void app_ui_init(void)
455	{
456	    touch_on(1);                             /* velocity and pressure: the keys' readings on */
457	    lcd_fill(0, 0, 240, 240, C_BLACK);
458	    ui.redraw = 1;
459	}

461	void app_frame(void)
462	{
463	    static uint32_t last_pct, lit_until, last_ble, last_midi;
464	    uint32_t i, now = plat_ms(), pct = plat_master() * 100u / 4096u;
465	    input();
466	    speak();
467	    for (i = 0; i < NE; i++)                 /* an encoder's light goes out */
468	        if (ui.turned_at[i] && now - ui.turned_at[i] < 400u && now > lit_until)
469	            lit_until = ui.turned_at[i] + 300u;
470	    if (lit_until && now >= lit_until) {
471	        lit_until = 0;
472	        ui.redraw = 1;
473	    }
474	    if (FM1B_BLE_CENTRAL) {                  /* looking: a device found is named at once (REC connects to it) */
475	        static int found;
476	        int n = ui.looking ? btdev_count() : 0, ev;
477	        btdev_page(ui.looking && !set.ble_off);
478	        if (n > found && btdev_pick() < n)
479	            ble_device_say();
480	        found = n;
481	        while ((ev = btdev_event()) != BTDEV_NONE)   /* a device connected, given up or lost */
482	            if (ev == BTDEV_CONNECTED || ev == BTDEV_NO_ANSWER || ev == BTDEV_LOST)
483	                app_say("DEVICE", btdev_word(ev));
484	    }
485	    if (midi_count != last_midi) {
486	        last_midi = midi_count;
487	        ui.redraw = 1;
488	    }
489	    if (pct != last_pct || (uint32_t)(plat_ble_connected() | plat_ble_device() << 1) != last_ble ||
490	        (ui.msg_until && now >= ui.msg_until)) {
491	        last_pct = pct;
492	        last_ble = (uint32_t)(plat_ble_connected() | plat_ble_device() << 1);
493	        if (now >= ui.msg_until)
494	            ui.msg_until = 0;
495	        ui.redraw = 1;
496	    }
497	    if (ui.redraw) {
498	        ui.redraw = 0;
499	        draw();
500	    }
501	}

504	int app_expect(const char *what, int *got)
505	{
506	    if (!strcmp(what, "octave"))
507	        *got = set.octave;
508	    else if (!strcmp(what, "wave"))
509	        *got = set.wave;
510	    else if (!strcmp(what, "note"))
511	        *got = voice_note;
512	    else if (!strcmp(what, "dirty"))
513	        *got = set_dirty;
514	    else if (!strcmp(what, "vel"))           /* the last key's velocity and pressure */
515	        *got = ui.vel[ui.last_key];
516	    else if (!strcmp(what, "prs"))
517	        *got = ui.prs[ui.last_key];
518	    else if (!strncmp(what, "turns", 5))    /* turnsN: encoder N's count (plat.h EN_*) */
519	        *got = ui.turns[atoi(what + 5) % NE];
520	    else
521	        return 0;
522	    return 1;
523	}
524	#endif
```

```text
3	/* fm1-base's platform interface (from X0X's, by way of FoMni-1): everything the app needs from the hardware.
4	 *
5	 * The device implementation (plat_fm1.c) wraps Felucca's HAL and panel map; the
6	 * host implementation (host/plat_host.c) is a simulator fed by a script, which is
7	 * what lets the whole app — UI, sequencer, engines — run and be tested on a Mac.
8	 * Drawing goes through Felucca's lcd_fill / lcd_blit (lcd.c on the device, a
9	 * framebuffer on the host) and gfx.c on top. */
10	#pragma once
11	#include <stdint.h>

13	/* big zero-initialised buffers go in the .pool RAM region on the device */
14	#ifdef PLAT_HOST
15	#define PLAT_POOL
16	#else
17	#define PLAT_POOL __attribute__((section(".pool")))
18	#endif

20	/* PLAT_RAM_CODE: a function that runs from RAM (section .app_ram, copied at boot with .ram_text, at the start of
21	 * the RAMTEXT region they share: 32 KiB, 24 KiB with WiFi; with fm1.toml ram_layout = "packed", device/app_packed.ld,
22	 * at the start of the packed SRAM, as big as its one budget lets it), out of the way
23	 * of the XIP cache's misses: an audio path. It may call
24	 * only RAM code (other PLAT_RAM_CODE functions, felucca-bsp's RAM functions) and nothing through a pointer; the build
25	 * checks it over the disassembly, to any depth (tools/ramcode.py; fm1.toml ram_code_allow names the exceptions an app
26	 * vouches for). Not for code that runs with the flash off: it may read constants in the flash. XIP code it may not
27	 * call: the compiler's own calls (memcpy for a struct copy, a 64-bit divide), and a static inline helper the compiler
28	 * keeps out of line (at -Os it often does: fastmath.h's fm_exp2f), whose one copy is in XIP; a helper RAM code uses
29	 * is always_inline, or PLAT_RAM_CODE itself.
30	 * PLAT_FAR(fn): fn through a pointer the compiler cannot turn back into a direct call. RAM code and XIP code are
31	 * mostly farther apart than a direct call reaches (+-4 MiB), so XIP code calls RAM code this way (the linker refuses
32	 * a direct call that does not reach: "relocation truncated to fit"); a call from RAM code into XIP this way is one
33	 * the check refuses, unless allowed. The host: plain calls. */
34	#ifdef PLAT_HOST
35	#define PLAT_RAM_CODE
36	#define PLAT_FAR(fn) (&(fn))
37	#else
38	#define PLAT_RAM_CODE __attribute__((section(".app_ram")))
39	static inline __attribute__((always_inline)) void *plat_far_ptr(void *fn)
40	{
41	    void *volatile held = fn;           /* read back from memory: the compiler no longer knows the target */
42	    return held;
43	}
44	#define PLAT_FAR(fn) ((__typeof__(&(fn)))plat_far_ptr((void *)&(fn)))

128	 * USB session ended (a device lost, the mode changed): release what its notes hold. Without FM1B_USB_HOST all stay
129	 * USBH_OFF / 0. */
```
